If you want to give your laptop a new and unique case, one way to do it is by fusing plastic bags together into a durable and waterproof case. This eco-friendly project is a fun way to upcycle plastic bags, and you can customize the design with your choice of colors and patterns. Follow these steps to make your own laptop case out of fused plastic bags.

Part 1: Fusing the Plastic Bags

1. Cut off the handles and save them. You'll use them later to stuff the case.

2. Cut off the bottom of the bag. Cut it as straight as you can.

3. Turn the bag inside out if there's a logo on it. This will make sure the label doesn't show up on your finished product.

4. Fold the bag twice so you have eight layers. This will make it thicker and more durable.

5. Get ready to start fusing. Heat up your iron (no steam) to the lowest setting.

6. Sandwich the plastic bag between two pieces of wax paper. Make sure the wax paper is larger than the plastic bag.

7. Iron over the "sandwich". Press down firmly and move the iron around for about 20 seconds.

8. Peel the wax paper away from the plastic bag. Be careful, as hot wax paper can burn. Your fused plastic should be smooth and no longer have any gaps or wrinkles.

9. Fuse about 10 plastic bags. Keep fusing until you have enough plastic to make your case.

10. True up all the fused plastic bags by trimming the sides. Cut off any jagged edges or excess plastic.

Part 2: Sewing the Case Together

1. Arrange the 10 fused plastic bags in a rectangle that's large enough to fit your laptop twice, plus a little extra for a flap.

2. Sew the pieces together by overlapping them slightly and using a zigzag stitch. Make sure the seams are strong and secure.

3. Cut out a piece of lining fabric (in this case, an old sweatshirt) that's the same size as the fused plastic bag piece. This will help protect your laptop from scratches.

4. Stack the pieces together, right sides facing in. Pin them together with bobby pins.

5. Remove the bobby pins from one short side. Turn it inside out.

6. Sew a seam about one inch in from the sewn edges. This will create a border around the fused plastic bags.

7. Sew a seam about two inches in from the bottom edge (the sewed short edge). This will create a pocket for the handles and additional stuffing.

8. Stuff the inside with the handles and wax paper you set aside, and/or additional plastic bags. This will give the case extra padding.

9. Fold and sew the open edge closed. Make sure the opening is neatly sewn shut.

10. Place the case right sides together, leaving room for the flap. Pin the edges together.

11. Fold in and sew the edges of the flap. This will give it a clean finish.

12. Add Velcro to close the flap. Make sure it's positioned correctly and securely attached.

13. Put in the laptop and you're done! You now have a creative and eco-friendly laptop case that's unique and stylish.

If you're interested in communicating with spirits or entities beyond the physical realm, creating your own Ouija board is a great way to do it. Follow these steps to create your own Ouija board:

Materials:
- Large piece of paper
- Letters of the alphabet
- Numbers 0-9
- Words "Yes", "No", "Hello", and "Goodbye"
- Glue
- Smooth surface for the pointer
- Soldering iron
- Varnish
- Embellishments

Instructions:
1. Begin by covering your large piece of paper with the letters of the alphabet, the numbers 0-9, and the words "Yes", "No", "Hello", and "Goodbye". You can print these out or handwrite them, as long as they are clear and easy to read.
2. Lay the letters in a circle, putting a sun in the top left hand corner and next to that the word "Yes".
3. Sit around the table with a couple of friends, who will be your partners in using the board.
4. Start by writing out all of the letters in one or two rows, making sure that the characters are large enough to read. In the row below that, write the numbers 0-9.
5. Write out the symbols for "Yes", "No", and "Goodbye", which will make communicating with the spirits easier. Cut out the characters, numbers, words, and phrases.
6. Adhere them with glue to the paper according to your desired layout.
7. To make the pointer slide, you can make it a smooth surface. You can use a small glass planchette or a circular piece of cardboard with a small window cut out in the center.
8. Get your board prepped by clearing the surface of any debris or dirt.
9. Draw out your design on the board with a pencil or pen.
10. Use a soldering iron to go over your designs, burning them into the surface of the board.
11. Let the board cool and clean the surface to remove any debris left behind. Smooth down any rough edges with fine-grit sandpaper.
12. Apply a layer of varnish to the surface to protect the board and give it a glossy finish.
13. Add further details like embellishments or paint.
14. Choose your layout, font, embellishments and colors for the planchette.

Lastly, it's important to note that using a Ouija board can be a serious endeavor and should be approached with caution and respect. Always begin by grounding yourself, setting your intention, and creating a safe environment in which to use the board. And remember to always say goodbye at the end of each session to close the board and prevent any negative energies from lingering. Enjoy your new Ouija board and have fun communicating with the other side!

Assuming there is any sort of art or knack to conversing and relating to British people is setting yourself up for a fall. In reality, British people are diverse and come in all shapes and sizes, each with their own unique personality. However, there are a few things you can do to make it easier to converse and relate with them.

1. Learn a little bit about football.
Football - or soccer, if you prefer - is practically a religion in the UK. It is a topic that is widely discussed and is almost bound to come up in conversation. So, make an effort to learn a little bit about the teams and the players. You don't need to be a die-hard fan, but knowing a few names will help you join in on the conversation.

2. Words like "candy" and "Jello" aren't frequently used in Britain, so learn their equivalents ("sweets" and "jelly").
British English and American English can differ significantly, with many different words having different meanings. So, it is worth taking the time to learn a few new words you may not be familiar with. For example, sweets are candy, biscuits are cookies, and chips are fries.

3. Don't talk about tea, scones, etc.
While it may seem like a staple of everyday British life, not everyone in the UK is obsessed with tea and scones. It's fine to enjoy them, of course, but don't assume that all British people love them too. Plus, it can get tedious when that's the only topic you want to discuss.

4. Cook foreign dishes to impress.
If you're at a dinner party and cooking is on the menu, it can be helpful if you can cook a foreign dish as well as British ones. British people love exotic and complex foods, as shown on the popular Channel 4 show "Come Dine With Me." So, try to create something out of your comfort zone to truly impress.

5. Learn a bit about British monarchs.
The British pride themselves on their rich history, which includes the monarchy. So, it helps to know a bit about the British monarchs, from Queen Elizabeth I to the current reigning monarch, Queen Elizabeth II.

6. Complain about the weather.
It's a well-known national pastime for British people to complain about the weather, as all weather is too hot or too cold. So, feel free to jump into the weather conversation and you will likely get a lot of nods in agreement.

7. British people aren't still living in the 19th century.
Despite what some people might think, the UK has moved on from the 19th century. However, some areas may still retain their historic feel, with buildings from centuries ago still standing. So, try not to assume all British people live in a time warp.

8. Don't forget, some British people love Americans.
There's no need to apologise for being American when meeting and talking with British people. Some may even love American culture, so if you have enough American culture about you, show it off!

9. Be aware of the differences in education.
While British children have Preschool, Primary, Junior, Secondary and Sixth Form, Americans have Preschool, Elementary, Middle, and High School. Try not to assume the schooling system is the same as what you are used to.

10. Be yourself—whatever your culture.
Remember that being yourself is key, even when trying to relate to British people. While these tips may help you join in with conversations and relate to others, it is important to remain true to yourself and your cultural background.

In summary, learning how to converse and relate to British people can be a fascinating journey. Remember to be yourself, learn a little bit about football and British culture, try new things, and join in on the conversation. With these tips, you'll be chatting with British people in no time!

How to Investigate the Bible Authorized by the U.S. Congress and President

The Aitken's Bible, also known as "The Bible of the Revolution," was the first entire Holy Bible printed in America. It was printed by Robert Aitken in 1782, and authorized and recommended by the U.S. Congress and President. If you are interested in investigating this historic Bible, here are some steps to get started.

1. Note the Bible's nickname, "The Bible of the Revolution."

The Aitken's Bible was printed during the Revolutionary War, when it was not practical to import the English language Bible from England. This Bible was considered an important symbol of American independence and was nicknamed "The Bible of the Revolution."

2. Examine the fact that the Congress authorized a loan of money to help the printing and distribution of this approved Bible to be made available to the public.

In 1781, Robert Aitken petitioned the U.S. Continental Congress for a loan to print an American edition of the holy scriptures in English. In 1782, Congress authorized a loan of money to help with the printing and distribution of this approved Bible.

3. See that it is called the "Aitken's Bible Endorsed by Congress" by the Library of Congress.

The Library of Congress refers to the Aitken's Bible as "Aitken's Bible Endorsed by Congress" and has a digital image of the actual title page of this edition of the Bible.

4. Read the Library of Congress blurb about the Bible.

The Library of Congress website has a blurb about the Aitken's Bible, stating that "Aitken published Congress's recommendation of September 1782 and related documents (Item 115) as an imprimatur on the two pages following his title page."

5. Read the report of the committee to whom the petition was referred.

The Journal of the U.S. Continental Congress under the Articles of Confederation with President John Hanson of Maryland, the first president of the Confederation officiating, contains a report of the committee, consisting of Mr. Duane, Mr. McKean, and Mr. Witherspoon, to whom was referred a petition memorial of Robert Aitken, printer, dated 21 January 1781, respecting an edition of the holy scriptures.

6. Read the recommendation and report of the committee.

The report of the committee states that Mr. Aitken had finished an American edition of the holy scriptures in English at a great expense. The committee recommended the Bible to the two chaplains of Congress to examine and give their opinion of the execution, who then reported on it. On September 1st, 1782, the recommendation and report were formalized and signed by James Duane as the Chairman.

7. Read the second report continued in the Journal of Congress on September 10th, 1782.

The second report states that the committee paid attention to Mr. Robert Aitken's impression of the holy scriptures, of the old and new testament. The committee was satisfied with his care and accuracy in the execution of the work. They recommended this edition of the Bible to the inhabitants of the United States and authorized Robert Aitken to publish this recommendation in the manner he deemed proper.

In conclusion, the Aitken's Bible is an important piece of American history. It was the first entire Holy Bible printed in America, authorized and recommended by the U.S. Congress and President, and helped symbolize American independence during the Revolutionary War. By using these steps, you can investigate this significant Bible and learn more about its historical context.

Breeding ghost shrimp can be an exciting and enjoyable process for aquarists of all levels. Whether you want to raise them as pets or as feeder shrimp for other fish, there are a few steps to follow to ensure a successful breeding process. In this article, we'll walk you through the process of breeding ghost shrimp and keeping them healthy and happy.

Part 1 of 3: Setting Up Your Tanks

1. Purchase a large fish tank – A minimum 5-10 gallon tank will work for breeding ghost shrimp.

2. Purchase a second tank for breeding – A smaller 2-3 gallon tank will work for the breeding process.

3. Use any filter for the main tank, and a sponge filter for the breeding tank – A sponge filter will provide a gentle flow of water which is necessary for breeding ghost shrimp.

4. Install an air pump in each tank – Ghost shrimp require oxygen-rich water, so an air pump is necessary to provide this.

5. Cover the bottom of each tank with sand or gravel – Sinking pellets and other food particles tend to fall to the bottom of the tank and the shrimp like to dig and burrow, therefore sand or gravel is essential.

6. Fill the tanks with appropriate water – Ghost shrimp prefer alkaline water with a pH between 7.0 and 8.5.

7. Keep the water at 65-82º F (18-28º C) – A stable temperature is crucial to the health of your shrimp, therefore it's important to keep the temperature at the right level.

8. Add live plants and hiding places – Ghost shrimp need hiding places such as caves or plants; they like to retreat during the day and come out at night for feeding.

Part 2 of 3: Introducing and Caring for Your Shrimp

1. Buy high-quality shrimp for pets, and feeder shrimp if you're breeding them as animal food – Purchase large-size shrimp for breeding; they should be 1-2 inches long.

2. Introduce the shrimp to the new water slowly – Allow the shrimp to acclimate by adding water from the main tank to the container you are transporting them in. Add small amounts of water with time until the bag/tank is lightening is right to but add the shrimp to the main tank.

3. Feed the shrimp tiny amounts of fish food – Feed them once a day, with only enough food that they can consume in 2-3 hours.

4. Change the water once every week or two – Change at least 20% of the water each time, and remove any debris or algae from the tank.

5. Be cautious about adding other fish to the tank – Ghost shrimp are sensitive to other fish and can be easily predated upon.

6. Check that you have both males and females – You will need at least one male and one female shrimp for breeding.

7. Look for females carrying eggs – When you see a female carrying eggs (a saddle) on its back, it's time for breeding.

Part 3 of 3: Breeding Your Ghost Shrimp

1. After a few days, transfer females carrying eggs to the breeding tank – Provide enough hiding places so the female can move around without being disturbed.

2. Wait 21-24 days until the eggs hatch – Keep the water at the same temperature and provide adequate food during this period.

3. Transfer the female back to the main tank – Once the eggs hatch, the female can be transferred back to the main tank.

4. Feed the shrimp small amounts of specialized tiny food – High-quality shrimp fry food can be purchased from any pet fish store.

5. Feed them the same food as regular shrimp once they've grown legs – When they are old enough, the fry can be fed the same food as the adult shrimp.

6. Transfer the shrimp back to the tank once they are fully grown – Once the fry have grown legs, you can transfer them back to the main tank.

7. Don't transfer the females if it causes the eggs to fail – If the eggs are disturbed during the transfer process, they may be less likely to hatch.

8. Keep watching if the young shrimp won't eat – Providing enough food and hiding places is essential to the development of young shrimp.

9. If all the shrimp die after putting them in the tank, use different water or introduce the shrimp more slowly – Ghost shrimp are sensitive to water parameters, so be mindful of this when transferring them to the tank. If they are not thriving, it may be due to issues with the water. Test your water, and make adjustments as necessary.

Breeding ghost shrimp can be a fun and rewarding experience. By following these simple steps, you can ensure that your shrimp are healthy and happy in their new home. Good luck with this fascinating process!

Becoming an attorney in California requires a lot of hard work and dedication. If you are interested in pursuing a career in law in the Golden State, here's how to do it:

1. Create a Law School Admission Council (LSAC) account.
The LSAC is the organization that manages the law school application process. You'll need to create an account on their website to get started. This will give you access to all of the resources you need to apply to law school.

2. Register for the Law School Admissions Test (LSAT).
The LSAT is a standardized test that all law school applicants must take. Make sure you register for the right test date and allow yourself plenty of time to prepare. You can find study materials and practice tests on the LSAC website.

3. Prepare for the LSAT.
The LSAT is a challenging test, so give yourself plenty of time to study. Consider taking a prep course or hiring a tutor to help you prepare. Practice tests can also be helpful in getting yourself ready.

4. Apply to accredited law schools.
Once you've taken the LSAT and received your score, it's time to apply to law school. Make sure you research the schools you're interested in and apply to those that are accredited by the American Bar Association (ABA).

5. Devote yourself to your legal education.
Law school is a challenging and demanding experience, so be prepared to work hard. Attend all of your classes, participate in discussions, and ask questions. Make the most of your time in law school by immersing yourself in the subject matter and learning as much as you can.

6. Complete your first-year classes.
Your first year of law school will be focused on core subjects like contracts, torts, and civil procedure. It's important to do well in these classes, as they will lay the foundation for the rest of your legal education.

7. Take part in extracurricular activities including law review and mock trial.
Extracurricular activities like law review and mock trial can help you develop your legal skills and gain practical experience. These activities can also look impressive on your resume when you start applying for jobs.

8. Complete second and third year courses.
In your second and third years of law school, you'll have more freedom to choose the courses that interest you. Take advantage of this opportunity to explore different areas of the law and figure out what you want to specialize in.

9. Work during your summer breaks.
Law firms and other legal organizations often offer summer internships to law students. These can be a great way to gain practical experience and make connections in the legal field.

10. Graduate with a Juris Doctor (J.D.).
After completing all of your coursework and meeting your school's graduation requirements, you'll earn your J.D. degree. This is the degree that will enable you to practice law.

11. Apply to take the California Bar Exam.
In order to become licensed to practice law in California, you'll need to pass the state bar exam. You can apply to take the exam on the California State Bar website.

12. Study for the California Bar Exam.
The California bar exam is notoriously difficult, so give yourself plenty of time to study. There are many test prep materials available, including review courses, practice exams, and study guides.

13. Take the exam.
The California bar exam is administered over two days and includes both multiple choice and essay questions. Make sure you are well-rested and focused during the test.

14. Pass the examination.
If you pass the California bar exam, congratulations! You can now officially practice law in California.

15. Send in a moral character evaluation.
Before you can be admitted to the state bar and practice law in California, you'll need to undergo a moral character evaluation. This is a background check that evaluates your fitness to practice law.

16. Take the Multistate Professional Responsibility Examination (MPRE).
In order to be admitted to the California state bar, you'll also need to pass the MPRE. This is an ethics exam that tests your knowledge of the rules and regulations governing the legal profession.

17. Comply with family support requirements.
Before you can be admitted to the California state bar, you'll need to certify that you are current on any court-ordered family support payments.

18. Provide your Social Security number.
You'll need to provide your Social Security number to the California state bar in order to be admitted to practice law.

19. Look for a job early.
There is a high demand for attorneys in California, but there is also a lot of competition. Start looking for job opportunities as early as possible.

20. Take part in campus interviews.
Many law firms and legal organizations come to law schools to conduct on-campus interviews. Take advantage of these opportunities to make connections and secure job offers.

21. Search online.
There are many online job boards and other resources that can help you find job openings in the legal field.

22. Set up informational interviews.
Reach out to attorneys and other legal professionals you admire and ask if you can interview them. These conversations can provide valuable insight into the legal profession and can help you make connections.

23. Attend bar events.
The California state bar and other legal organizations often hold events and conferences. Attend these events to meet other attorneys and learn more about the legal profession.

24. Volunteer.
Volunteering for legal aid organizations or other community groups is a great way to gain experience and make connections while giving back to your community.

25. Stay up to date with continuing legal education (CLE) requirements.
In order to maintain your license to practice law in California, you'll need to complete a certain number of hours of continuing legal education each year. Make sure you stay on top of these requirements.

26. Abide by required ethical standards.
As an attorney, you are held to high ethical standards. Make sure you understand and abide by the rules and regulations governing the legal profession.

27. Stay out of legal trouble.

7. Fertilize if necessary. Depending on the results of your soil test, you may need to add fertilizer to the soil. Use a slow-release organic fertilizer to avoid damaging the plants.

8. Purchase or harvest ginseng seeds. You can purchase ginseng seeds from a reputable supplier or harvest them yourself if you live in an area where ginseng grows naturally. Make sure to only harvest seeds from mature plants to ensure the best chance of success.

9. Keep seeds moist before planting. Ginseng seeds need to be kept moist before planting to ensure they sprout properly. Use a misting spray bottle to keep them moist.

10. Prepare your seeds for sprouting if they are not stratified. If your seeds are fresh, they may need to be stratified. This means they need to be chilled for a period of time before planting to mimic the winter season. Soak the seeds in cold water for 24-48 hours and then place them in a damp container in the refrigerator for 3-4 months.

Part 3: Planting Your Ginseng Seeds
11. Plant sprouting seeds in the spring. Once your seeds have sprouted and grown to about 2 inches in length, you can transplant them to your growing area. Plant the seeds about 1 inch deep and 6 inches apart.

12. Sow other seeds in the fall. For those seeds that have not yet sprouted, plant them in the fall after the first frost. Plant the seeds about 1 inch deep and 6 inches apart.

13. Soak seeds in bleach and water before planting. To prevent disease, soak your seeds in a solution of 10% bleach and 90% water for 10-15 minutes before planting.

14. Remove small weeds and ferns from the area. To avoid competition for nutrients, remove smaller weeds and ferns from your growing area before planting.

15. Plant large numbers of seeds quickly by scattering them. For larger planting areas, scatter the seeds evenly and rake the soil gently to cover them.

16. Plant smaller numbers of seeds more thoroughly. For smaller planting areas, plant the seeds in rows about 6 inches apart.

17. Cover the area with leaves or mulch. Covering the area with leaves or mulch helps to retain moisture and prevent weeds from growing.

Part 4: Caring for Your Ginseng Plants
18. Mark the plot discreetly or locate it using a GPS device. To avoid theft or tampering, mark your growing area discreetly or use a GPS device to locate it.

19. Keep the location secret and secure. Only share the location of your growing area with those who need to know.

20. Thin densely growing ginseng each year. Thin the plants each year to ensure they have enough space and resources to grow properly.

21. Research carefully before using pesticides and pest poison. Use caution when using pesticides or pest poison. Do your research and choose products that are safe and effective.

22. Wait for the plants to mature. Ginseng takes several years to mature. Be patient and avoid disturbing the plants during this time.

23. Don't expect the plants to stay visible year round. Ginseng plants die back in the winter and may not be visible during this time.

Part 5: Harvesting Your Ginseng
24. Harvest red berries annually after the third year. After 3-4 years, ginseng plants will produce small red berries. Harvest these berries annually and save the seeds for future planting.

25. Harvest mature plants at any point past the seventh year. After 7-10 years, ginseng plants reach maturity and can be harvested. Dig the roots carefully so as not to damage them.

Growing ginseng is a long and rewarding process. By following these steps and being patient, you can enjoy the many health benefits of this amazing plant. Remember to take care of your growing area and keep it secure, and always research before using any pesticides or pest poison. Good luck!

Using a jigsaw can be a bit intimidating at first, especially if you’ve never used it before. However, with the right preparation, equipment and techniques, you can use a jigsaw effectively and with confidence. Follow these steps to learn how to use a jigsaw the right way.

Step 1: Select a jigsaw suitable for your project.

The first step in using a jigsaw is to select the right one for your project. Look for a jigsaw that fits your hand securely and has enough power to handle the type of material you’ll be cutting.

Step 2: Select the correct blade for the material you are going to cut.

Matching the right blade to the material you’ll be cutting is crucial to achieving a good result. There are many different types of blades available for jigsaws, so take the time to select the one that’s suitable for your project.

Step 3: Prepare your workpiece for your cut.

Before you start cutting, make sure your workpiece is properly prepared. This may involve cleaning the surface, clamping it down securely and smoothing any rough patches.

Step 4: Measure and mark the cut line you need for your project.

Use a ruler or measuring tape to mark the cut line on your workpiece. Double-check the accuracy of your measurements before you begin cutting.

Step 5: Place the material you are cutting on saw horses or a workbench, or clamp it in a vice, depending on which is best suited for your purpose.

Secure your workpiece on sawhorses or a workbench to keep it stable while you cut. Alternatively, you can clamp it in place on a vice.

Step 6: Make sure you have sufficient light to see your cutting marks easily.

Good lighting is essential when using a jigsaw, especially when cutting intricate shapes. Make sure the area is well lit so you can see your cutting marks easily.

Step 7: Position the blade close to the edge of the material where you will begin your cut.

Start your cut at the point closest to the edge of the material. Be careful not to cut too deep too quickly.

Step 8: Guide your saw along its path by twisting the back of the saw in the opposite direction you want the blade to travel, keeping the blade aligned with the cut line.

Guide the saw smoothly and steadily along the cut line. To keep the blade straight, twist the back of the saw in the opposite direction you want the blade to move.

Step 9: Stop the saw if sawdust or debris accumulates blocking your view of the cut line, or if this material interferes with the travel of the saw.

If sawdust or debris starts to accumulate, stop the saw and clear the area. This will help you see the cut line clearly and ensure the blade travels smoothly.

Step 10: Complete your cut by continuing through the material, being careful to support any piece that may drop when the cut is finished until the blade is free of it.

Complete the cut, being careful to support the piece you are cutting until the blade is free. This will prevent the piece from dropping and possibly getting damaged.

Step 11: Use a sander or plane to finish edges that become spalled or rough from the cutting process.

After cutting, you may notice rough edges or spalling on the material. Use a sander or plane to smooth out any rough patches.

In conclusion, using a jigsaw is not rocket science. As long as you have the right equipment and follow these steps, you can make precise cuts in a variety of materials with ease.

How to Make No Sew Curtains

Are you in need of new curtains but don't know how to sew? Look no further! Follow these simple steps to create your own no sew curtains.

Materials:
- Fabric of your choice
- Measuring tape
- Scissors
- Iron 
- Clip-on curtain rings (optional)

Step 1: Measure your windows to decide how large your want each curtain panel to be.
Using your measuring tape, measure the height and width of your window. Decide how high and wide you want each panel to be, and add 12 inches to the height and 2 inches to the width.

Step 2: Choose your fabric, then wash, dry, and iron it, if necessary, to get rid of any shrinking and wrinkles. 
Select a fabric that complements your decor. Pre-wash and dry the fabric according to the care instructions, and iron out any wrinkles.

Step 3: Cut each panel 12 inches (30.48 centimeters) longer and 2 inches (5.08 centimeters) wider than you want them to be.
Use your measuring tape and scissors to cut your fabric to the desired size.

Step 4: Fold the bottom hem up by ½ inch (1.27 centimeters), and press it flat with an iron.
Making sure that the right side of the fabric is facing down, fold the bottom hem up by half an inch, and press it flat with an iron.

Step 5: Fold the bottom hem up again, this time by 5 inches (12.7 centimeters).
Fold the bottom hem up again, this time by 5 inches, and iron it flat.

Step 6: Fold each side hem over twice by ½ inch (1.27 centimeters), and press flat with an iron.
Fold each side hem over twice by 1/2 inch, and iron it flat.

Step 7: Fold the top hem down by ½ inch (1.27 centimeters), and press flat with an iron.
Fold the top hem down by 1/2 inch, and iron it flat.

Step 8: Fold the top hem down again, but this time by 6 inches (15.24 centimeters), and press flat with an iron.
Fold the top hem down again, this time by 6 inches, and iron it flat.

Step 9: Flip the curtain so that the right side is facing you, and press the hems flat for 3 to 5 seconds.
Flip the curtain over, so that the right side of the fabric is facing up. Press each hem flat for 3 to 5 seconds.

Step 10: Leave the top hem alone if you want to slide it onto the curtain rod, or use clip-on curtain rings.
If you want to slide the curtain panel onto the curtain rod, leave the top hem as is. Alternatively, you could attach clip-on curtain rings to the top of your curtains.

Step 11: Consider attaching some tabs to make a self-pleating curtain.
If you want your curtains to have a pleated look, consider attaching tabs to the top hem. Cut strips of fabric and sew them onto the top hem at regular intervals, creating evenly spaced pleats.

Step 12: Hang your curtains.
Now that your curtains are complete, hang them up and enjoy your new window treatment!

Soccer is a game that requires a lot of skill, strategy, and teamwork. Defending in soccer is one of the most important aspects of the game, as a strong defense can prevent the opposing team from scoring goals. Whether you are a new player or a seasoned veteran, it is always important to work on your defensive skills. In this article, we will provide tips and strategies on how to defend in soccer, and establish a training regimen that will help you become a better defender.

Establish a training regimen

To become a better defender in soccer, you need to establish a training regimen that works for you. This means focusing on specific exercises and drills that will help improve your speed, agility, and strength. Some of the best exercises for soccer players include running, jumping, and sprinting. You can also try incorporating weight training into your workout routine to build muscle and improve your endurance.

Increase your cardiovascular activity

In addition to strength training, it is important to focus on cardiovascular exercises that will increase your endurance on the field. This includes activities like running, cycling, or swimming. These exercises will help you develop the stamina necessary to keep up with the opposing team without getting tired.

Raise awareness of positional developments on the field

When defending in soccer, it is important to be aware of your position on the field at all times. This means keeping an eye on the opposing team's movements and adjusting your position accordingly. For example, if you see an opposing player making a run towards the goal, you should move into position to cut off their angle of attack.

Polish your basic skills

One of the most important aspects of defending in soccer is having good technique. This means having strong footwork, tackling ability, and the ability to read the game. Take time to hone your skills by practicing dribbling, passing, and shooting. This will improve your overall play and make you a better defender.

Know where to look

When defending in soccer, it is important to keep your eyes up and be aware of your surroundings. This means looking both at the ball and the movement of the opposing team. This will help you anticipate their moves and react more quickly to defend against them.

Cover opponents and their angles of approach

As a defender, your job is to cover your opponent and prevent them from getting into scoring position. This means taking away their angle of attack and closing down space to limit their options. You should also be aware of their strengths and weaknesses so that you can adjust your strategy accordingly.

Be determined in your mindset

Defending in soccer can be a physical and mental challenge. It is important to stay focused and determined throughout the game. This means maintaining a positive mindset and being willing to work hard to defend your team's goal.

Evaluate the opposing players style

Each player on the opposing team may have different styles of play. It is important to evaluate their strengths and weaknesses so that you can adjust your strategy accordingly. This will help you anticipate their moves and prevent them from scoring.

Cut off attacks on net and passes between players

When defending in soccer, it is important to cut off attacks on the net and passes between players. This means closing down space and taking away the opposition's options. You should also be aware of your position on the field and work as a team to defend the goal.

Limit your stabs at the ball

Jabbing your foot out to try to haphazardly prod the ball away from your opponent can compromise your balance and give him an opportunity to pass you by. Instead, focus on intercepting the ball or making a controlled tackle.

Angle your hips and your approach

When defending in soccer, it is important to angle your hips and your approach to cut off the angle of attack and limit the opposition's options.

Herd attackers into positions of pressure

You can do this by cutting off the angle of an attacker's approach in a way that is accessible to other defenders, like midfielders. This will create pressure and limit the opposition's options.

Communicate with fellow defenders

Defenders need to communicate clearly with the keeper, the midfield, and each other. If the defense is playing an offside trap, or if a defender is not in line or not marking a player, he should be informed of this loudly and quickly.

Practice one-on-one defense

One-on-one defense is an essential skill for any defender. Practice this skill by playing one-on-one with a teammate or coach, focusing on your technique and positioning.

Try a faster paced two-on-two drill

This drill will help you improve your speed and quick decision making when defending against two attackers.

Learn to defend against crosses

Crosses can be challenging to defend against, but practicing defending against them can help you improve your overall defensive strategy.

Enact a full-on penalty area defensive drill

This drill will simulate a game situation and help you develop the skills necessary to defend against shots on goal.  By following these tips and strategies, you can improve your defensive skills and become a stronger player on the soccer field.

Have you ever experienced a damaged laptop display hinge? If so, you know how frustrating it can be when your display doesn't stay in the correct position. Fortunately, there's a workaround that you can use to fix this issue without having to replace the entire laptop hinge. This wikihow article will guide you through the process of using Velcro and fishing line to strengthen your laptop display hinges, keeping your display in the right position while you work.

1. Read the entire article, and check that your specific laptop can be repaired in the way presented.

Before getting started with any repairs, it's important to read the entire article to make sure that this method will work for your laptop model. Some laptops may have different hinge designs that won't be compatible with the Velcro and fishing line method we're using here.

2. Cut two strips of the fuzzy Velcro and round the corners.

To begin the repair process, you'll need to cut two strips of fuzzy Velcro and round the corners of each strip. This will make it less likely that the Velcro will detach after gluing.

3. Glue the Velcro to the laptop display and bottom.

Next, mix your epoxy glue according to the instructions, and use it to glue the two strips of fuzzy Velcro - one on the back of the display and one on the bottom of the laptop. Make sure that the two strips are co-linear, meaning that the alignment of one strip, when extended, coincides with the alignment of the other strip.

4. Wait for the glue to dry.

After gluing the Velcro to the laptop, you'll need to wait for the epoxy glue to harden fully. This may take several hours, so be patient and allow the glue to dry completely.

5. Cut a strip of hooked Velcro to length.

Once the glue has dried, close your laptop display and cut a strip of hooked Velcro more or less to the length required when sticking it to the two glued strips in their entirety.

6. Check that the Velcro can prevent the display from falling into the closed position.

After the glue has hardened to maximum strength, check that the Velcro can now prevent the display from falling into the closed position. If it's still loose, you may need to repeat steps 3-5 with stronger epoxy glue and larger strips of Velcro.

7. Tie a fishing line loop around the laptop.

Take the fishing line and tie it into a loop which exactly encircles the laptop when the display is open to the working position. Be sure to check that the fishing line loop is strong enough to prevent the display from falling into the fully open position.

8. Glue foam tape to the laptop edge.

To finalize the repair, glue a small strip of two-sided foam tape on the edge of the laptop where the fishing line should rest. Optionally, you can also use a plastic bag closure to adjust the exact size of the fishing line loop and the working position of the laptop display.

With these simple steps, you can work around damaged laptop display hinges and fix the issue without having to replace the entire hinge. Keep in mind that this repair method may not work for all laptop models, so be sure to check if your laptop can be repaired in this way before getting started. Good luck!

Tanning in the sun is a popular leisure activity that many people enjoy during the summer months. However, it is important to tan safely and take precautions to prevent skin damage and skin cancer. Here is a step-by-step guide on how to tan in the sun safely and effectively.

1. Change into clothes that expose your skin to the sun.
Wear comfortable, lightweight clothing that will allow your skin to breathe and soak up the sun's rays.

2. Tan before 10 AM or after 4 PM for the safest results.
During these times, the sun's rays are weaker, and the UV index is less intense, making it less likely that you'll burn.

3. Apply sunscreen with SPF 15-30 at least 20 minutes before heading out.
Choose a broad-spectrum sunscreen that will protect against both UVA and UVB rays. Apply liberally to all exposed skin, paying close attention to areas that are prone to burning, such as your nose, ears, neck, and shoulders.

4. Wear UV-protecting sunglasses.
Protect your eyes from harmful UV rays by wearing sunglasses that block at least 99% of UVA and UVB rays.

5. Do not use "accelerating lotions" or other quick-tan methods.
These products can damage your skin and increase your risk of skin cancer.

6. Understand how tanning works.
Tanning is your skin's way of protecting itself from the sun by producing melanin. The more time you spend in the sun, the more melanin your skin will produce, resulting in a darker tan.

7. Lie in direct sunlight for 20-30 minutes.
Gradually increase the amount of time you spend in the sun, taking breaks every hour to reapply sunscreen and hydrate.

8. Reapply sunscreen and flip over to get an even tan.
Make sure to cover all exposed areas with sunscreen, and reapply every two hours or after getting wet or sweating.

9. Hydrate while you tan.
Drink plenty of water to prevent dehydration and heat exhaustion.

10. Do not tan for more than 1 hour at a time, even with sunscreen.
It's important to take regular breaks and give your skin a chance to rest.

11. Stop tanning if you feel pain or your skin becomes red.
These are signs of sunburn, which can cause permanent damage to your skin and increase your risk of skin cancer.

12. Supplement your tan with bronzing cream.
If you want to enhance your tan, use a bronzing cream or spray instead of spending more time in the sun.

13. Adjust the time in the sun based on skin type.
People with fair skin are more prone to burning and should spend less time in the sun than those with darker skin.

14. Know that you do not need to burn in order to get a deep tan.
Burning your skin will only cause damage and increase your risk of skin cancer.

15. Use gentle moisturizing lotions, like aloe, to treat burns.
If you do get sunburned, use aloe vera or other gentle moisturizers to soothe your skin.

16. Drink a lot of water.
Drinking water can help prevent dehydration and heat stroke.

17. Take some ibuprofen.
If you experience pain or inflammation from a sunburn, ibuprofen can provide relief.

18. Place a cool, damp towel on your skin.
Cooling down your skin with a damp towel can help reduce redness and inflammation.

19. Do not pick off skin or pop blisters.
This can cause further damage to your skin and increase your risk of infection.

20. Check your skin head to toe each month.
Take note of any moles, freckles, or other spots that look unusual or change in size or appearance. See a dermatologist if you notice any changes or have concerns about your skin.

By following these tips, you can safely and effectively achieve a sun-kissed glow without putting your health at risk. Remember, always practice safe sun habits and protect your skin from damage.

Working abroad can be a life-changing experience. Whether you are looking to gain international work experience, dive into a different culture, or simply feed your wanderlust, working abroad can fulfill a wide range of goals. However, the process of finding and obtaining a job overseas can be challenging and overwhelming, especially if you are not familiar with the legal requirements and job market of the country you are interested in. In this article, we will provide you with a step-by-step guide on how to work abroad, from choosing a location to obtaining necessary permits and regulations.

1. Choose a location.

The first step to working abroad is selecting a location that meets your personal and professional goals. Whether you are interested in Europe, Asia, or Latin America, there are plenty of opportunities to work abroad in almost every corner of the world. Do some research, talk to people who have worked in that country, and identify the job market, cost of living, and other factors that affect your decision to move.

2. Research and obtain any necessary permits and regulations.

To work abroad in most countries, you will need to obtain a work visa from that country, or a visa that allows certain types of work. Each nation has specific and individual laws regarding foreign workers, so make sure to research these when deciding where you want to work abroad. A good starting point is to check with the country's immigration department to find out what type of visa you will need and how to get it.

3. Decide if you want short-term or long-term work.

Knowing whether or not you want to spend an extended period of time working abroad will help you when seeking a position overseas. Short-term work is typically less than a year and can involve jobs such as teaching English, working on a farm, or volunteer projects. Long-term work can involve a wide range of job opportunities, including corporate positions, development work, or non-profit positions.

4. Figure out if you want to find a job and then move or move first and find a job once you are abroad.

Either option may be viable, depending on your situation and location. If you already have a job offer or secured employment before you arrive in your new country, it can give you a sense of security and peace of mind. On the other hand, if you are interested in exploring different job opportunities and don't have specific employment plans in advance, moving first and then starting the job search once you get there can be an exciting adventure.

5. Learn about the language and culture.

Immersing yourself in the language and culture of a nation abroad is the best way to gain real international experience. Even if you speak the same language, culture shock is a real phenomenon that can be overwhelming. Make an effort to learn the language, explore the local customs, and seek out cultural experiences. Understanding the local language and customs can also be an asset when interviewing for jobs in the country.

6. Develop special skills that will be valued abroad.

If you have skills in a technical area, trade, or high-demand field – such as medicine, engineering, or Teaching English as a Foreign Language (TEFL) – it may be easier to find work abroad. Having a specialized skill set that is in demand can make you more marketable and competitive in the job market.

7. Familiarize yourself with resources for finding jobs abroad.

Many resources exist to help connect job seekers with opportunities abroad. Job search engines, social media platforms, recruitment agencies, and job boards offer plenty of job listings. Websites such as LinkedIn, Glassdoor, Monster and Indeed are just a few online resources that may help in the job search.

8. Seek an overseas position with a company or organization based in your home country.

One of the easiest ways to find work abroad is to shift to an international position in a company or organization that you already work for. If your company has a global presence, explore the possibilities of transferring or applying for international positions.

9. Find a government job.

Many governments offer opportunities to work in foreign affairs, peacekeeping missions, and diplomatic missions. Check with your home country's government and/or the country you are interested in working in to learn more about these opportunities.

10. Work for a nonprofit.

Non-governmental organizations and nonprofits can also provide exciting work opportunities abroad, including positions in international development, education, or healthcare. These organizations can be a great way to make a difference in the world while broadening your horizons.

11. Volunteer abroad.

If you can't find paid employment overseas, you may want to seek volunteer work instead. Many organizations offer volunteer positions for people interested in contributing to their work and supporting their causes. Although these positions may not provide financial compensation, they can offer valuable field experience and help you build your resume.

12. Use a placement service.

Placement services are recruitment agencies that specialize in international job placement. These agencies can assist with the job search process, including visa applications, resume building, and cultural training.

13. Consider other forms of employment.

Teaching English as a Foreign Language, working on a cruise ship, or becoming a digital nomad are a few examples of jobs that can provide an opportunity to travel and live abroad.

Are you tired of manually feeding your chickens every day? An automatic chicken feeder could be the solution you need! Here's how you can make one using a few inexpensive supplies:

Materials:

- Large plastic bin without wheels
- Marker
- Hole saw
- PVC pipes (1-2 inches in diameter)
- PVC pipe fittings (elbows, tees, etc.)
- Pipe caps
- Caulking
- Wood blocks
- Concrete slabs
- Lid

Instructions:

1. Purchase a large, plastic bin without wheels. It should be big enough to hold several days' worth of chicken feed.

2. Use a marker to mark where you want to make feeding holes. Draw circles in marker of the same diameter as your PVC pipes.

3. Create the holes at the bottom of the bin using a hole saw. Be sure to wear protective gear, such as gloves and safety glasses.

4. Cut the bottom two inches of the pipe fittings using a saw, cutting about 150 degrees around. This will create an opening where the chickens can access the feed.

5. Fit the pipe fittings into the holes you've made, ensuring they are secure.

6. Make grain windows with pipe caps. These windows should balance accessibility to the grain while keeping it from pouring out of the feeder.

7. Place the modified pipe caps on the pipes, leaving two-thirds of the front missing to act as a grain window.

8. Waterproof the edges around the feeder with caulking to prevent water from spoiling the grain.

9. Secure the feeder to prevent it from moving or falling. You can nail blocks of wood to the bin to keep it in place.

10. Elevate the bin by placing it on concrete slabs. This will allow the feeding openings to be at head level with the chickens.

11. Finally, add a lid to the bin to keep the feed dry and contaminant-free.

12. Fill the feeder with chicken feed and watch your automatic feeder do its job!

If you notice any issues, feel free to make necessary changes to optimize your automatic chicken feeder.

By following these instructions and making a few modifications, you can make your chickens' feeding easier and more efficient. Happy farming!

Are you tired of making game theory decisions based solely on analysis and calculations? Why not spice things up a bit and use a wristwatch as a randomizing device?

Using a wristwatch as a randomizing device may sound unconventional, but it can add an element of surprise to your decision-making process. Here's how you do it.

Before relying on a game theory decision, assess the situation based on the information you have. For example, if you're in the middle of a football game, consider factors such as the kick returner's form and the opponents' linemen. If you decide to use a game theory approach, you can move on to the next step.

To avoid telegraphing your decision, consider using a surprise onside kick instead of an onside kick formation. In other words, make it less obvious to the opposing team. To do this, you'll need to quantify your directions. In this example, you "might" try an onside kick, but you'll need to assign a specific probability to it.

To use your wristwatch as a randomizing device, divide the 12 numbers on the watch into two sets. The first set of numbers will be from 1 to 50 seconds, and the second set will be from 51 to 60 seconds. You can assign a probability to each set based on your desired outcomes.

For example, let's say you assign a 60% probability to your watch. This means that you'll do an onside kick if, when you suddenly look at your watch, the second hand is on 1 to 30 seconds (6/10 of the way through the first set). The decision-making process will be instantaneous after looking at your watch just once.

If you're still unclear about how to use a wristwatch as a randomizing device, consider this second football example. Let's say you're trying to determine whether to run or pass the ball on third down. You might assign a 70% probability to running the ball if the second hand is on the first set of numbers (1-50 seconds) and a 30% probability to passing if the second hand is on the second set of numbers (51-60 seconds).

Using a wristwatch as a randomizing device may not be the most conventional approach, but it can certainly add an element of surprise to your game theory decisions. Give it a try and see if it works for you.

Do you want to delete protected system fonts in your Windows 7 operating system? Sometimes, you may need to delete fonts for various reasons such as freeing up space, resolving font errors, or simply personal preference. However, deleting system fonts can be tricky and potentially cause issues with your computer. Read on to learn how to delete protected system fonts in Windows 7 safely.

Part 1: Determining if the Font is a Protected System Font

1. Open the Control Panel. You can access it by clicking on the "Start" button and selecting "Control Panel" or by typing "Control Panel" in the search box.

2. Click on "Appearance and Personalization".

3. Click on "Fonts".

4. Look for the font you want to delete. If it has a shield icon next to it, it is a protected system font.

Part 2: Deleting the Font

1. Open the Registry Editor. You can access it by typing “regedit” in the search box or by pressing “Windows Key + R” and typing “regedit” in the “Run” box.

2. On the left side of the editor, open the folders HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE → Software → Microsoft → Windows NT → CurrentVersion → Fonts.

3. On the right side of the window, select the fonts you want to delete, right-click on them, and select "Delete".

4. Open any program in which you can change the font.

5. Go to the folder C:\Windows\winsxs.

6. Scroll about a fifth of the way down the long list of folders, and you should see a series of folders beginning with "amd64_microsoft-windows-font-truetype-", where “amd64” is the architecture of your system (e.g. x86), and “font-name” is the name of a font.

7. Right-click on the folder containing the font you want to delete and select "Properties".

8. Click the "Security" tab and click the "Advanced" button at the bottom of the window.

9. Click the "Owner" tab in the resulting window, then click "Edit".

10. In the new window, click on either "Administrators" or the name of your account, check the box next to "Replace owner on subcontainers and objects," and click OK.

11. Click OK on all the other Properties windows you opened to get out of them.

12. Open the folder's properties again (right-click on it and select "Properties"), click the "Security" tab, and click "Edit".

13. Select the account you chose in step 11, check the box under "Full control", and click "OK".

14. Exit the Properties window.

15. Delete the font file first, then delete the folder.

16. Go into the Registry Editor again and delete the font's entry.

17. Restart your computer.

Congratulations, you have successfully deleted a protected system font in Windows 7. Always remember to be cautious when deleting system files and ensure you have a backup before doing so.

If you're looking to draft a recording contract, you'll want to make sure you cover all the legal bases in the document to protect yourself and your artist. Below are some steps to help you format and include all the necessary elements in your recording contract.

1. Format the document: Your recording contract should be a clear, well-organized document that is easy to read. Use clear, concise language and break up the text with headings and subheadings as needed.

2. Add the title: Clearly state the title of the contract at the top of the document.

3. Identify the parties to the contract: Clearly identify the parties involved in the contract, including the artist and the record label or producer.

4. Insert your recitals: The recitals are the introductory paragraphs in the contract that state the purpose and intentions of the agreement.

5. Include a definition section: Define any specific terms or words that may be unclear to the parties involved.

6. Clarify the artist’s recording obligations: Clearly state what the artist is obligated to do in terms of recording and producing music.

7. Identify costs which will not be charged back: This section should outline any costs the artist should not be responsible for, such as marketing or promotional expenses.

8. Include an “overcall album” provision: This clause requires the artist to provide additional material if the record label determines that more recordings are necessary to fulfill the terms of the agreement.

9. Add an exclusivity provision: This provision should state that the artist cannot record music for any other label or producer during the duration of the contract.

10. Add a non-compete clause: This clause outlines the area and duration in which the artist cannot participate in similar work.

11. Identify any deposit the artist paid: If the artist had to put down a deposit, make sure to clearly state the amount and terms.

12. Explain how the artist will pay the balance of the recording fees: Clearly state the payment terms for the recording fees and how the artist is expected to pay for them.

13. Explain how the artist can cancel a recording date: Outline the cancellation policy for recording sessions and what happens if a session is cancelled.

14. Explain who owns the tracks recorded: Make it clear who owns the rights to the recordings and what the artist is allowed to do with the tracks.

15. Identify your distribution rights: State what the record label or producer is allowed to do with the produced work, including distribution and licensing.

16. Identify the royalty rate: Clearly state the percentage of royalties the artist will receive from the work created under this contract.

17. Include a covenant that the artist’s work is original: A covenant is a legally binding promise and this clause can protect against any legal disputes that may arise due to work that infringes copyright law.

18. Add an indemnity provision: An indemnity clause can protect the artist and record label from any legal disputes that may arise as a result of the recording.

19. Insert a dispute resolution clause: Outline the steps that should be taken if a dispute arises between the artist and the record label.

20. Include provisions that explain the music industry is risky: Including clauses that explain the risks of the music industry can help protect both the artist and the record label.

21. Include a termination clause: Clearly state the conditions that would allow either party to end the contract early.

22. Add a merger clause: This clause states that this contract is the final agreement and supersedes any prior versions or agreements.

23. Insert a choice of law provision: This clause states that the laws of a particular state or country will apply to any legal disputes that may arise.

24. Include the address of the parties: Clearly state the address of the artist and the record label.

25. Include signature lines: Add signature lines for both parties to sign the agreement.

26. Add a notary block: A notary block ensures that the contract is properly executed and legally binding.

27. Show the contract to your lawyer: It's always a good idea to have a lawyer review your contract before signing it.

28. Give the draft contract to the artist: Allow the artist to review the contract and ask any questions before signing.

29. Distribute copies of the signed agreement: Make sure that both parties have signed copies of the agreement for their records.

By following these steps, you can draft a comprehensive recording contract that protects both the artist and the record label.
