How to Calculate Benefits

Calculating your employee benefits package can be challenging, especially when offered a diverse selection of benefits. However, knowing how to calculate benefits and determine their value is crucial to understanding your financial well-being. By identifying your employer's contribution to health insurance, insurance available as part of your compensation package, retirement contributions, paid leave, expenses reimbursed, and additional compensation, you can add up the total value of all benefits paid for with pre-tax and post-tax dollars. Here's how to calculate benefits and determine their value.

1. Look up the value of your employer's contribution to health insurance

If you receive health insurance through your employer, it's essential to determine your employer's contribution to your premium. You can locate this value on your pay stub, employee handbook, or by asking your HR representative.

2. Calculate the value of other insurance available as part of your compensation package

In addition to health insurance, your employer may offer additional insurance, such as dental, vision, or life insurance. Determine the value of these benefits by adding up their premiums.

3. Check the benefit value for retirement contributions, including any fund matching

Retirement contributions are a crucial component of your benefits package. Determine your employer's contribution to your retirement fund and add their funds' matching contribution.

4. Add up the total number of hours or days of paid leave permitted per year and multiply that by the hourly or daily pay scale for the position

If your employer offers paid leave, calculate the benefit's value by multiplying the number of hours or days permitted per year by your hourly or daily pay scale.

5. List any expenses reimbursed by your company as part of the benefits package

Some employers will reimburse your expenses, such as tuition and textbook fees, travel expenses, and other job-related expenses. List these expenses, and determine their total value.

6. Calculate the benefit value for any employee stock purchase plans or similar vehicles.

If your employer offers employee stock purchase plans, determine their value by calculating their market value.

7. Add up any additional compensation such as bonuses and commissions

If you receive bonuses and commissions, add their total value to your benefit package.

8. Divide the results into two different lists: those paid for with pre-tax dollars and those paid for with post-tax dollars

Dividing your benefits package into two categories can help you understand the funding sources and tax implications of each benefit.

9. Total the value of all benefits paid for with post-tax dollars

Add up the total value of all benefits paid for with post-tax dollars.

10. Determine which pre-tax benefits in your compensation package receive a tax credit if purchased by a private citizen.

If you purchase pre-tax benefits, determine if they receive a tax credit when purchased by a private citizen.

11. Total the value of all benefits that would be paid for under a tax credit

Add up the total value of all benefits that would be paid for under a tax credit.

12. Estimate the tax cost of each benefit that is paid for with taxable income if you purchase it as an individual

If you purchased a benefit with taxable income as an individual, estimate the tax cost.

13. Add up the total of all three categories in your compensation package

Add up the total value of all benefits paid for with pre-tax dollars, post-tax dollars, and those included in a tax credit.

By following these steps, you can calculate your total benefit package and determine its value. Understanding your benefits package is crucial to financial planning and understanding your financial well-being.

Painting a winter tree at sunset in watercolor is a beautiful and rewarding project to take on as an artist. With the right tools and techniques, you can create a stunning piece of art that captures the magic and wonder of this natural scene. In this article, we'll guide you through the steps to paint a winter tree at sunset in watercolor.

Materials:

- #140, cold-pressed watercolor paper, cut to 6 x 9"
- Heavy cardboard or foam core board
- Pencil
- Watercolor palette
- Red, yellow, blue, brown, grey and black watercolor tubes
- Large paint brushes
- Sharpie markers, fine brush, India ink or opaque watercolor

Step 1: Prepare Your Paper

Begin by cutting a 6 x 9" piece of #140, cold-pressed watercolor paper. Place the paper on a sheet of heavy cardboard or foam core board larger than the paper, but don't mount it to the board. This allows you to work on the paper without it moving around too much.

Step 2: Separate the Sky From the Earth

Draw in pencil, a line two inches up from the bottom to separate the sky from the earth.

Step 3: Set Up Your Palette

Set up your palette by squeezing 1/2 inch amounts of tube watercolors; red, yellow, and blue. Use a large brush for each color. Load your brush to almost dripping with one of the colors and working from left to right paint a single, juicy stroke from side to side. Repeat as many times as you wish until you reach the pencil line for the earth.

Step 4: Paint the Earth

Prepare paints for the earth by squeezing out 1/4 inch amounts of browns, greys, and black. Paint the earth strip by mixing dark colors randomly.

Step 5: Research and Plan

Do your research. Look at photos or paintings of winter trees in sunset to get some ideas and inspiration. Plan the amount of space the tree will take on the paper by sketching in pencil the position of the trunk.

Step 6: Paint the Tree Trunk and Branches

Draw or paint the tree using dark media such as Sharpie markers, a fine brush and India Ink, or opaque watercolor. Bear in mind that the trunk and branches tend to taper and get smaller as they grow upward. Use a light touch to create thin branches with a fine brush or pen.

Step 7: Add the Sunset

To add the sunset, use a clean brush to mix red, yellow, and a little bit of blue to create different shades of orange. Paint the sky with light strokes of this color, blending it into the earth. Use a wet brush to blend the colors together and create a soft transition. You can also add clouds or other details to the sky or earth to give the painting more depth and interest.

Step 8: Finish Your Painting

Allow the painting to dry completely before touching it or framing it. Once it's dry, you can sign it and enjoy your beautiful artwork.

Painting a winter tree at sunset in watercolor can be a challenging but rewarding experience. With the right materials and techniques, you can create a stunning piece of art that captures the magic and wonder of nature. Follow these steps and let your creativity soar.

How to Get Federal Financial Aid to Rehabilitate Historic Buildings

If you own or plan to own a historic building, you may be eligible for federal financial aid to assist you in the building's rehabilitation. Federal financial aid can take the form of grants, loans, tax credits, and other incentives. In this article, we will guide you through the steps to apply for federal financial aid to rehabilitate historic buildings.

Consider the National Preservation Tax Incentives program.

The National Preservation Tax Incentives program provides a 20% tax credit for historic building rehabilitation. However, to be eligible for this tax credit, you need to comply with specific conditions. For example:

Meet the requirement of the 20% tax credit.

The 20% tax credit applies to qualified rehabilitation expenses of a certified historic structure. The rehabilitation expenses eligible for the credit include expenses related to property improvements, building services, development costs, and other construction activities. To be eligible for the tax credit, the total cost of rehabilitation should exceed $5,000.

Determine whether the property is a “certified historic structure.”

A building can be considered a certified historic structure if it meets either of two requirements: if the building is listed individually in the National Register of Historic Places; or if it is located in an area that is a registered historic district and is certified by the National Park Service as contributing to the historic significance of that district.

Comply with the certified-rehabilitation requirements.

To qualify for the 20% tax credit, the rehabilitation of the building must comply with certified-rehabilitation requirements. These requirements include maintaining the historic character of the building, using specific materials, and following other guidelines.

Photograph the building.

Before and after rehabilitation projects, it is crucial to document the building's condition with photographs. This documentation will help you meet the certification requirements.

Apply for the tax incentive program.

To apply for the tax incentive program, you can download the application from the National Park Service website and submit it to the National Park Service's Technical Preservation Services. You will need to provide detailed information about the building's rehabilitation, including the cost, work plans, and documentation of the building's condition before and after it underwent renovation.

Pay the application fees.

To process your application, you need to include application fees. The fees range from $250 to $2,500, depending on the total cost of rehabilitation.

Meet IRS requirements.

To claim the 20% tax credit, you need to meet IRS requirements. You will need to file Form 3468 and include it on your federal income tax return for the year you completed the rehabilitation project.

Claim your tax credit.

You can claim the tax credit by filing Form 3468 with your federal income tax return. If the credit exceeds your income tax liability, you can carry the excess credit forward for up to 20 years.

Maintain ownership of the rehabilitated building for at least five years.

To be eligible for the 20% tax credit, you need to maintain ownership of the rehabilitated building for at least five years.

Determine whether you are eligible to receive a federal grant.

Aside from the National Preservation Tax Incentives program, there are other federal programs that provide financial aid for rehabilitated historic buildings. These programs include grants, loans, and other incentives. To apply for these programs, you need to:

Apply for a DUNS number.

A DUNS number is a unique nine-digit identifier that is required to apply for federal grants and loans. You can obtain a DUNS number for free on the Dun & Bradstreet website.

Register with the System Award Management (SAM).

SAM is a database that contains information about organizations that want to do business with the federal government. You need to register with SAM to apply for federal grants and loans.

Create a username and password on Grants.gov.

Grants.gov is a website that provides a centralized location to find and apply for federal grants. To apply for federal grants, you need to create a username and password on the Grants.gov website.

Search for grants.

Grants.gov provides a variety of search options to help you find grants that match your interests and eligibility.

Consider a Challenge Grant.

The Challenge Grant program is a competitive grant program that provides matching funds for non-profit organizations that want to restore and rehabilitate historic buildings.

Review eligibility for National Park Service grants.

The National Park Service provides grants for historic preservation, including preservation planning, rehabilitation, and restoration. To be eligible for these grants, you need to meet specific requirements, such as maintaining the historic character of the building.

Join the National Trust Preservation Fund.

The National Trust Preservation Fund is a non-profit organization that provides financial aid to preserve historic buildings. By joining this fund, you can receive financial aid, technical assistance, and advocacy support to rehabilitating historic buildings.

In conclusion, getting federal financial aid to rehabilitate historic buildings can be a challenging process. However, with the right resources and tools, you can successfully apply for and receive financial aid to assist you with historic building rehabilitation.

Acorn squash is a popular variety of winter squash that's easy to grow and delicious to eat. With a little bit of preparation and care, you can grow your own acorn squash in your backyard garden. In this article, we'll guide you through the process of planting, caring for, and harvesting your own acorn squash.

1. Ensure you have at least a three and a half month growing season in full sun.

Acorn squash needs plenty of sunlight to grow properly. Make sure you have a long enough growing season to allow your squash to mature before the first frost. The ideal growing season is three and a half months, or around 105 days.

2. Purchase a packet of acorn squash seeds at your local gardening supply store.

You can find acorn squash seeds at most gardening supply stores. Look for high-quality seeds that are specifically labeled for acorn squash.

3. Start seeds inside three to four weeks before you expect the last frost of the season. Check your state’s almanac to see when that will be.

To give your acorn squash the best head start, it's a good idea to start your seeds indoors before transplanting them outside. Check your state's almanac to find out when the last frost of the season is expected in your area, and start your seeds three to four weeks before that date.

4. Cover the seeds in a warm damp paper towel for a few hours, while you prepare your soil.

Before planting your seeds, you can give them a head start by wrapping them in a warm, damp paper towel for a few hours. This will help them germinate faster.

5. Plant six seeds in three-inch (7.6 cm) pots.

Fill small pots with potting soil, and plant six acorn squash seeds in each pot. This will give you several seedlings to choose from when it's time to transplant them outside.

6. Place the seeds in a sunny window that you can supplement with fluorescent light.

Acorn squash needs plenty of sunlight to grow properly. Place your pots in a sunny window, and supplement with fluorescent light if necessary.

7. Thin the seeds to three per pot when they start to crowd.

As your acorn squash seedlings start to grow, they'll crowd each other out. Thin them down to three seedlings per pot, choosing the strongest and healthiest ones to keep.

8. Prepare your beds.

Prepare your garden bed by loosening the soil to a depth of at least 12 inches. Add compost to the soil in the winter, if possible, to help improve soil quality.

9. Aim to plant your seedlings when the soil has warmed to approximately 70 degrees Fahrenheit (21 Celsius).

Acorn squash needs warm soil to thrive. Wait until the soil has warmed to at least 70 degrees Fahrenheit before transplanting your seedlings outside.

10. Place mulch around your squash for the first few weeks if you have a weed problem.

Mulch can help prevent weeds from growing around your acorn squash plants. Spread a layer of mulch around the plants during the first few weeks after transplanting.

11. Water your squash mounds when the soil begins to dry out.

Acorn squash needs plenty of water to grow properly. Water your plants regularly, and be sure not to let the soil become too dry.

12. Look out for squash vine borers that leave “sawdust.” You can remove them by hand.

Squash vine borers can be a problem for acorn squash. Look for signs of sawdust around the base of the plants, which can indicate that the borers are present. If you find any, remove them by hand and destroy them.

13. Test the acorn squash individually after two to three months.

Acorn squash typically takes two to three months to mature. Test the squash by pressing your fingernail into the skin. If the skin is firm, the squash is ripe. If it's soft, it needs more time to mature.

14. Cut the squash from the stem, leaving approximately one inch (2.5 cm) of stem on the squash.

When your acorn squash is fully mature, use a sharp knife to cut the squash from the stem. Be sure to leave about an inch of stem attached to the squash.

15. Rinse and dry the surface, and place them side by side rather than stacking them.

After harvesting, rinse the acorn squash with cool water and dry them off. Don't stack them on top of each other, as they can bruise and damage each other. Instead, place them side by side in a cool, dry place. 

By following these simple steps, you can grow your very own acorn squash and enjoy the delicious taste of fresh, homegrown produce.

Accessing equity in your home can be a smart financial move if done correctly. It can allow you to borrow money using the equity you’ve built up in your home through mortgage payments and property value appreciation. If you’re considering accessing equity in your home, it's important to take several steps to ensure that you are obtaining the best loan terms available. In this article, we will discuss how to access equity in your home, beginning with accessing your credit report.

Part 1: Accessing Your Credit Report

1. Obtain a copy of your credit report:

Before taking any steps to access equity in your home, it's important to obtain a copy of your credit report. Contact one of the three major credit reporting agencies – Equifax, Experian, or TransUnion – to obtain a copy of your report.

2. Review your credit report:

Review your credit report carefully to ensure that it is accurate. If there are any inaccuracies, dispute them with the credit bureau. This will improve your credit score, making you more attractive to lenders.

3. Pay off existing debts:

If you have any unpaid debts, such as credit card balances, car loans, or other debts, it's important to work to pay them off. This will improve your credit score, making you more attractive to lenders.

Part 2: Determine the Amount of Equity You Can Access

1. Determine Your “Cash Out” Amount:

Create a comprehensive list of all your debts, including credit card balances and car loans, as well as any upcoming expenses such as home improvements or college tuition. Add up all of these debts to determine the cash out you will need. 

2. Request an Estimate of Your Home's Current Market Value:

Request an estimate of your home's current market value from a local appraiser or from your loan officer. You will need this information later.

3. Calculate Your Loan-to-Value Ratio:

Refer to your most recent loan statement, and add the balance of your mortgage to the cash-out amount you wish to borrow. Divide this total by the value of your home to determine your loan-to-value ratio (LTV). Most lenders will require an LTV below 80%.

Part 3: Decide on Your Loan Options

1. Consider Your Options for Accessing Home Equity:

There are several loan options available for accessing the equity in your home. These options include refinancing your mortgage, home equity loans, and lines of credit. Consider the interest rate and the total monthly payments before making a decision. 

2. Choose the Best Option for You:

If the interest rate of the refinancing option is more than 1% lower than your existing loan, refinancing may be the best option. Alternatively, if you need a smaller amount of funds, a home equity loan may be more suitable. A line of credit based on your equity works much like a credit card and may be a good option if you don't need the funds all at once.

3. Request Quotes from Several Competing Banks:

Request quotes from several different banks and compare the loan options based on the amount of payment, length of loan, interest rates, and any additional fees applicable.

4. Decide and Move Forward:

Once you have identified the best option for your needs and your budget, inform the bank that you have chosen that you'd like to move forward with your application. Complete and sign the application, attach the necessary updated paperwork, and return it to the bank.

In conclusion, equity in your home can be a valuable asset if used appropriately. If you are interested in accessing the equity in your home, it's important to take the right steps and work with a reputable lender to ensure that you receive the best possible loan terms. Obtaining a copy and review of your credit report, determining the amount of equity you can access, and researching your loan options are all important steps in accessing equity in your home.

Chelsea buns are a delicious treat that are perfect for breakfast or as a sweet snack any time of day. The combination of warm bread, butter, sugar, and cinnamon is simply irresistible. Making Chelsea buns at home might seem daunting, but with a few simple steps you can enjoy warm buns straight from your oven. Follow the steps below to learn how to make Chelsea buns:

Ingredients:
- 1 cup milk
- 2 tablespoons butter
- 1 package dry yeast
- 2 cups flour
- 1 teaspoon salt
- 2 tablespoons sugar
- 1 beaten egg
- 3 tablespoons butter, softened
- 1/2 cup brown sugar
- 1/2 cup currants
- 2 teaspoons cinnamon
- Glaze (1/2 cup powdered sugar, 1/4 teaspoon vanilla extract, and enough milk to make desired consistency)

Step 1: Warm up the milk and 2 tablespoons butter on the stove until warm and liquid.
In a small saucepan, warm up the milk and butter over low heat on your stove. Stir gently until the butter is melted and the liquid is warm.

Step 2: Whisk together 2 cups of flour, 1 teaspoon salt, yeast, and 2 tablespoons sugar in a large mixing bowl.
In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the flour, salt, yeast, and sugar until well blended.

Step 3: Create a well (hole) in the center of the flour mixture and pour in the milk/butter mixture, plus the beaten egg.
Create a well in the center of the flour mixture. Pour in the milk/butter mixture and the beaten egg. With a wooden spoon, mix everything together until well combined.

Step 4: Combine the dough with a wooden spoon, then knead for 10 minutes.
Once the dough is combined with a wooden spoon, knead it on a floured surface for 10 minutes. If the dough is too sticky, add a little more flour.

Step 5: Place in a lightly greased bowl, covered, to rise for an hour.
Place the dough in a lightly greased bowl and cover it with a clean towel or plastic wrap. Let it rise in a warm place for an hour.

Step 6: Grease a rimmed baking sheet.
Grease a rimmed baking sheet with cooking spray.

Step 7: Flatten and roll the dough into a rectangle on a floured surface.
On a floured surface, flatten the dough into a rectangle with a rolling pin. Make sure the dough is even with no holes.

Step 8: Soften 3 tablespoons of butter and spread evenly on the dough.
Using a pastry brush, spread softened butter onto the flattened dough. Make sure the butter is evenly distributed.

Step 9: Mix up the brown sugar, currants, and cinnamon and then spread it evenly on the butter.
In a small mixing bowl, mix together brown sugar, currants, and cinnamon. Spread this mixture evenly on top of the buttered dough.

Step 10: Roll the entire dough rectangle up along the long side, leaving you with a raw dough roll.
After spreading the brown sugar mix, roll the dough up along the long side to create a log.

Step 11: Cut perpendicular to the roll to make nice individual rounds.
Cut the dough roll into even sized pieces perpendicular to the log. Place the rolls evenly spaced onto your greased baking sheet.

Step 12: Set the rolls in your greased dish and let them rise for another 30 minutes.
Let the rolls rise for another 30 minutes. They will become larger and touch each other on the baking sheet.

Step 13: Cook your buns for 20-25 minutes at 400F, or until golden brown.
Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Bake the buns for 20-25 minutes until golden brown.

Step 14: Apply your glaze right out of the oven, then eat while still hot.
Whisk powdered sugar, vanilla extract, and milk until a smooth glaze is formed. Once the buns are baked, apply the glaze using a pastry brush. Serve your Chelsea buns still warm and enjoy!

Harvesting pecans is a fun and rewarding activity for those who enjoy fresh, delicious nuts straight from the tree. However, it's important to know when and how to harvest the nuts to ensure a successful harvest. In this article, we'll provide you with a step-by-step guide on how to harvest pecans.

Part 1: Preparing to Harvest Pecans

1. Observe the pecan trees for indications the nuts are ready to fall.
The first step to harvesting pecans is to keep an eye on the trees and wait for them to show signs that the nuts are ripe and ready to be harvested. Pecans usually start falling from the trees in late September or early October in most regions. Look for the following indications that the nuts are ready:

- When the green outer hulls start to split and turn brown, it's a sign that the pecans are ready to be harvested.
- Shake a few branches of the tree and see if any nuts fall to the ground.
- Look for trees that have had a good crop in the past. If you see a tree where the nuts are large and healthy, chances are that it will produce a good crop again.

2. Establish the fact that the nuts your target tree are bearing are worth the efforts you will put forth.
Before you start harvesting pecans, it's important to determine if the nuts you're targeting are worth the effort. Some trees produce small or low-quality nuts that are not worth harvesting. Look for the following indications that the nuts are of good quality:

- The nuts are large and plump, with no signs of damage or rot.
- The tree has a consistent crop of nuts that are all similar in size and quality.
- The nuts have a good flavor and texture when tasted.

3. Observe the tree itself for indications of the nut crop, both in quality and quantity.
When looking at a pecan tree, there are several indicators of the quality and quantity of the nut crop. Look for the following indications:

- The tree has a good number of branches with nuts growing on them.
- The nuts are evenly spaced on the branches, indicating that the tree is healthy and producing a consistent crop.
- The leaves of the tree are green and healthy, indicating that the tree is healthy and well-nourished.

4. Watch for the husks to begin splitting.
As mentioned earlier, one of the signs that the pecans are ready to be harvested is when the green outer hulls start to split and turn brown. This indicates that the nuts are ready to be picked and that you should start looking for them on the ground.

5. Mow around trees with lawn grasses beneath them, circling the tree so that the clippings discharge away from the trunk, while beginning to circle as near the trunk as possible.
To make it easier to find the pecans when they fall to the ground, it's important to keep the area around the tree clean and well-kept. You can do this by mowing around the tree with a lawn mower and circling the tree so that the clippings discharge away from the trunk. Start by mowing as close to the trunk as possible, then gradually expanding the circle as you move away from the tree.

6. Pick up pecans when they begin to drop, since wet weather can be detrimental to the nuts, and foraging wildlife may beat you to them if they are left on the ground.
It's important to pick up the pecans as soon as they start falling to the ground. This will prevent them from getting wet, which can damage the nuts, and it will also prevent wildlife from getting to them before you do. You can pick up the nuts by hand or use a nut gatherer to make the task easier.

7. Keep leaves raked up or blown away using a leaf blower if possible, since finding the pecans in a sea of similarly colored leaves will make the task even more difficult.
Leaves can make it harder to find the pecans on the ground, so it's important to keep them raked up or blown away using a leaf blower. This will make it easier to find the nuts and prevent them from getting lost in a sea of similarly colored leaves.

Part 2: Harvesting and Storing the Pecans

1. Harvest the pecans using a method that's appropriate for your scale.
Once you've collected the pecans, you can either shell them yourself or take them to a commercial processor to have them shelled. The method you choose will depend on how many pecans you have and how much time you have to spend on the task.

2. Sort out deformed or damaged nuts when you have finished harvesting them.
When you're finished harvesting the pecans, sort through them and remove any that are deformed or damaged. These nuts will not store well and should be discarded.

3. Sack your pecans for storage.
To store your pecans, place them in a breathable sack or mesh bag. This will allow air to circulate and prevent them from getting moldy or rotting. You can store the sacks in a cool, dry place such as a pantry or garage.

4. Shell your nuts.
When you're ready to eat the pecans, you'll need to shell them. You can do this using a nutcracker or by hand, depending on how many nuts you have. Once the nuts are shelled, they can be eaten raw or roasted in the oven for a delicious snack.

In conclusion, harvesting pecans can be a fun and rewarding activity, as long as you know when and how to do it. By following the steps outlined in this article, you can ensure a successful harvest and enjoy fresh, delicious pecans throughout the year.

How to Recognize a Good Listener

Have you ever had a conversation with someone and felt like they weren't really listening to you? It can be frustrating and make you feel undervalued. On the other hand, when someone is a good listener, it can make you feel heard and understood. Whether you're trying to build better communication skills or just want to find someone who is attentive, here are some things to look for in a good listener.

1. See if the listener is 'in the moment'.

A good listener will be present and engaged in the conversation, rather than being distracted by external stimuli or their own thoughts. They might lean in slightly, nod along, or make small sounds of agreement or encouragement, like "mm-hmm" or "yeah".

2. See if the listener is maintaining, or making, eye contact.

Another way to tell if someone is engaged in the conversation is if they are making eye contact with you. They might be looking directly at you or glancing at your face frequently. This shows that they are focused on what you're saying and not merely pretending to listen.

3. Look to see if he is responding in any fashion.

A good listener will respond to what you're saying in a way that shows they are paying attention. They might nod, smile, or make a thoughtful expression when you say something meaningful. If they're not sure what to say, they might pause for a moment before responding, rather than jumping in with a generic response.

4. Note if the listener is actually listening, or interrupting.

One of the most frustrating things in a conversation is being interrupted. A good listener will let you finish your thoughts before adding their own perspective. If they do interrupt, it will usually be to ask a clarifying question or make a relevant comment.

5. The Listener Will Parrot Back What You Are Saying When Appropriate.

Every once in a while, a good listener will parrot back what you say to indicate they are paying attention and that they are right in your story with you. For example, if you say, "I'm really nervous about the job interview next week," they might respond with, "So you're feeling anxious about the interview coming up?"

6. The Listener Will Only Finish Your Sentence When Appropriate.

A good listener will only finish your sentence when the timing is right, not to try to rush you through your story or to help you out when you are at a loss of words, but to show that they are on the same wavelength as you. For example, if you say, "I'm not sure what to do about this issue -" they might finish with, "you want to take some time to think it over before making a decision?"

7. The Listener Goes By the 80% Listening, 20% Talking Rule.

A good listener knows that the art of being a good listener (whether that is because they just intuitively know or because they are actually aware of the rule) will listen about 80% of the time during the course of the conversation and only spend 20% of the conversation talking. This ensures that you are the focus of the conversation and can feel fully heard.

8. The Listener Will Keep The Conversation Focused on Your Topic of Discussion.

There is nothing more annoying than to open a conversation with someone and they change the topic on you in the middle of what you are trying to express. A good listener will keep the conversation on track with the topic you want to discuss until it is fully finished.

9. The Listener Will Ask You Thoughtful and Open-ended Questions About What You Are Talking About.

A good listener will ask you thoughtful questions that will lead you into opening up into further detail about your topic of discussion. This shows that they care about your perspective and are willing to invest the time and energy to fully understand what you're saying.

10. The Listener Knows How to Empathize With You.

When a good listener feeds back how you are feeling, their description of the feeling or emotion will actually match how you are feeling. For example, if you say, "I'm feeling really disappointed," they might respond with, "It makes sense to me that you would feel disappointed in that situation." This shows that they understand and respect your emotional experience.

By looking for these qualities in a conversation partner, you can identify someone who is a good listener and build more meaningful connections. Additionally, if you aspire to be a better listener, by following these tips you can begin to develop the skills necessary to be an attentive communicator.

Heterocyclic organic chemistry is a fascinating branch of organic chemistry that deals with the chemistry of cyclic organic compounds with at least one heteroatom in its structure. 1. Understand the Basics of Heterocyclic Chemistry

To be knowledgeable with the subject of heterocyclic chemistry, it is essential first to understand the basics of this field. Heterocyclic compounds are cyclic organic compounds that contain at least one heteroatom, which is an atom other than carbon. The heteroatom can be nitrogen, oxygen, sulfur, or any other element.

2. Learn About the Different Types of Heterocyclic Compounds

Heterocyclic compounds are classified based on the type of heteroatom present in the ring. The most common heteroatoms found in heterocyclic compounds are nitrogen, oxygen, and sulfur. Examples of heterocyclic compounds include pyridine, pyrrole, furan, and thiophene.

3. Understand the Synthesis of Heterocyclic Compounds

The synthesis of heterocyclic compounds is mainly by the process of cyclization of a linear compound that includes a heteroatom in its structure. This process is done through various methods, including the Friedel-Crafts reaction, the Hantzsch pyridine synthesis, and the Knorr synthesis, among others.

4. Study the Properties of Heterocyclic Compounds

Besides electronic and spectroscopic properties of heterocyclic compounds can be very interesting to study and to evaluate based on its applications in many types of industries. The properties of heterocyclic compounds are also dependent on their ring size and the nature of the heteroatom present in the ring.

5. Learn About the Applications of Heterocyclic Compounds

Heterocyclic compounds have a wide range of applications in various industries, including medicine, agriculture, and the chemical industry. Some examples include the use of pyridine in the manufacture of pharmaceuticals, the use of pyrimidine in agrochemicals, and the use of imidazole in corrosion inhibitors.

6. Keep Up-to-Date with Research in the Field

This area of organic chemistry is a relatively new to the chemical science, and there is still an actively ongoing research that is done on these compounds and its derivatives. To be knowledgeable in the field, it is essential to stay up-to-date with current research and trends in heterocyclic chemistry.

In conclusion, heterocyclic organic chemistry is an interesting and diverse field with numerous applications in various industries. To be knowledgeable in this subject, it is crucial to understand the basics of heterocyclic chemistry, learn about the different types of heterocyclic compounds, understand their synthesis and properties, and keep up-to-date with research in the field. If you're looking for a way to keep your furry friend safe and contained, an electric dog fence may be just what you need. This can be a daunting task, but with the right approach, you and your dog can learn to use the fence safely and effectively. Here's how to train a dog to use an electric fence:

Part 1: Introducing Your Dog to the Boundary

Step 1: Install the Fence

Before you can begin training your dog to use an electric fence, you need to install the fence first. Follow the manufacturer's instructions carefully to ensure that the fence is installed correctly.

Step 2: Get Your Dog on a Lead

Step 3: Walk to the Boundary with Flags

With your dog on the lead, casually walk to the boundary of the electric fence where the flags are. These flags mark the perimeter of the fence and will help your dog understand where the boundaries lie.

Step 4: Repeat the Lesson

Repeat the same lesson on days two and three to reinforce the idea of the boundary. The repetition will help your dog understand the concept and learn the boundaries quickly.

This will help them understand that their safety is important and they will be rewarded for staying within the boundaries.

Step 7: Practice in Different Areas

Continue this lesson at a number of different areas around the boundary of the electric fence. This will help your dog understand that the boundary extends around the entire area and not just in one spot.

Stay with the dog when it's in the yard until they are comfortable and confident. This will help them feel safe and reduce their anxiety.

Step 3: Teach off Lead and Unsupervised

Teach the “off lead unsupervised” lesson by keeping a close eye on your dog for two weeks from inside the house. Before and after each unsupervised session in the pet containment area, continue the play and praise routine to continue to reinforce that the yard is a happy, fun, and safe place to be.

Step 4: Remove the Flags

Once your dog has learned where the boundaries lie, remove the flags. This will help your dog understand that the boundary is now permanent and they can continue to enjoy their safe pet containment area.

In conclusion, training your dog to use an electric fence can take some time and patience but it's worth it to keep your furry friend safe and contained. Follow the steps above and you'll be well on your way to having a happy and well-trained pup.

Have you ever wanted to add a pop of color to your room but don’t want to spend a lot of money on décor? Well, you’re in luck because with just a few supplies, you can make a beautiful paper dahlia that will brighten up any space! Follow these simple steps to create your own paper dahlia.

Part 1 – Gathering Your Supplies

Before you get started, you’ll need a few supplies. Here’s what you’ll need:

- 10 sheets of card stock paper in different colors
- Scissors
- Paint and a sponge
- Glue
- Plastic plate
- Fringe paper

Part 2 – Cutting the Card Stock Papers

Cut the card stock papers into 4 inch squares. You’ll need a total of 50-60 squares to create the dahlia.

Part 3 – Painting the Papers

Pour a small amount of paint into a palette and dip your sponge in it. Dab the sponge onto the paper squares until they are covered in paint. Allow them to dry completely before moving on to the next step.

Part 4 – Folding the Papers

Apply a line of glue to top right corner of the square as shown. Then, fold the left side of the square to the center and wrap the right side of the square over it to make a cone shape. Repeat this step with all of the paper squares.

Part 5 – Attaching the Cones to the Plate

Use the plastic plate as the base. Paste the cone on the back side of the plate leaving a one inch gap between each cone you paste. Dab glue in a V shape to the back of each cone. Glue it in between two cones of the first layer so that it sticks nicely. Repeat this step with the remaining cones until you have formed 5-6 layers depending upon the size of the plate.

Part 6 – Making the Center of the Flower

Once you reach the point where the plate is almost covered, it is time to make the center of the flower. Roll the fringe paper and dab a small amount of glue when you reach the end of the paper and attach another paper to the roll. Do this until the center piece is formed to a desired size. Apply hot glue at the base of the center piece and glue it to the flower.

Part 7 – The Final Touch

Be amazed at your beautiful creation! Finally, glue a thread on the back of the plate and hang it on the wall using a command hook or thumb tack. 

Now that you’ve made your own paper dahlia, you can experiment with different colors and sizes to create a unique decoration for any room in your home. Enjoy!

How to Manage a Change in Ownership (when Taking over a Business)

Managing a change in ownership can be a daunting task, especially when it comes to taking over someone else's business. However, it can also be an exciting opportunity to create something new and rewarding. As the new owner, it is your responsibility to make sure that you handle the transition smoothly by communicating effectively with employees, ensuring that everyone is on the same page, and keeping the business running smoothly. Here are some tips to help you manage a change in ownership:

1. Communicate with your employees

The first step in managing a change in ownership is to communicate with your employees. Hold individual sessions with each of your employees, explain the reason for the change in ownership, and help them understand how it will affect them. Make sure that you listen to their concerns, answer their questions honestly, and reassure them about their job security.

2. Develop a strategy for each employee

Once you have communicated with your employees, it is time to develop a strategy for each of them. Consider what their strengths and weaknesses are, and how they could fit into the new business. Be transparent about your goals and give your employees a sense of ownership in the transition.

3. Develop personal relationships with your staff

Developing personal relationships with your staff is a crucial step in managing a change in ownership. Take time to get to know your employees individually and find out what motivates them. Create a sense of camaraderie and team spirit to help them feel at home in the workplace.

4. Offer your employees a range of options

It is important for your employees to feel that they have a range of options that they could pursue in the short term or long term. Offer them training opportunities, promotions, and other incentives that will help them feel valued and invested in the future of the business. Be open to new ideas and suggestions from your employees, and encourage them to take ownership of their roles.

5. Keep your employees informed

Communication is key when managing a change in ownership. Keep your employees informed about the progress of the transition, any changes in policies, and any other developments that may affect them. Make sure that they have the information they need to feel confident and secure in their roles.

In conclusion, managing a change in ownership can be a challenging process, but it can also be a rewarding one. By communicating effectively with your employees, developing personal relationships with them, and offering them a range of options, you can help ensure a successful transition and a bright future for your business.

How to Recaulk a Bathtub

Recaulking a bathtub or shower is a straightforward process that can be done with a few basic tools. Old caulk can become moldy or discolored, potentially leading to water damage if left unchecked. Thankfully, recaulking is an easy and affordable way to prevent these issues. Here's how to do it:

1. Clean the tub or shower area with a bathroom surface cleaner that also removes soap scum.
Before beginning the recaulking process, it's important to clean the area thoroughly. Make sure to remove all soap scum and any other buildup that could interfere with the caulk's adhesion. Use a bathroom surface cleaner for best results.

2. Strip the existing caulk from the tub or shower area.
If there is already caulk in place, it will need to be removed in order to apply new caulk properly. Use a caulk removal tool or a putty knife to gently scrape away the old caulk. Take care not to damage the surrounding area.

3. Scrub the joints where the caulk had previously been with rubbing alcohol.
To ensure that the new caulk adheres properly, the area must be completely clean and free of residue. Use a cloth soaked in rubbing alcohol to wipe down the joints where the caulk was removed.

4. Vacuum out any pieces of caulk that may have gotten stuck between the tile and the tub or shower pan.
Even after the old caulk has been scraped away, there may be small pieces or debris still lingering in the joints. Use a vacuum with a crevice attachment to thoroughly clean out any leftover bits.

5. Spray on a 10% bleach to 90% water solution that will kill mold and mildew that may have grown when water got into the loose caulk joints.
Mix a solution of bleach and water to kill any lingering mold or mildew. Spray the solution onto the area and let it sit for a few minutes before wiping it away.

6. Allow the tub or shower area to dry at least overnight.
Before beginning the recaulking process, make sure the area is completely dry.

7. Choose a type of caulk to use for recaulking.
Select a caulk that is specifically meant for use in areas with frequent exposure to water. Silicone caulk is a popular choice for bathtub and shower areas.

8. Cut the tip off of the tube of caulk.
Use a utility knife to cut the tip off of the tube of caulk at a 45-degree angle.

9. Squeeze a bead of caulk no more than 1/4 inch (0.6 cm) evenly down the vertical joints first.
Starting at the highest point, apply a thin bead of caulk down the length of each joint, taking care not to overapply.

10. Smooth your finger over the fresh bead of caulk to press it evenly into the joint.
Once the caulk has been applied, use your finger to gently smooth it out and press it into the joint.

11. Squeeze a bead of caulk no more than 1/4 inch (0.6 cm) evenly into the horizontal joints around the tub or shower.
After the vertical joints have been caulked, move on to the horizontal joints around the tub or shower.

12. Smooth your finger over the fresh bead of caulk to press it evenly into the joint.
As before, use your finger to smooth out the fresh caulk evenly and press it into the joint.

13. Apply an additional small amount of caulk to any places that seem a little thin and seem to need a little extra caulk.
If any areas seem particularly thin, you can add an extra bit of caulk to ensure complete coverage.

14. Allow the caulk to set and dry for 24 hours, then drain water when completely dry.
It's important to give the caulk ample time to dry before using the tub or shower again. Wait at least 24 hours before using the area and make sure to drain all the water when completely dry.

That's it! With these simple steps, you can easily recaulk your bathtub or shower and keep your bathroom looking its best.

Vegan pumpkin pie is a delicious and healthy alternative to traditional pumpkin pie. With just a few simple steps, you can create a mouth-watering dessert that everyone will love. Follow these easy instructions to make your own vegan pumpkin pie.

Ingredients:
- For the crust:
  - 1 1/4 cups all-purpose flour
  - 1/2 teaspoon salt
  - 1/2 cup vegetable shortening
  - 3-4 tablespoons ice water

- For the filling:
  - 1 (14-ounce) block of firm tofu
  - 1 (15-ounce) can pumpkin puree
  - 3/4 cup granulated sugar
  - 1 teaspoon salt
  - 1 teaspoon cinnamon
  - 1/2 teaspoon ground ginger
  - 1/4 teaspoon nutmeg
  - 1/4 teaspoon allspice

Instructions:

1. In a mixing bowl, combine the flour and salt.

2. Cut the vegetable shortening into cubes and add it to the flour mixture. Mix it all together using a pastry blender until the mixture becomes crumbly.

3. Pour the water 1 tablespoon at a time over the flour mixture and mix it with a fork. Keep mixing until the dough comes together in a ball.

4. Cover the dough with plastic wrap and chill it for at least 30 minutes.

5. As the dough chills, preheat your oven to 450°F (230°C).

6. Take the dough out of the fridge and roll it out until it is ¼-inch (0.64 centimeters) thick and a little bit bigger than your pie dish.

7. Transfer the dough into the pie dish and press it down to fit the pan.

8. Pierce the bottom of the crust several times with a fork and bake the crust for 15 minutes at 450°F (230°C).

9. Take the crust out of the oven and set it aside to cool.

10. Preheat your oven to 450°F (230°C).

11. Put the tofu, pumpkin, sugar, salt, and spices in a blender and blend the ingredients together until they are smooth.

12. Pour the mixture into the baked pie crust.

13. Bake the pie for 15 minutes, then reduce the temperature to 350°F (175°C) and continue baking for another 40 minutes.

14. Let the pie cool before serving it.

15. Alternatively, you can make a crustless pie by putting all of the ingredients into a blender or food processor and blending them together until they are smooth.

16. Pour the filling into a pie dish and bake the pie for 55 to 60 minutes at 350°F (175°C).

17. Let the pie cool to room temperature and then chill it in the fridge for 3 to 4 hours before serving it.

Vegan pumpkin pie is a perfect dessert to serve at Thanksgiving, Christmas, or any other special occasion. You can also customize this recipe by adding your favorite toppings such as whipped cream or caramel sauce. Enjoy your delicious vegan pumpkin pie!

How to Act Immediately to Lessen Brain Damage from a Stroke

If you suspect someone may be having a stroke, time is of the essence. Every minute counts when it comes to protecting the brain as much as possible. Follow these steps to act immediately and lessen brain damage from a stroke.

Headline: Save brain cells or a life: act right then.

1. Urge anyone involved to "get tests right now" for stroke and determine whether there is a need for emergency medical care.
 
2. Get special care within three hours (or less if possible). This may involve emergency treatments by trained emergency responders and/or at a clinic or hospital within 60, 120, or even 180 minutes of the onset of symptoms. 

3. Determine the time that the first signs seemed to begin to occur. This information can be very helpful to medical professionals in determining proper treatment.

4. Call the Emergency Medical Services (EMS) for an ambulance. Call the emergency number in your area or Emergency Services without delay for an ambulance to take the individual to the hospital.

5. Get advanced life support in the ambulance if available, if not, use non-EMS ambulance (rural/volunteer fire department, etc.). 

6. Quickly take the person to the nearest city or large town with EMS care available. If necessary, transport the victim yourself.

7. Check a list of signs of a stroke, such as in the "Tips" section below. 

8. Take action immediately. Do not roll over and go back to sleep. 

9. Make sure the person only drinks water until they get a medical evaluation. Do not offer them alcohol, caffeine/coffee, tea, or soft drinks as a "pick me up" or boost. 

10. Err on the side of caution. The person may not be aware of, or may not have obvious symptoms that they have had a stroke. 

11. Help the possible stroke victim decide to get a medical evaluation/examination without delay. 

12. Apply a cloth-covered ice bag/ice pack on the head. Do not apply heat, such as a hot pack.

Tips: 
- Some common signs of stroke include sudden numbness or weakness in the face, arms, or legs (especially on one side of the body), confusion, trouble speaking or understanding, trouble seeing in one or both eyes, trouble walking, or severe headache without any known cause. 
- Time is of the essence when dealing with a stroke, so act fast. If you suspect a stroke, do not wait to see if symptoms worsen. Call for emergency services immediately. 
- Remember not to hesitate when it comes to helping someone you believe is having a stroke. Quick action can greatly improve a person's chances of recovery and help prevent further brain damage.

How to Heal Skin Damage from Frostbite

Frostbite is a serious condition that occurs when the skin and underlying tissues freeze due to prolonged exposure to cold temperatures. Skin damage resulting from frostbite can be painful and take a long time to heal. If you or someone you know is suffering from skin damage caused by frostbite, there are steps you can take to help speed up the healing process. In this article, we'll look at how to heal skin damage from frostbite and what you can do to prevent future occurrences.

Move to a Warmer Place or a Sheltered Area

The first thing you should do if you suspect you have frostbite is to move to a warmer place or a sheltered area. Exposure to cold temperatures will only worsen the damage to your skin, so it's important to get to a warmer area as soon as possible.

Elevate the Injured Area

Elevating the injured area can help to reduce swelling and promote healing. If your hands or feet are affected by frostbite, try to keep them elevated above heart level.

Take off Any Tight Fitting Clothes or Jewellery

If you have frostbite on your fingers or toes, remove any tight-fitting clothes or jewellery. These items can restrict blood flow to the affected area and limit the body's natural healing response.

Pour Water with a Temperature of 104–108 °F (40–42 °C) into a Water Bottle or a Hot Compress Pad

Once you've moved to a warmer area and elevated the injured area, you can begin to warm the affected skin. Start by pouring water with a temperature of 104–108 °F (40–42 °C) into a water bottle or a hot compress pad. Gently place the bottle or pad on the affected area for 20-30 minutes at a time. Repeat this process several times a day.

Pour Warm Water into a Basin

You can also soak the affected area in warm water. Fill a basin with warm water and immerse the affected area for 15-20 minutes at a time. Remember to keep the water at a comfortable temperature - never use hot water as this can worsen the injury.

Avoid Massaging or Rubbing the Area

While it may be tempting to massage or rub the affected area to promote circulation, this can actually do more harm than good. Avoid massaging or rubbing the area, as this can cause further damage to the skin.

Never Use Dry Heat to Heal Frostbite

Using dry heat - such as a heating pad or heat lamp - can damage the skin and worsen the injury. Stick to using moist heat when warming the affected area.

Avoid Touching Any Blisters on a Frostbite Injury

If blisters form on the affected area, avoid touching them. Blisters can be very painful and prone to infection, so it's important to keep the skin clean and dry.

Wrap the Blistered Area with Gauze or a Clean Cloth

If you have blisters on the affected area, wrap them with gauze or a clean cloth. This can help to protect the skin and prevent further injury.

If Possible, Have a Medical Professional Drain Any Blisters

If your blisters are especially large or painful, it may be necessary to have them drained by a medical professional. This can help to reduce pain and promote healing.

Take Acetaminophen (Tylenol) for Pain Relief

If you're experiencing pain as a result of frostbite, you can take acetaminophen (Tylenol) for relief. Avoid taking aspirin or ibuprofen, as these can make the injury worse.

Consult with Your Doctor if Your Blisters Do Not Heal or the Skin Does Not Return to Normal After Three Months

If your skin does not return to normal after three months, or if your blisters do not heal, it's important to consult with your doctor. They may recommend further treatment to promote healing.

Ask Your Doctor About Other Treatment to Help Your Skin Heal

There are several different treatments that can help to heal skin damage from frostbite. Speak with your doctor to determine which treatment is right for you.

Notice if You Feel Pain, Numbness, or Needles and Pins on the Surface of the Exposed Skin

If you're exposed to cold temperatures for a prolonged period, you may experience pain, numbness, or needles and pins on the surface of your skin. These are all indications of frostbite and should be taken seriously.

Check for Any Darkened, Red, or Gray Areas on the Exposed Skin. The Texture of the Skin in the Affected Area May Also Feel Hard and You May Develop Blisters

If you suspect you have frostbite, check for darkened, red, or gray areas on the exposed skin. The texture of the skin in the affected area may also feel hard and you may develop blisters.

Be Aware of the Three Levels of Frostbite

Frostbite can be divided into three levels - frostnip, superficial frostbite, and deep frostbite. Frostnip is the mildest form of frostbite and can be treated by warming the affected area. Superficial and deep frostbite are more severe and require medical attention.

In conclusion, skin damage resulting from frostbite can be painful and slow to heal. If you suspect you have frostbite, it's important to take action quickly to prevent further damage to the skin. Remember to move to a warmer area, elevate the injured area, take off any tight-fitting clothes or jewellery, and warm the affected skin with moist heat. Avoid massaging or rubbing the area, and never use dry heat to heal frostbite. If you're experiencing pain or blisters, seek medical attention and consult with your doctor about other treatments that can help to heal the skin.

Marble countertops are an elegant and timeless addition to any kitchen or bathroom. Buying a marble countertop requires careful consideration, research, and planning. From determining the scope of your project to finding the right fabricator, this article will guide you through the process of buying a marble countertop.

Part 1: Planning and Preparation

1. Determine the Scope of Your Project
Before you start shopping for marble countertops, it is important to determine the scope of your project. Decide on the size, shape, and color of the countertop you want. Consider the purpose of the countertop, such as whether it will be used for cooking, baking, or simply aesthetic purposes.

2. Decide If You Can Do It Yourself
Marble countertops can be installed by a professional or a homeowner with some DIY experience. Consider your skill level and the time it will take to complete the project. If you are not confident in your abilities, it may be best to hire a professional.

3. Find Out About Permits
If you are making significant changes to your kitchen or bathroom, such as removing walls or cabinets, you may need a permit. Contact your local building department to find out what permits are required.

4. Take Into Consideration Your Design Knowledge
Marble countertops are available in a wide range of colors and patterns. If you are not familiar with different types of marble, it may be helpful to do some research or consult with a designer before making a final decision.

Part 2: Choosing Your Marble Countertop

5. Find the Stone
Visit a local stone distributor or fabricator and ask to see the available inventory. Look at samples and ask questions to learn more about each type of marble.

6. Draw a Sketch of Your Project or Provide Blueprints
Before you can get an accurate estimate for your marble countertop, you will need to provide the fabricator with a sketch or blueprint of your project. This should include walls, cabinets, sink locations, and any other relevant dimensions.

7. Ask About Fabrication and Installation
Ask the supplier if they fabricate or install their own material. If not, they may be able to refer you to a reputable fabricator.

8. Find out the Square Foot Cost
Knowing the square foot cost will help you compare estimates from different fabricators. Be sure to ask if there are any additional charges, such as delivery or installation fees.

9. Obtain Several References
Ask for references and call every one to ask about overall quality, project timeliness, project cleanliness, or any damage. This will help you gauge the reliability and reputation of each fabricator.

10. Verify Licenses
Verify the contractor's license and business licenses with the local or state agencies. This will ensure that the fabricator is properly licensed to work in your area.

Part 3: Installation

11. Get a Written Estimate and Schedule
Once you have decided on the material and installer, ask for a written estimate and schedule. This should include the cost of the marble, installation, and any additional fees.

12. Write a Joint Check
For larger projects, when payment is made for material and labor, write a joint check to both the fabricator and supplier. This will help ensure that both parties receive payment.

13. Help with the Layout of the Project
Ask if you can help with the layout of the project on your marble or granite slab. This will ensure that the marble is cut to the correct specifications.

14. Be On-Site During Installation
Try to be on-site the day of installation to answer any questions that may arise during installation. This will ensure that the project goes smoothly and the countertop is installed correctly.

15. Seal Your Countertop
Make sure all stone is professionally sealed with a professional-grade sealer. This will help protect the marble from stains and damage.

16. Make Final Payment When Satisfied
Finally, do not make a final payment until you are satisfied with the installation and the quality of the countertop. This will help ensure that any issues are resolved before you pay in full.

Buying a marble countertop requires careful planning and research. By following these steps, you can ensure that you find the right fabricator, choose the perfect marble, and have a beautiful and functional countertop installed in your home.

Are you in the market for a new home, but not sure where to start with financing? This wikiHow article will guide you through the steps of finding the best home financing in today's market.

1. Determine your loan needs and desires.
Before you start researching lenders, think about what you need and want in a loan. What type of loan do you need? What is your budget? What terms are important to you, such as the length of the loan or interest rate? Clarifying your needs and desires will help you find a lender who can meet them.

2. Research online to gain understanding of where rates are at the moment and to fill in any personal knowledge gaps.
Do your online research to learn about the current market rates and any concepts or terminology you may be unfamiliar with. This will help you understand the loan options and terms available to you, and prepare you for talking to lenders.

3. Ask those whose financial judgement you respect if they can recommend someone personally.
Talk to friends, family members, or colleagues who have recently purchased a home or refinanced a mortgage. Ask about their lender and whether they would recommend them to you. Personal recommendations can be valuable in finding a reputable and trustworthy lender.

4. Find five and interview them by telephone by allowing them to ask the questions and answer yours.
Compile a list of potential lenders and interview them over the phone. Allow them to ask questions about your needs and provide you with information about their loan options and terms. Be sure to ask questions about their experience, credentials, and fees.

5. Check the BBB for each and check each out with their state's regulatory agency.
After narrowing down your list of potential lenders, research their background on the Better Business Bureau website and check their credentials with their state's regulatory agency. This will help you ensure that they are reputable and have no history of fraudulent activity.

How to Get Into Graphic Design

Graphic design is a creative field that allows you to use your imagination and artistic skills to create visual content for businesses, nonprofits, and individuals. If you’re interested in pursuing a career in graphic design, there are a few steps you can take to get started.

1. Learn how to draw.

Drawing is an essential skill for graphic designers since it forms the foundation of most designs. You don’t need to take a lot of drawing classes to learn how to draw (though that might help). Instead, start by practicing basic shapes like circles, squares, and triangles and work your way up to more complex objects.

2. Get an education.

If you plan on working for yourself, you might think that you don’t need a degree. However, most employers require a degree or some formal training in graphic design. Look for a program that offers courses in design principles, software applications, typography, and color theory.

3. Find your specialty.

Graphic design is a broad field with many subfields within it. Some designers focus on web design, while others specialize in branding or illustration. Finding your niche will help you develop the specific skills and expertise required for your area of focus.

4. Get the right hardware.

Graphic design is a technology-intensive field. You need the right tools to create high-quality designs. Invest in a powerful computer with a high-resolution monitor, a graphics tablet, and a mouse that feels comfortable in your hand.

5. Purchase software.

Graphic design software can make your job easier and allow you to quickly accomplish tasks that would otherwise take much longer. Consider investing in professional software applications like Adobe Photoshop, Illustrator, and InDesign.

6. Download useful tools.

There are many free tools available online that can help you improve your design work. Look for design blogs, forums, and online communities that offer tutorials, templates, and other resources to help you develop your skills.

7. Network with others in your field.

Networking is an essential part of any career, and graphic design is no exception. Attend design conferences, join professional associations, and participate in online communities to meet other designers and learn about job opportunities.

8. Volunteer with nonprofits.

Many local nonprofits require graphic design or web design assistance. Volunteering with these organizations can help you build your portfolio while giving back to your community.

9. Develop an online presence.

There are many venues online where you can exhibit your work. Create a website or portfolio that showcases your best work and make sure to share it on social media and other online platforms.

10. Don’t stop creating.

Even if you aren’t employed in graphic design, you should use your free time to continue exercising your creative talent and developing your abilities. Create designs for fun, experiment with new techniques, and stay up to date with current design trends.

11. Look for work.

Once you’ve developed your skills and built your portfolio, it’s time to start looking for work. Look for job postings online, contact local design firms, or consider freelancing to get your foot in the door.

12. Tailor your resume to each job.

In other words, if the company is looking for a graphic designer with a specific skill set or specific bunch of experiences, you should be sure to list those experiences and skills which the company seems to be particularly interested in.

13. Write a cover letter.

Your cover letter should give more depth to the info on the resume. Use it to highlight your unique skills and experiences and explain why you’re the best candidate for the job.

14. Apply for jobs.

Once you have your resume and cover letter ready, start applying for jobs. Make sure you follow the instructions in the job posting carefully and submit your materials on time.

15. Land a job.
