Becoming a bid manager requires a unique combination of skills and expertise, especially if you want to work in the construction or engineering industry. Bid managers are responsible for preparing, submitting, and winning bids for contracts or projects. In this wikihow article, we will discuss the steps you can take to become a successful bid manager.

1. Obtain an Engineering Degree

While it is not mandatory to have a degree to become a bid manager, it is advisable to have a background in engineering, especially if you want to work in the construction industry. An engineering degree will provide you with the necessary technical skills and knowledge to understand the complexities of the projects that you will be bidding on.

2. Obtain a Business Degree

Alternatively, you can opt for a business degree if you want to focus on the business aspects of bidding, such as financial analysis and risk assessment. A business degree will provide you with a sound understanding of business principles and practices that you can apply to your bid management career.

3. Obtain a Writing-Intensive Degree

Bid managers need to have excellent writing skills, given that they need to prepare proposals and reports. Consider obtaining a degree in a writing-intensive field, such as journalism, communications, or English. This degree will provide you with the writing skills needed to excel in the bid management field.

4. Obtain Significant Experience in the Industry in Which You Want to Manage Bids

Bid managers need to have an excellent understanding of the industry in which they are bidding. Consider working as a consultant or project manager in the industry to gain an in-depth knowledge of the industry practices, regulations, and trends. This experience will help you to understand the specific requirements of the projects you are bidding on and to develop winning strategies.

5. Work as an Estimator

An estimator is an industry expert who provides cost estimates for specific jobs or materials. Working as an estimator will give you an understanding of the costing and pricing aspects of the industry, which is crucial in developing winning bids.

6. Work as a Project Manager

Working as a project manager will give you the opportunity to manage the execution of specific projects in the industry. This experience will provide you with strong project management skills, which are useful when planning and initiating bids.

7. Develop Strong Communication Skills

As a bid manager, you will need to communicate effectively with stakeholders, clients, and team members. Developing strong communication skills will help you to present your ideas clearly and persuasively, which is essential in winning bids.

8. Learn Time Management Skills

Bid managers need to submit bids within a specific time frame and manage multiple bids simultaneously. Learning time management skills will help you to prioritize your tasks, meet deadlines, and deliver quality bids.

9. Be a People Person

Bid managers need to collaborate with various stakeholders, including project managers, engineers, estimators, and clients. Being a people person means that you can work effectively with different personalities and communicate clearly with stakeholders.

10. Stay Cool Under Pressure

Bidding can be a stressful process, given the tight deadlines and the high stakes involved. Staying cool under pressure means that you can manage stress effectively and deliver quality bids despite the pressure.

11. Develop an Eye for Detail

Submitting winning bids requires attention to detail, especially in the proposal and report preparation processes. Developing an eye for detail means that you can spot errors, inconsistencies, and omissions that may affect the quality of your bid.

In conclusion, becoming a bid manager requires a commitment to learning, developing your skills, and gaining experience in the industry. By following the steps outlined above, you will be on your way to becoming a successful bid manager.

If you're a parent, disciplining your child can be a challenging task. You want your child to behave appropriately, but you don't want to emotionally or physically harm them. Spanking can be a last resort method used to discipline a child, but it should only be done when necessary. Here's how to use spanking as a last resort:

1. Decide ahead of time what behaviors are serious enough to spank for.
As a parent, you should make a list of behaviors that are serious and should be deserving of a spanking if necessary. These negative behaviors should be communicated to the child, so they understand what actions could lead to physical discipline.

2. Sit down and talk with your child.
Before an issue arises, it's crucial to sit down and talk with your child about expectations and appropriate behaviors. Communicate with your child in a positive way, explaining the benefits of good behavior, and how this can create a happier and more peaceful home.

3. When the child misbehaves and/or commits one of the behaviors that you deemed serious enough, put the child in time-out.
When your child commits a behavior that is on your spanking list, put them in time-out. Time-out should be a milder form of punishment and should give the child time to reflect on their behavior.

4. Once you are calm, think about the best consequence for the offense.
Take time to think about the offense once you have calmed down. As a parent, you should always approach disciplining your child with a clear mindset.

5. If you decide to not spank the child, have a discussion with the child about the misbehavior and then announce what the consequence will be.
If spanking isn't necessary, discuss the issue with your child and provide them with an alternative consequence. This shows the child you are still willing to administer consequences for their actions, but, based on the offense, spanking wasn't necessary.

6. If you decide a spanking is necessary, have a discussion with the child about the misbehavior and then announce that the consequence will be a spanking.
If spanking is the consequence, you still need to discuss the misbehavior with the child, so they understand why it's necessary.

7. Pull down the child's pants and underwear.
Before spanking, make sure the child's pants and underwear are pulled down.

8. Bend your child over your knee.
Bending the child over your knee puts them in a vulnerable position, which is a crucial part of the discipline.

9. Relax your hand and all your limbs, with one firm hand on their back and one on their bottom.
You need to be relaxed before spanking your child. A slap administered in anger can hurt your child and create an emotional rift.

10. Begin spanking.
Start administering the spanking with the desired force to ensure your child feels the consequences of their actions.

11. If the child is squirming and struggling during the spanking, apply more pressure with your hand on the child's back to help hold them down.
Your child may squirm or struggle during their spanking. In this case, put more pressure on their back to stop moving, so you can administer the consequences appropriately.

12. Know when to stop.
Once you've determined the spankings are enough to discipline the child, stop immediately, and console your child. Spanking should not cause physical or emotional harm.

13. After the spanking, comfort and reassure the child that the spanking is over and that you still love them more than they could possibly imagine.
Reassure your child that you still love them very much, and the spanking only exists to ensure their positive behavior.

14. After they calm down, have a brief talk with them.
Ask your child if they understand why they were spanked, and address what they could have done differently to avoid this punishment.

15. Hug the child more, and give them another kiss.
End your discipline with a hug and a kiss so your child feels loved and support. It helps them to know that your discipline is not born of anger, but instead love. 

Following these steps can help ensure that discipline is not done in anger, and spanking becomes a last resort method of disciplining your child. Always keep in mind that a gentle and loving approach towards discipline ensures your child feels safe and supported while also learning the consequences of their actions.

Sky lanterns are a popular way to create an enchanting ambiance during celebrations or events. While it may seem daunting to make one from scratch at home, it can actually be a fun and easy DIY project. Here is how you can make your own sky lanterns.

Materials:
- Lightweight, non-flammable fabric cut into a square of approximately 36" x 36" (90cm x 90cm)
- Florist's wire, cut into two 24" (60cm) pieces
- Candle wax
- Aluminum foil, cut into a strip of 3" x 1" (7.5cm x 2.5cm)
- Bamboo skewers, cut into halves
- Non-flammable tape
- Kitchen paper towel or tissue paper cut into 4" x 4" (10cm x 10cm) pieces
- Fireproofing spray
- Brown craft paper
- Non-flammable glue
- Paper bag

Instructions:

1. Start by tying the fabric into a tight knot.

2. Center the two 24" (60cm) pieces of florist's wire over the knot.

3. Wrap the wire around the knot, and twist them tightly to make them secure.

4. Place the candle over a lighter or other open flame until the wax melts down into a liquid state.

5. Place the knot into the hot, melted wax and let it soak for three to five minutes.

6. Remove the newly created wick from the wax.

7. Wrap the aluminum-foil strip around the knot in the center of the wick.

8. Cut three bamboo skewers in half lengthwise using either a razor blade or a utility knife.

9. Line the split bamboo up end to end on a table to make a single long strip.

10. Secure the overlapping connection points together with non-flammable tape.

11. Tape the ends of the foil-wrapped wires that protrude from the wick to opposite sides of the bamboo frame.

12. Hang 16-20 pieces of kitchen paper towel (or about half that of tissue paper) on a clothesline using clothespins (pegs). Place a plastic or canvas drop cloth under the paper to catch any drippings.

13. Spray both sides of each piece of paper thoroughly with the fireproofing spray.

14. Draw a vertical line 40" (about 1 meter) long down the center of the brown craft paper.

15. Draw a horizontal line 12" (30cm) long at the base of the vertical line.

16. Draw a second horizontal line that is 22" (1/2 meter) long approximately two thirds of the way up the vertical line.

17. Connect the two horizontal lines by sketching a line that curves gently inward before meeting the vertical line.

18. Draw a second line mirroring the line that you just drew to connect the left tips of the two horizontal lines.

19. Sketch mirroring lines that connect each end of the upper horizontal line to the top of the vertical line.

20. Cut the shape that you've drawn out of the brown craft paper using scissors.

21. Lay the 16-20 fireproofed paper pieces on a flat surface.

22. Use a non-flammable glue to seal the overlapped ends of the papers together.

23. Lay one 2-piece panel of paper towel/tissue paper over the brown craft paper pattern.

24. Repeat this step with the remaining 2-piece paper panels.

25. Connect the pointed tips of the paper towel/tissue paper panels together.

26. Attach the opening of the paper bag to the bamboo frame.

27. Fold the end of the paper bag upward to cover the frame.

28. Take your lantern outside at night or at dusk.

Enjoy the unique and mesmerizing glow of your handmade sky lanterns as they drift up into the sky. Remember to take proper safety precautions and check local regulations before launching your sky lanterns.

Laying tile on concrete can be a great way to spruce up an old floor or add a decorative touch to a new one. However, careful preparation and attention to detail are required to ensure that the job is done correctly. In this article, we will guide you through the process of laying tile on concrete, from cleaning the surface to sealing the finished product.

Part 1: Preparing the Concrete

1. Clean the surface of the concrete with a vacuum. Before starting to lay the tile, it is essential to ensure that the concrete surface is clean and free of any debris. Use a vacuum cleaner to remove any dirt, dust, or other loose particles.

2. Check the levels on the floor to determine if the concrete is level. Use a long straight edge to check for any high or low spots in the concrete surface. If you find any, you will need to use a self-leveling underlayment to even them out.

3. Roll or brush a latex primer onto the surface of the concrete. This helps the thinset mortar to bond to the concrete surface better. Follow the manufacturer's instructions for application and drying time.

4. Mix the self-leveling underlayment in a bucket or purchase it pre-mixed. Pour the mixture onto the low spots in the concrete and use a trowel to spread it evenly. Watch where the leveling compound stops flowing to ensure that you have filled all the low spots.

5. Purchase an anti-fracture membrane to lay over your leveled concrete. This helps to prevent any cracks in the concrete from transferring to the tile surface. Follow the manufacturer's instructions for application.

Part 2: Laying the Tile

1. Snap center lines through the length and width of the room with a chalk line. This will help you to keep the tile straight and centered.

2. Unpack all your tile to check for damage and color mismatches. It is essential to make sure that all the tile is in good condition before starting to lay it.

3. Lay out the tile on the surface of the floor. This will help you to determine the best placement and avoid any awkward cuts or alignment issues.

4. View the edges of the tile. If the tiles near one edge are less than one-half tiles, you will need to adjust your center lines accordingly.

5. Cut your tiles near the edge of the room. Use a tile cutter to make precise cuts for a professional finish.

6. Check that your newly cut tile fits back into your layout before you start to lay the tile. This will ensure that your cuts are accurate and the tile placement is correct.

7. Remove the tile in the quarter of the room farthest away from the door. This will allow you to start laying the tile and work your way out of the room.

8. Mix your thinset mortar. Follow the manufacturer's instructions carefully to ensure the correct consistency.

9. Spread a three by three foot area with thinset. Use a notched trowel to apply an even layer over the surface of the concrete.

10. Comb the thinset using your notched trowel. This helps to create a grooved surface for the tile to adhere to.

11. Set your first tile against the corner of the center line. Place one-fourth inch (0.6cm) tile spacers between the tiles if you want even, thick grout lines.

12. Place the ceramic tiles down in your three by three grid. Work your way out of the room, carefully pressing the tiles into the thinset.

13. Move across the floor in a three foot by three foot area, working in one quarter of the room at a time. Repeat steps 9-12 until all the tile has been laid.

14. Allow the thinset to set for at least 24 hours before grouting. This gives it enough time to dry and set firmly.

Part 3: Finishing the Job

1. Mix your grout with cool water. Follow the manufacturer's instructions carefully to ensure the correct consistency.

2. Lift grout out of the bucket with a grout float. Use the float to press the grout into the spaces between the tiles.

3. Leave the grout to set for 20 minutes. Use a damp sponge to wipe away any excess grout from the surface of the tile.

4. Allow the grout to set for two hours. Use a dry cloth to buff away any remaining grout haze.

5. Seal the grout. This helps to protect it from dirt, stains, and discoloration. Follow the manufacturer's instructions for application and drying time.

Congratulations! You have successfully laid tile on concrete. With proper preparation and attention to detail, you can achieve a beautiful and long-lasting finish that will add value to your home.

Do you love Sonic the Hedgehog and want to learn how to draw him? Drawing Sonic is fairly easy, and this wikiHow article will walk you through the steps!

Method 1: Basic Sonic

1. Draw a medium-sized circle.
Begin by drawing a medium-sized circle in the middle of your page. This will be Sonic's head.

2. Underneath the head, draw an oval for his torso.
Draw an oval shape or two overlapping circles below the circle for his head. The bottom part will be his snout.

3. Start with the top circle.
Draw an oval above the head circle. This will help you get the shape of his head.

4. Draw 2 upside down v's on the head.
Draw 2 upside down v's in the oval you just made. It will help you draw his ears.

5. With the ears, add two bigger v's on top to complete the ears.
Finish Sonic's ears with two bigger upside-down v's. These should be on top of the other v's you just drew.

6. For the eyes (and part of the muzzle), draw a butterfly shape.
Draw a butterfly shape with the top part being almost connected to the top part of the circle we drew for his head.

7. With the butterfly shape, join it to the head.
Line the butterfly shape up along the head circle to remove any visible gaps. Then add detail to the face.

8. Move onto the body.
Now we will draw Sonic's body by connecting his chest and head.

9. Draw the arms like you were drawing a couple of bread sticks.
Add Sonic's arms. They should look like thin breadsticks on either side of his body.

10. For the hands, make the gloves look like doughnuts.
Draw Sonic's hands by making round shapes that look like doughnuts.

11. Now it's time for the legs.
Draw Sonic's legs similar to his arms, just a bit thicker and longer.

12. Add detail to the sticks to make them look like his legs.
Add spikes to Sonic's legs and make them look like his signature look.

13. Do the same doughnuts wrapped around his ankles for the socks.
To draw Sonic's socks, make circles that look like doughnuts – one around each ankle.

14. Draw some triangles for shoes.
His shoes should be pointy, so add pointed triangles at the bottom of each leg.

15. Add detail to the shoes.
Add some detail onto the shoes to show some texture.

16. Add detail to rest of the drawing.
Add spikes to Sonic's back and add curves to his limbs to show motion.

17. Erase extra lines.
Carefully erase any extra lines that you don't need anymore.

18. Go over lines using a black felt-tip marker.
Use a black felt-tip marker to go over all the pencil lines you drew in the previous steps.

19. Add color!
Finally, add the colors that make Sonic unique. Blue body, red shoes, white gloves – you get the idea.

Method 2: Sonic Running in a Circle

1. Draw a circle.
Draw a large circle in the center of the paper.

2. Merge the circle and the spiky shape together.
Draw Sonic's spiky hair design around the top of the circle. Merge the two shapes together.

3. Draw the shape of his body.
Draw the shape of Sonic's torso and legs.

4. Outline his hands and shoes.
Add Sonic's gloves and his trademark red shoes.

5. Add details.
Add details like spikes and any other marks you see from a Sonic picture.

6. Continue adding details.
Add more details like Sonic's eyes, nose and other characteristics.

7. Sketch circles behind Sonic to serve as a background.
Add some overlapping and slightly different sized circles behind Sonic.

8. Outline the background circles.
Make the circles darker on the outer edges and lighter towards the middle of the circle.

9. Color your artwork.
Finally, color in your drawing the way you like it!

Now that you've learned how to draw Sonic like a pro, see if you can draw some of his friends like Tails or Knuckles. Keep practicing and soon you'll have a whole Sonic universe drawn by you!

2. Use the smallest workable ratchet, breakover wrench, and/or cheater leverage extension correctly - It's important not to over tighten (over-torque) bolts; otherwise, you may break off a bolt or screw. 3. Avoid engine damage - The timing belt is an integral component of your engine, and if it breaks, it can cause major damage and potentially ruin your engine. To avoid engine damage, it is important to change the timing belt, timing belt tensioner, and its idler pulley.

Basketball is a dynamic sport that requires both physical and mental skills. One of the mental skills required is the ability to apply math and geometry in basketball. Understanding the geometry involved in basketball can help improve your game, especially when it comes to shooting, rebounding, and defense. In this article, we will discuss some ways to apply math and geometry to basketball.

1. Get to know the court's geometry: You have to know all the measures from where you play, so you can have a better spatial notion.

Before you can apply math and geometry to basketball, you need to have a basic understanding of the court's geometry. The basketball court measures 28 meters long and 15 meters wide. How to Dye Hair With Jell-O

If you're looking for a fun and easy way to dye your hair, why not give Jell-O a try? With a few simple supplies and some basic instructions, you can transform your hair into a colorful work of art. Just follow these steps to learn how.

Part 1: Consider Bleaching Your Hair

1. Gather your supplies. Before you begin dyeing your hair with Jell-O, you'll need to gather a few supplies. Here's what you'll need:

- A packet of Jell-O in your desired color
- Hair conditioner
- Petroleum jelly
- An old towel
- Gloves

2. Know what to expect. Dyeing your hair with Jell-O can be messy and time-consuming, but it's also a lot of fun. Keep in mind that the color may not be as vibrant as other hair dyes, and it may fade more quickly as well.

3. Consider bleaching your hair if it is very dark. Jell-O works best on light-colored hair, so if you have very dark hair, you may need to bleach it first. This will help the color show up more vividly.

4. Use your fingers to apply some petroleum jelly around your forehead, neck, and ears. This will help protect your skin from getting stained by the dye.

5. Drape an old towel over your shoulders like a cape. This will help catch any stray drips of Jell-O dye.

6. Put some gloves on your hands so that they don't get stained. Jell-O can be very messy, so it's important to protect your hands from getting dyed as well.

Part 2: Bleaching Your Hair

1. Deep-condition your hair three days before you bleach it. This will help strengthen your hair and reduce any damage that may be caused by the bleach.

2. Don't wash your hair just before you bleach your hair. This will help protect your scalp from getting irritated by the bleach.

3. Consider performing a strand test first. This will help you determine how your hair will react to the bleach.

4. Put on the gloves and drape the towel across your shoulder. This will protect your skin and clothing from getting stained by the bleach.

5. Prepare the bleach according to the instructions on the package. Be sure to mix it well before applying it to your hair.

6. Divide your hair into four parts to make it easier to work. This will help ensure that you cover all of your hair with the bleach.

7. Start bleaching your hair from the back of your head and move your way up towards the top. This will help ensure that you cover all of your hair evenly.

8. Wait 30 minutes, or however long the manufacturer recommends. Be sure to check your hair periodically to ensure that it's not getting too light.

9. Rinse the bleach out and follow up with shampoo and conditioner. This will help remove any excess bleach and protect your hair from damage.

10. Dry your hair with a towel. Be sure to press the towel gently against your hair, rather than rubbing it, to avoid causing damage.

Part 3: Dyeing Your Hair With Jell-O

1. Divide your hair into four sections to make it more manageable. This will help prevent tangles and ensure that you cover all of your hair with the dye.

2. Undo the bottom left section and apply the dye to it. Use your fingers to work the dye into your hair, making sure to cover all of the strands evenly.

3. Roll the dyed section into a bun and secure it with a hair tie or clip. This will help prevent the dye from getting on your skin or clothing.

4. Repeat the process for the other three sections. Be sure to apply the dye evenly and cover all of the strands.

5. Put a shower cap over your head. This will help keep the dye from dripping onto your skin or clothing.

6. Leave the shower cap on for at least one hour. This will give the dye time to fully saturate your hair.

7. Rinse your hair using lukewarm water after the time is up. Be sure to rinse thoroughly to remove all of the dye.

8. Dry your hair. Be sure to use a soft towel and gently press it against your hair to avoid causing damage.

- Method 1: Twist and Foil
Divide your hair into four sections and apply the dye to each strand. Twist each strand into a rope and wrap a piece of tin foil around it. Wait at least one hour before rinsing your hair.

- Method 2: Foil Only
Apply the dye to each strand and wrap a sheet of tin foil around it. Leave the foil and dye in your hair for at least one hour before rinsing.

Divide your hair into four sections and apply the dye to each strand. Wrap a sheet of tin foil around each strand and leave it in your hair for at least one hour before rinsing.

In conclusion, dyeing your hair with Jell-O is a fun and unique way to add some color to your look. If none of the above fixes the problem, turn off the water to the toilet.

After the water is off, flush the toilet to empty the tank.

Taking care of your book is essential in maintaining its condition and ensuring that it lasts for many years. Whether you've just bought a new book or borrowed one from the library, there are steps you can take to protect it from wear and tear. Here's how to take care of your book:

1. Hold your book properly: When holding your book, make sure you hold it from the side you open the book, not from the side you hold while reading. This will prevent the spine from getting damaged.

2. Open your book gently: Avoid opening your book more than 100 geometrical degrees. Forcefully opening the book can cause the spine to weaken and eventually break.

3. Don't use a highlighter or any kind of pen for bookmarking: Highlighting or writing in your book can damage the pages and reduce its value.

4. Eat or drink after reading your book: Food stains and spills can damage your book and make it difficult to read.

5. Don't give your book away: Your book is your book. Don't give it to someone who simply asks to borrow it. Only lend your book to someone you trust to take care of it.

6. Store your book horizontally: To keep your book in its best shape, store it on a horizontal surface like a shelf or table. This ensures that the weight is evenly distributed and doesn't put pressure on the spine.

7. Dust your book regularly: Open your book and gently dust it every month, or every two months if you're feeling lazy. Dust can accumulate on the pages and make it difficult to read.

8. Keep your book in a dry place: Make sure your book isn't exposed to a humid environment, which can damage the pages and weaken the binding.

9. Read your book in a safe location: If you're reading your book outside of your house, sit down and read instead of walking around. This prevents you from dropping or damaging the book.

10. Always place your book back where you found it: When you're finished reading, make sure you place your book back on the shelf where you found it. Don't leave it on a table or any other surface.

11. Avoid photocopy points and black drops: If you notice any of these on the page, they will permanently stay on the page, so be extra careful when handling your book.

By following these simple steps, you can take care of your book and ensure that it stays in great condition for years to come. Enjoy your forever new book!

How to Supercharge Business Meetings Using "Note and Vote" 

Business meetings are a necessary aspect of any organization. However, many meetings can be ineffective and a waste of precious time. Do not let your business meetings fall into the trap of becoming boring and unproductive. To supercharge your business meetings, consider using the "Note and Vote" method. This method allows for creative and democratic decision-making, resulting in effective business meetings and a more engaged team. Here's how to use "Note and Vote" during your next business meeting: 

1. Pick the organizer/facilitator for the proceedings.

Before the meeting, assign an organizer/facilitator to ensure the meeting runs smoothly and stays on track. The organizer should be responsible for leading the group through the "Note and Vote" process and ensuring that everyone participates.

2. Set the meeting place and time.

Select an appropriate meeting place and time. Ideally, this should be a space where everyone can focus without any distractions.

3. Gather the supplies.

Gather the necessary supplies for the meeting. This may include pens, paper, whiteboards, and markers. You may also want to have a laptop or tablet available to record any important information.

4. Select a decider by chance.

To ensure fairness, select a decider (the person who makes the final decision) by chance. For example, you could pull a name out of a hat or use a random number generator.

5. Set the stage for gathering individual thoughts.

Provide a set amount of time for everyone to gather their initial thoughts. During this time, everyone should write down their ideas and thoughts on the given topic.

6. Lay out the plan.

Explain the "Note and Vote" method to the group.

7. Reveal the objective (or restate it).

Restate the objective of the meeting. Ensure that everyone understands what needs to be accomplished.

8. State the time allotted for this task.

Set a time limit for the note-taking phase. This typically ranges from 5 to 10 minutes.

9. Filter the preliminary thoughts.

After the allotted time, ask everyone to share their ideas. The goal should be to filter and refine the preliminary thoughts.

10. Share the best ideas.

Identify the best ideas from the preliminary thoughts. This can be done using a whiteboard to write down the top ideas.

11. Number the choices on the whiteboard.

Once the best ideas are identified, number them on the whiteboard.

12. Vote individually on the favorites.

Provide a set amount of time for everyone to vote on their favorite ideas. 

13. Announce the votes.

Collate the votes and announce the top choices.

14. Accept the outcome decided upon.

Accept the outcome as decided by the group.

15. Shape the process appropriately.

Tweak the process as needed for future business meetings.

16. Allow multiple votes.

If the decider is not satisfied with the winning idea, allow for a revote. 

17. Realize the benefits of silence/isolation while noting.

Silence and isolation while noting often lead to better ideas and more thoughtful discussion.

18. Acknowledge the value of dumping linear decision-making.

The "Note and Vote" method allows for a more democratic and creative decision-making process, rather than the usual top-down approach.

19. Revel in the power of parallel processing.

By coming up with multiple ideas at once, parallel processing helps to ensure a thorough and well-rounded decision.

20. Realize that independent notes short-circuit "groupthink."

By taking notes independently, groupthink is avoided, leading to more diverse and innovative ideas.

21. Recognize the beauty of the blind vote.

A blind vote helps to ensure impartiality during the decision-making process.

22. Value the insight gained during pitching.

Hearing other perspectives during the pitching phase allows for open discussion and collaboration.

23. Understand the power of alone time.

Providing time for individuals to gather their own thoughts can lead to better for more developed ideas.

24. Realize that the strongest choices often come from an individual charged with a responsibility—in this case, the decider.

Trusting your assigned decider is key in ensuring that the final decision is made with the organization's best interests in mind. 

Using the "Note and Vote" method can supercharge your business meetings and lead to better collaboration, creativity, and effective decision-making. Give it a try at your next meeting!

Changing the timing belt on a 2.0L, 4 cylinder Mazda 626 from 1993 to 2002 may seem like a daunting task, but with the proper tools and instructions, it can easily be accomplished. Below is a step-by-step guide on how to successfully change the timing belt on your Mazda 626.

Readying to Remove the Timing Belt

Before beginning the process, make sure the engine is cool and the car’s battery is disconnected. It’s important to start with a flat car and a reliable workspace. Also, ensure that you have the necessary tools such as an Allen “el-shaped” hex tool and a 14mm socket.

1. First, locate the timing belt-tensioner pulley. Turn the timing belt-tensioner pulley toward “counter-clockwise” with an Allen “el-shaped” hex tool that fits in a hole in the pulley. Rotating it will allow you to slip the belt off, little by little.

2. Pivot the timing belt tensioner pulley toward “clockwise” with the Allen hex wrench. This step takes the tension off of the timing belt tensioner spring. Once the tension is off, remove the spring with very long-nose-pliers.

3. Remove the tensioner pulley by its one bolt in the middle. The bolt size for this is typically 14mm.

4. Remove the “idler” pulley of the timing belt system by one bolt in the middle. This bolt size is typically 14mm as well.

5. The next step is to remove the 4 or 5 water pump bolts. These bolts can be hard to see, so use a 12mm socket and a medium size ratchet (called 3/8 inch drive in the USA).

6. After removing the water pump bolts, carefully clean the engine block surface where the water pump gasket will make contact. This is important to ensure sealing well. To do this, carefully scrape off any pieces of stuck-on old gasket material corrosion, rust, or dirt to bare metal but not gouging or roughing the metal.

7. Then, put on the “new water pump” and follow the instructions that came with it.

8. Install the “new timing tensioner” pulley and tighten its mounting bolt securely.

9. Install the new “idler pulley” and tighten the mounting bolt securely.

Installing the New Timing Belt

10. Put on the “new timing belt” and follow the instructions that came with it.

11. Press the timing belt onto place while keeping the tensioner pulley out of the way enough, using the Allen hex wrench toward counterclockwise for the pulley to be as far backed off as possible to allow the belt to slide onto the sprockets.

12. With the Allen wrench in the hole in the tensioner pulley for that purpose, press it toward clockwise against the belt and press it in for a little tightening of the belt. Then, release it slowly for the spring to bring it back into position.

13. Finally, remove the “stopper block” from the cams before you put on the top half-cover on the timing belt area.

In conclusion, changing the timing belt on a 2.0L, 4-cylinder Mazda 626 from 1993 to 2002 can be a relatively easy process with the right instructions. Following the above step-by-step guide will help ensure a successful replacement of your timing belt. Remember to take your time and have all the necessary tools on hand before beginning.

Teamwork is a crucial element in the success of any business, but it can be challenging to evaluate. This article will guide you through the steps necessary to evaluate teamwork in a business.

Part 1: Starting with the basics

Before diving into the evaluation of teamwork in a business, it is essential to have a clear understanding of the basics. This includes knowing the objectives and goals of the business, understanding the team structure, and identifying the roles team members play.

Part 2: Keep a confidential checklist of your considerations of changes

At this stage, it is important to keep a confidential checklist of considerations for changes that might improve processes. This checklist could include ways to implement better technologies, strategies to enhance employee engagement, and more. This step is crucial as it helps to identify areas that require improvement.

Part 3: Talk to team members

It is essential to communicate with team members about their feelings, concerns, goals, and ambitions. This can be done in two stages; as a group and then individually. This communication will help you to identify any obstacles team members are facing in their roles.

Part 4: Identify any "underground" problems

Sometimes, team members might not feel comfortable discussing issues that bother them. As an evaluator, it is essential to identify any "underground" problems that might not have been expressed openly and address them accordingly.

Part 5: Listen carefully

When team members are sharing their opinions or concerns, ensure that you listen carefully. Active listening will help you gain a better understanding of their feelings and concerns.

Part 6: Identify challenges

Some employees might be experiencing challenges that need to be addressed. Identifying these challenges will help you to create solutions that will assist them in their roles.

Part 7: Take a regular opportunity to check existing procedures and systems

It is crucial to check whether existing procedures and systems are being used to monitor their effectiveness and identify areas that require improvement.

Part 8: Invest in improving the layout of the building and equipment

An appropriate working environment is essential to teamwork. Investing in improving the layout of the building and equipment can help set the tone for a positive working environment.

Part 9: Install a system for staff members to make fair suggestions or comments

Creating a system for staff members to provide their suggestions or comments will help identify areas that require attention and will help promote teamwork.

Part 10: Consult, consult, consult

It is essential to consult with team members, fellow evaluators, and other stakeholders regarding decisions that might affect teamwork.

Part 11: Compare with your original expectations

After evaluating the teamwork in the business, it is necessary to compare the findings with the initial goals and expectations.

Part 12: Make changes as required and continue to monitor

Based on the findings, make necessary changes, and continue to monitor the progress of the business to improve teamwork.

In conclusion, evaluating teamwork in a business is crucial in enhancing productivity and achieving business objectives. By following the steps outlined in this article, evaluators can identify areas that require improvement, create solutions, and enhance teamwork.

How to Choose an Allowance for Your Child

Giving your child an allowance can be a great way to teach them financial responsibility. However, it can be tricky to decide on the right amount and frequency. Here are some tips for choosing the best allowance for your child.

Part 1: Choose when to begin giving your child an allowance

1. Consider your child’s age. There is no one right age to start giving your child an allowance, but it’s generally recommended to start around age five or six.

2. Think about your child’s maturity level. Your child should be able to understand the concept of money, and be responsible enough to take care of it.

3. Decide on your reasons for giving an allowance. Do you want to teach responsibility? Reward good behavior? Give your child some spending money?

4. Determine what your family budget can handle. Be realistic about how much money you can afford to give your child.

Part 2: Decide how much to give

1. Consider your child’s age and needs. A younger child may need less money than an older child who might want to buy more expensive items.

2. Think about what you expect your child to use the money for. Will they need to buy birthday gifts for friends? Pay for snacks after school?

3. Consider tying the allowance to chores or school performance (more on this later).

Part 3: Set a schedule for the allowance

1. Determine how often you will give the allowance. Some parents choose to give a weekly amount, while others prefer bi-weekly or monthly.

2. Make sure the schedule works with your own finances. If you get paid bi-weekly, for example, it may make sense to give your child an allowance on that schedule as well.

Part 4: Open a bank account for your child

1. Once you start giving your child an allowance, you can also help him or her open a bank account as a place to keep some of the money.

2. This can be a great way to teach your child about saving and budgeting.

Part 5: Decide if you want to have the allowance be dependent upon chores

1. Some parents think it is important to give a child an allowance only on the condition that chores like making the bed, cleaning the dinner table, taking out the trash, etc. are completed.

2. This can teach your child about the connection between work and earning money.

Part 6: Consider tying an allowance to school performance

1. The considerations for this approach are very similar to those you must weigh when deciding whether or not to relate your child’s allowance and responsibility for chores.

2. You might choose to give your child a bonus for good grades, or withhold some of the allowance for poor performance.

Part 7: Set guidelines for how the allowance can be used

1. To teach your child the value of money, you will want to monitor how he or she spends the allowance, but don’t dictate the spending.

2. Instead, set guidelines for what is acceptable spending and what is not (e.g. no purchasing violent video games).

Part 8: Let your child make mistakes

1. You may be tempted to give your two cents on everything your child wants to spend the allowance on.

2. But part of learning about money is making mistakes and learning from them. If your child wants to blow all their money on candy, let them—just make sure they understand the consequences.

Part 9: Evaluate the allowance periodically

1. Every so often, consider the amount of the allowance you provide against your child’s age, needs, and level of responsibility.

2. You may need to adjust the allowance as your child grows and their needs change.

Part 10: Explain if you need to lower your child’s allowance

1. If you are unable to raise an allowance, or must reduce it due to a financial hardship or your own budgeting needs, take the time to talk about this with your child.

2. Be honest about why you need to make changes, and how your child can adjust their own spending to accommodate the new allowance.

Part 11: Create an allowance contract

1. When your child is old enough, consider drafting an allowance contract—a simple document that explains the terms of the allowance.

2. This can include things like how much money will be given, what the allowance is dependent on, and what the consequences are for not meeting expectations.

Overall, giving your child an allowance can be a great tool for teaching responsibility and financial literacy. With a little thought and planning, you can create an allowance that works for both you and your child.

How to Splint a Finger

When you injure your finger, it's important to determine the severity of the damage before attempting to splint it. Seek medical attention right away if bones in your finger are visible or protruding from the injured area. Similarly, if your finger is numb or tingles, you should see a doctor as soon as possible. And if the injured finger appears deformed, let your doctor apply a splint. However, if your finger is swollen and stiff with no deformity, you can treat the injury at home. Here are some tips on how to apply a splint to your finger:

Method 1: Cardboard Splint

1. Clean the wounded area before you splint it. Use soap and water to wash the area gently, making sure to clean around the wound.

2. Look for two straight, firm objects such as two big paper clips, two popsicle sticks, or two long firm pieces of cardboard.

3. Measure the length of your finger to determine the size of the cardboard splint.

4. Cut the cardboard based on the length of your finger. The width of the splint should be about two inches.

5. Gather your materials. You'll need the cardboard splint, medical tape, and a pair of scissors.

6. Apply the splint. Place the splint under your injured finger, with one end near the base and the other near the tip. Use the tape to secure the splint to your finger.

7. Ensure the splint is snug on your finger. The splint should keep your finger immobilized but not so tight that it cuts off your circulation.

8. Use the finger beside your injured finger as an immobilizer. Rest the injured finger against the finger next to it to prevent any movement.

9. Measure your injured finger. Place the cardboard splint next to your injured finger and mark the area where the bend in your finger occurs.

Method 2: Commercial Splint

1. Purchase a commercial splint at a medical supply store or online.

2. Prepare your materials. You'll need the commercial splint, medical tape, and a pair of scissors.

3. Support the injured finger with your other hand and straighten it carefully.

4. Secure the finger to the splint by taping around the base of the finger.

5. Pinch the nail of the injured finger for three seconds. This can help to reduce any pain and swelling.

6. Avoid getting the splinted finger wet. Keep the splint dry to prevent infection and to ensure that the splint remains in place.

Note: If your finger does not improve within a few days, or if you experience severe pain, numbness, or tingling, seek medical attention immediately.

Constructing an inexpensive shelter can be a useful skill to have in many situations. Whether you're looking for a temporary shelter for camping, a place to store equipment, or a workshop for your DIY projects, building your own shelter can be both rewarding and cost-effective. In this article, we'll walk you through the process of building an inexpensive shelter using two parallel four-foot fences that are thirty feet long. 

Materials Required:

- Four 4”x4”x8’ pressure-treated posts
- Sixteen 2”x4”x10’ pressure-treated lumber
- Two 4’x8’ exterior plywood panels 
- Outdoor primer and paint 
- Three 60-pound bags of concrete 
- Water 
- Eight 24” pieces of fence top rail 
- Four 118” pieces of fence top rail 
- Two end midway connectors 
- One peak connector 
- Outdoor cover with grommets 
- Bungee balls 
- 30’ ropes 

Step 1: Build Two Parallel Four-Foot Fences, Thirty Feet Long.

Begin by building two parallel four-foot fences that are thirty feet long. Dig four holes spaced thirty feet apart and roughly three feet deep. Place a 4”x4”x8’ pressure-treated post in each hole and fill with concrete, making sure the posts are level. 

Step 2: Find the Four End Posts that Will Create the Imaginary Rectangle.

Next, find the four end posts that will create the imaginary rectangle, and mark them accordingly. 

Step 3: Brace the Posts When the Positions are Correct and the Posts are Plumb.

Once you have your end posts in place, brace them when the positions are correct and the posts are plumb. 

Step 4: Using a Wheelbarrow, Mix Three Sixty Pound Bags of Concrete and Water Until You Have a Wet (but Not Watery) Batch of Concrete.

Using a wheelbarrow, mix three sixty-pound bags of concrete and water until you have a wet (but not watery) batch of concrete. Pour the concrete into each hole, filling it three-quarters of the way up. 

Step 5: Find the Post with the Highest Ground Elevation, and Measure from the Ground 4' Up the Post.

Find the post with the highest ground elevation, and measure from the ground 4' up the post. This will be the height of your fence. 

Step 6: Using Your 10' Pressure-Treated 2”x4”s, Cut Them to the Exact Length Between Each Post.

Using your 10' pressure-treated 2”x4”s, cut them to the exact length between each post. This will be the length of your fence. 

Step 7: Place Intermediate 2”x4” Members on 8' Centers from One End Post, So That They Are Able to Accept the 4'x8' Plywood Panels.

Place intermediate 2”x4” members on 8' centers from one end post. This will allow you to accept 4'x8' plywood panels. 

Step 8: Paint the Outside and Top of the Fence with a Good Outdoor Primer and Paint.

Paint the outside and top of the fence with a good outdoor primer and paint to protect it from the elements. 

Step 9: Cut 8 24” Pieces from One of the Fence Top Rails.

Cut eight 24” pieces from one of the fence top rails. 

Step 10: Drill the Holes with a Drill Press or a Portable Hand Drill.

Drill the holes with a drill press or a portable hand drill. 

Step 11: From the Center of the First Post, Mark Along the Wall Every 10', and Then Mark a Line Using a Framing Square 22” Down the Wall.

From the center of the first post, mark along the wall every 10', and then mark a line using a framing square 22” down the wall. 

Step 12: Secure the Pipe to the Wall Using a 4” Lag Screw and a Thick Washer Between the Pipe and Wall – Do This in Only the Top Hole – Do Not Completely Tighten.

Secure the pipe to the wall using a 4” lag screw and a thick washer between the pipe and wall. Do this in only the top hole and do not completely tighten it at this point. 

Step 13: Once All the Connectors and 118” Top Rail Pipes Have Been Connected, Go Back and Secure the Bottom Lag Screw and Washer and Tighten Both.

Once all the connectors and 118” top rail pipes have been connected, go back and secure the bottom lag screw and washer and tighten both. 

Step 14: Gather Four 56” Top Rail Pipes and Two End Midway Connectors and a Peak Connector.

Gather four 56” top rail pipes and two end midway connectors and a peak connector. 

Step 15: Add a 56” Top Rail Pipe into the Second Wall Connector (1,2).

Add a 56” top rail pipe into the second wall connector (1,2). 

Step 16: Unfold the Cover in a Large Location So That It Can Accommodate the 20'x 30' Size.

Unfold the cover in a large location so that it can accommodate the 20'x 30' size. 

Step 17: Attach 30' Ropes in Three or Four Places Along the Length of the Cover Through the Grommets.

Attach 30' ropes in three or four places along the length of the cover through the grommets. 

Step 18: Pull Each Rope Three or Four Feet, Pulling the Cover over the Framework.

Pull each rope three or four feet, pulling the cover over the framework.
