Playing drum rudiments is essential for improving your drumming skills and overall rhythm. Whether you are a beginner or an experienced drummer, understanding the basic rudiments and mastering the advanced ones can help you take your drumming to the next level. In this article, we will guide you through the steps to learn various drum rudiments, from flams to sextuplets, and everything in between.

Part 1 – Basic Rudiments

1. Get either a drum pad or drum and be comfortable holding drum sticks
Before you dive into learning drum rudiments, it's important to have the right equipment. It is recommended to use a drum pad instead of a drum, as it is quieter and easier to practice with. Also, be sure to hold the drum sticks in a comfortable and correct way. For a guide on how to hold drum sticks, check out our article titled "How to Hold Drumsticks."

2. Learn Flams
Start with the basic flam rudiment. This rudiment involves playing with one stick high above the drum, about 8-12 inches, and one stick low, about 3 inches. Practice bouncing your sticks in unison with a focus on getting that flam sound.

3. Learn Flam Accents
Flam accents are played by following a flam with two taps. Start slow and gradually increase the tempo. Ensure that you're hitting the two taps strongly.

4. Learn Flamacues
Flamacues are counted "flam-bam-a-cue-flam" or "flam-left-right-left-flam". This rudiment begins with a flam, followed by a single stroke with the opposite hand, and then two strokes with the starting hand. The final note is a flam. Focus on getting a good, solid accent out of your left hand on the "bam" note.

5. Learn Paradiddles
A paradigm is a rudiment played "Right-Left-Right-Right-Left-Right-Left-Left". It's important to practice this rudiment in a variety of tempos to improve coordination.

6. Learn Flamadiddles
Flamadiddles are paradiddles that have a flam at the beginning. This rudiment is played "Flam-right-left-right-right-flam-left-left".

7. Learn Ruffs
Ruffs are similar to flams, except the "low" stick makes two strokes or bounces. Start slow and gradually increase the tempo.

8. Learn Lesson 25's
Lesson 25's are similar to flam accents, but for ruffs. This rudiment is played "Flam-right-left-right-left-right-right".

9. Learn Dragadiddles
There are two types of dragadiddles, No.1 and No.2, but both are a type of paradiddle with ruffs. This rudiment is played "Right-Left-Drag-Right-Left-Right-Left-Drag".

Part 2 – Advanced Rudiments

1. Learn Flam Taps
Flam taps are played "Flam-right-tap-left-tap". Ensure that the taps are solid and sound distinct.

2. Learn Drags
Drags are a form of ruff rudiment and can be single or double. This rudiment is played "Right-Drag-Right-Left-Drag-Left". It's all about the timing in drag rudiments.

3. Learn Sextuplets
Sextuplets are simply counted "1-2-3-4-5-6-7". Practice this rudiment by using alternate sticking and gradually increasing the tempo.

4. Ratamacues
Ratamacues are similar to sextuplets, but they're only "1-2-3-4". It's important to note the placement of the accents in this rudiment.

5. Learn Double Stroke Rolls
Double stroke rolls are a type of rudiment and have several different variations such as 5's, 6's, 7's, 9's, 10's, 11's, 13's, 15's, and 17's. Practice these rudiments using different stroke heights and rhythms to improve your overall technique.

6. Swiss Rudiments
There are several Swiss rudiments that can improve your style and skills. While not considered essential, learning Swiss rudiments such as the single stroke roll and the multiple bounce roll can help you to take your drumming skills to the next level.

In conclusion, playing drum rudiments is crucial for becoming a great drummer. With a little patience, practice, and focus, you can master these basic and advanced rudiments to improve your drumming skills and take your talents to the next level!

Step 5: Remove power supply cables 
Next, remove power supply cables that will run from the square box unit either at the top or bottom of your computer tower. 

Step 6: Remove your stock graphics card 
In most computer motherboards, the stock graphics card will be tightly secured in by plastic clips, which will be located on both sides left and right horizontally of the graphics card. Step 7: Install the new graphics card 
Now you should be able to take the new graphics card and line it up to the connectors on the motherboard in the PCI Express 2.0 16X slot. Make sure to line up the gold foil connectors as you see the connectors in the PCI Express 2.0 slot. 

Step 8: Reconnect IDE cable 
Next, reconnect your IDE cable back into the motherboard and make sure to apply firm force and to distribute it evenly so that the connectors are in place.

Are you in need of a cute, small coin purse that can easily fit in your pocket or purse? Look no further than this DIY project on how to make a small round coin purse. With just a few materials and some basic sewing skills, you'll have a custom-made coin purse in no time.

Part 1: Gather Your Materials
To begin, you'll need the following:
- Cardboard or plastic circles (for the purse's base)
- Fabric circles (for the purse's exterior and interior)
- Padding material (such as quilt batting)
- Zippers
- Scissors
- Needle and thread
- Sewing machine (optional)

Part 2: Trace and Cut the Circles
Using your desired size for the coin purse, trace and cut out four circles from the cardboard or plastic material. Then, cut four circles of fabric that are at least 3/4 inch (2cm) larger all around than the cardboard/plastic circles.

Part 3: Gather the Fabric Circles
Gather the edges of the fabric circles by stitching a running stitch along the outer edge of each circle and then pulling the thread to gather the fabric.

Part 4: Add Padding and Stiff Circles
Place the padding material and stiff circles inside two of the gathered fabric circles. Then, snug everything down by pulling on the gathering thread. Repeat with the remaining two fabric circles and cardboard/plastic circles.

Part 5: Measure and Shorten the Zipper
Measure the zipper to fit the diameter of the rounds. Shorten the zipper, if needed, by stitching a new zipper stop at the desired length.

Part 6: Create a Loop Handle
Create a loop handle at this point if you want one. Sew the loop to the "stop" or non-opening end of the zipper.

Part 7: Assemble the Layers
Roll the raw edges under and stitch again to make a smooth (French) seam. Then, assemble the layers by placing the zipper edge along the inside, unpadded fabric/cardboard circle. Hand stitch the zipper to the edge of the inner, un-padded circle.

Part 8: Finish the Purse
Repeat for the second zipper edge, stitching it to the other un-padded circle. Open the zipper (if it's not already open) and place the gathered side of a padded circle against the gathered side of the zipper. Slip stitch or blind stitch the two together. Tie off the thread, remove it, and then admire your beautiful new coin purse!

Framing a print is an excellent way to protect and display artwork. A well-framed print can add a touch of elegance to any room, and it also helps preserve the print for years to come. Here's how to frame a print:

1. Measure and cut a mat-board and a mounting board to the overall size calculated to create a mat 4 to 6 inches larger than the print so as to reveal 2 to 3 inches (5 cm to 7 cm) of the mat on all sides of a print.

Before beginning, measure the size of your print and the frame you intend to use. Cut the mat-board and mounting board to the calculated size. The mat-board should be cut to the size of the frame with an additional 4 to 6 inches on each side. The mounting board should be cut to the same size as the print.

2. Obtain a frame matching the dimensions of the finished matted print/mounting board.

Choose a frame that matches the dimensions of your matted print and mounting board. You can find frames at most craft stores or frame shops.

3. Lay the cut-to-size mounting board face up and center the print on it.

Once you have the mounting board cut to size, lay it on a flat surface with the print centered on it. Ensure that the print is straight and centered on the mount.

4. Tape the print to the mounting board with archival tape "hinges" at the top edge only so a print "hangs" and expands and contracts with the humidity.

Use archival tape to create "hinges" on the top edge of the print. This ensures that the print is not permanently stuck to the mounting board and will expand and contract as humidity changes over time.

5. Make a mat for the print using archival mat-board to prevent the print from touching the glass by doing the following.

Cut the archival mat-board to the size that you want your mat. You can choose any color mat that complements your print. The mat will prevent the print from touching the glass which can cause damage over time.

6. Cut the mat-board from the backside along these lines in one stroke for each cut.

Use a mat cutter and cut from the back of the mat-board. Ensure that you cut in one stroke for each cut.

7. Lay the frame face down.

Flip the frame over so that the back is facing up. This will allow you to add the glass, mat, and mounting board to the frame.

8. Clean both sides of the glass to be used in the frame and lay it into the fame.

Before laying the glass in the frame, clean it thoroughly to ensure there are no smudges or fingerprints. Lay the glass into the frame.

9. Lay the display side of finished, cut mat-board into the frame directly on the glass.

Take the finished, cut mat and lay it on the glass. The edges of the mat should overlap the edges of the frame.

10. Lay mounted print in the frame face down on the mat-board installed previously.

Take the mounting board with the print attached and lay it face down over the mat. Place it in the center of the mat.

11. Install backing material of same size as mounting-board/mat into the frame on top of the mounting board just laid in.

Place the backing material on top of the mounting board. It should be the same size as the mounting board and mat.

12. The print is now framed in a professional manner that will last for years.

Secure the backing material into place with the clips attached to the frame. Turn the frame over and admire your newly framed print. It will be protected and look great for years to come.

How to Improve Nutrition for Longer Life

Everyone wants to live a longer and healthier life, and achieving optimal nutrition is a key factor in making that possible. People over 100 years of age (who are hopefully enjoying longevity) have certain things in common, and if you can achieve these three things, you may be surprised at the other factors tied to longevity.

1. Healthy blood sugar and insulin levels

One of the most important factors for longevity is healthy levels of blood sugar and insulin in the blood. High blood sugar, as in diabetes, is known to slow the healing of injuries and complicate infections (especially in feet and legs) - and as many people get older, they have problems with circulation in the legs and feet. To improve your blood sugar and insulin levels, consider eating a healthy diet that is low in sugar and carbohydrates.

2. Raise your immunity

Another important factor in longevity is a strong immune system, which can help protect you from disease and allow you to maintain your health well into old age. You can raise your immunity by up to 92%, instead of reducing it, by consuming less sugar. Studies have shown that consuming even a small amount of sugar can lower your immunity significantly. To avoid this, reduce your sugar intake and consider using supplements such as vitamins, minerals, and natural compounds such as gymnema sylvestre, banana leaf extract, cinnamon, and biotin.

3. Avoid depleted food values

Mass-produced groceries often yield depleted food values as the farm soils are not rich in micro-nutrients and mineral nutrients compared to what they used to be. Avoid consuming these depleted foods and consider buying fresh produce from local farmers markets as much as possible.

In summary, if you want to improve your nutrition for a longer and healthier life, focus on achieving the three things that people over 100 have in common - healthy blood sugar and insulin levels, a strong immune system, and consuming nutrient-rich, whole foods. By doing this, you may be surprised at what other factors are tied to longevity and what a significant impact nutrition can have on your overall health and well-being.

Indiana Jones is one of the most iconic movie characters of all time. His signature hat and whip make for a classic costume that's perfect for Halloween or any costume party. Creating an Indiana Jones costume is easier than you might think. In this article, we'll guide you through the steps to create your own whip and hat, and show you how to put together the rest of the costume for a convincing Indiana Jones look.

Part 1: Making the Whip

Step 1: Line up a 6-9 feet (1.75-2 meter) roll of cabinet liner.

Step 2: Measure and cut the liner starting from one end to the other end starting out from 3 inch wide from one end.

Step 3: Increase width of liner by 3/8 - 1/2 inch every 6 inches.

Step 4: Cut along until you've reached the desired length of your whip.

Step 5: Put a 10 feet long string or yarn through the loop of a sewing needle.

Step 6: Run the needle weaving the piece of yarn straight through one edge of the piece of liner you had cut.

Step 7: Cut a 10 feet piece of wire or nylon fishing line.

Step 8: Pass the wire through a sewing needle's loop.

Step 9: Weave the piece of wire through the liner starting from the same place as you did the piece of yarn.

Step 10: Weave the wire straight through the liner at an angle.

Step 11: Line up the jump-rope along the edge of the liner where the piece of yarn was weaved.

Step 12: Wrap the jump-rope carefully with the liner like a burrito.

Step 13: Turn your hot glue gun on to heat it up while you are rolling and wrapping the rope with the liner.

Step 14: Glue the edge with the rope and the overlapping piece of liner as you hold one end with your other hand.

Step 15: Leave 6-8 inches of the thick end unwrapped.

Step 16: Cut a 6-8 inch long 1/2 inch wide round stick or dowel rod with a saw.

Step 17: Set the handle on the unwrapped end piece of liner.

Step 18: Glue the liner along the handle to secure it in place.

Part 2: Making the Hat

Step 1: Cut out a 12 inch diameter round piece of felt fabric.

Step 2: Cut out a donut shape piece of felt with a 6 inch (15.2 cm) diameter inside edge and a 12 inch (30.5 cm) diameter outside edge.

Step 3: Find two deep bowls or cooking pots that one fits inside the other.

Step 4: Place the round shaped piece of felt centered on top of the bigger pot.

Step 5: Place the smaller pot on top of the felt piece and the big pot.

Step 6: Glue or stitch the donut shaped piece of felt to the dome shaped felt piece.

Step 7: Cut out a strap for your hat from the piece of liner you have left over from making the bull-whip.

Step 8: Glue the strap to your hat.

Part 3: Putting the Costume Together

Step 1: Find some khaki pants.

Step 2: Wear a beige or white shirt.

Step 3: Get a brown leather jacket, if you can.

Step 4: Put on your hat and grab your whip.

With these simple steps, you can quickly and easily create your own Indiana Jones costume. Whether you're going trick-or-treating or heading to a costume party, you'll look the part with this iconic costume.

Installing a Smartbus Dimmer and Relay can add automation and convenience to your lighting system. With the ability to control the lights through a network, it is easy to create custom lighting scenes and schedules. In this article, we will guide you through the necessary steps to install a Smartbus Dimmer and Relay.

Part 1: Understanding the S-BUS Network

The S-BUS network is a communication protocol that enables devices to interact with each other to control lighting and other electrical systems. To achieve this network, you need only four wires; DATA +, DATA-, GND, and +24V. You can use any type of DATA cable, such as CAT5 or CAT6.

Part 2: Preparing Your Tools

Before starting the installation process, you need to gather some tools. You will need a screwdriver, pliers, wire strippers, and a voltage tester. Make sure to wear safety gloves and goggles while working with electrical wires.

Part 3: Considering Your Options

Smart BUS G4 devices are rail mountable devices, and they are equipped with two connectors on both sides that enable multiple devices to be cascaded in a train-like manner on the rail. Consider what type of Smartbus Dimmer and Relay you need based on the requirements of your lighting system.

Part 4: Understanding the Smartbus G4 Dimmer

The Smart BUS G4 Dimmer is a device that controls the light, with the ability to dim any dimmable lights. Light circuits always run with two wires, the line and the neutral, the hot and the cold, and the phase and the black. Smart BUS G4 Dimmers accept both 220V and 110V AC power input.

Part 5: Checking the Dimmer Channels Load Handling

Each channel of the dimmer can handle a maximum load of 3 Amps. For extra protection, it is recommended to connect an external fuse ahead of each channel to protect against overload, shorts, and any other electrical issues. The simple buttons on the surface of the dimmer act as a manual switch to turn the lights on and off.

Part 6: Installing the Smartbus Dimmer

To install the dimmer, follow these steps:

1. Turn off the power to the lighting circuit at the main breaker.
2. Identify the line and neutral wires in the light switch box.
3. Strip 1/2 inch of insulation off the ends of the line and neutral wires and connect them to the dimmer.
4. Connect the DATA + and DATA- wires to the dimmer.
5. Connect the GND and +24V wires to the dimmer.
6. Test the dimmer and switch on the power to the lighting circuit.

Part 7: Programming the Dimmer

After the bus is connected, you can control the channels and dim them using other devices like the DDP or an Apple device using the G4 iOS application. Refer to the programming manual for the Dimmer-DDP for more information on how to program it.

Part 8: Wiring the Relays

The Smartbus Relay is a device that can control multiple electrical devices. To wire the relays, follow these steps:

1. Turn off the power to the electrical circuit at the main breaker.
2. Identify the line and neutral wires in the electrical switch box.
3. Strip 1/2 inch of insulation off the ends of the line and neutral wires and connect them to the relay.
4. Connect the DATA + and DATA- wires to the relay.
5. Connect the GND and +24V wires to the relay.
6. Test the relay and switch on the power to the electrical circuit.

In conclusion, installing a Smartbus Dimmer and Relay can enhance your lighting system's functionality, creating a more comfortable and convenient environment for your home or office. Follow the above steps carefully and ask for professional help if you are uncertain about any part of the installation process.

Watching your neighbors' cat while they are away can be a fun and rewarding experience. It can also provide a good opportunity for you to get to know your neighbors better, as well as the furry friend they have living with them. However, there are a few things you should do before, during, and after the cat's stay with you to ensure that everything goes smoothly. Here's how to watch the neighbors' cat.

1. Visit the cat over at your neighbors' house before they drop him/her off to stay.
Before the owner leaves the cat with you, it is a good idea to meet the cat and the owner in their environment. This will help you get a sense of the cat's personality and habits, and also give you a chance to ask any questions you may have.

2. Ask the owner about feedings, allergies/medications, sensitivities (such as getting along with other animals, etc) and whether or not the kitty is litter-trained.
It is important to know how often the cat needs to be fed, and what type of food he/she eats. You should also check if the cat has any allergies or medical conditions that you need to be aware of, and if he/she gets along with other animals. Knowing if the cat is litter-trained is also important as it can prevent any unpleasant situations.

3. Get contact phone numbers for emergency use or questions you may have later: the owner, the vet, and a friend of the owner who has a car in case of emergency (necessary if you yourself do not have a car).
Make sure you have all the necessary contact information in case of an emergency or if you have any questions. This includes the owner's contact info, the vet's contact info, and a friend of the owner who can help in case of an emergency.

4. Kitty-proof your place before the cat comes over.
Before the cat comes over, you should make sure that your house is safe for him/her. This includes removing any harmful objects or plants, closing small openings, and keeping any valuable items out of reach.

5. When the cat is over, open his/her kennel and let her come out when he/she is ready to - never reach in as this could result in a nasty scratch.
When the cat arrives at your place, it may take some time for him/her to adjust. Be patient and let the cat come out of the kennel on his/her own terms.

6. Set up food dishes and water where they are accessible and make sure that the cat sees where you put them.
Make sure the cat knows where his/her food and water dishes are, and that they are easily accessible.

7. Give the cat time to adjust to his/her new surroundings, so sit back and let him/her explore.
Be patient and give the cat time to adjust to his/her new surroundings. Let him/her explore and become comfortable with his/her new environment.

8. Expect the cat to be somewhat skittish for the first day, but by the first night, he/she should be playful and willing to at least sit on the couch with you.
The cat may be a bit nervous or anxious at first, but he/she should become more comfortable over time. By the end of the first night, the cat should be more relaxed and willing to spend time with you.

9. Set up a play time each day and give plenty of cuddles!
Make sure to spend some quality time with the cat each day. This includes playing with him/her, petting him/her, and giving plenty of cuddles! 

Watching your neighbors' cat can be a fun and rewarding experience for both you and the cat. By following these tips, you can help ensure that the cat has a comfortable and enjoyable stay with you.

How to Crack a Safe

Cracking a safe may seem like an impossible task, but with the right method and tools, it's possible to access what you need. In this article, we'll take a step-by-step approach to help you learn how to crack a safe.

Start with the combination dial.

The combination dial is the first part of the safe's lock that you'll need to manage. The dial is used to spin the combination wheels, which will allow you access to the safe. You should begin the process by studying the lock and getting familiar with the combination dial.

Know how the spindle works.

The spindle in the safe's lock is a metal rod that connects the combination dial to the rest of the lock. When you turn the dial, the spindle moves, and it's important to understand how it works to gain access to the safe.

Know how the drive cam is connected to the spindle.

The drive cam is a small part of the lock that engages the combination wheels. Understanding how the drive cam connects to the spindle will help you to visualize the internal workings of the safe and crack it open.

Understand a safe's wheels.

The wheels in the safe are connected to the lock, and they must be set to the correct combination to be able to open the safe. These wheels have small notches on them that must be set correctly to open the safe.

Visualize the fence.

The fence is a small metal rod inside the lock that moves back and forth as the combination wheels turn. To crack the safe, you need to understand the relationship between the fence and the combination wheels.

Understand how wheel notches come into play.

The notches on each combination wheel work with the fence to unlock the safe. You need to learn how to manipulate these notches to gain access to the safe.

Continue to the appropriate section based on your available knowledge.

Depending on your experience, you may already understand some of the concepts discussed above. Regardless of your knowledge, continue reading to learn how to crack a safe.

Turn the dial several full revolutions clockwise.

To begin opening the safe, turn the dial several full revolutions in a clockwise direction. This makes the wheels spin and allows you to begin listening for sounds that will help you determine the correct combination.

Place a stethoscope near the dial surface.

A stethoscope is a tool that helps you to hear faint sounds more clearly. Place the stethoscope near the dial to hear the clicks that indicate the correct combination. 

Rotate the dial counterclockwise and listen carefully for two clicks near each other.

Turn the dial counterclockwise and listen for clicks. You should hear two clicks close together at some point, which will help you determine the combination.

Reset the lock again and repeat.

If you don't hear the clicks clearly, reset the lock and repeat the process.

Dial counterclockwise until the dial is opposite the sound of the two clicks.

When you hear the two clicks, turn the dial counterclockwise until the dial is opposite the position where you heard the clicks.

Turn the dial clockwise and listen each time you pass the original point.

Turn the dial clockwise and listen for clicks each time you pass the original position.

Keep rotating and count the number of clicks you hear.

Rotate the dial and count the number of clicks you hear. You need to record this number.

Write down the total number of clicks.

Write down the total number of clicks you heard in the previous step.

Set up two line graphs.

Set up two line graphs to help you visualize the relationship between the dial position and the clicks you heard.

Label each graph.

Label each graph to make it easier to use.

Reset the lock, then set it to zero.

Reset the lock to its original position and set it to zero.

Rotate slowly counterclockwise and listen.

Rotate the dial counterclockwise and listen for the clicks.

When you hear two clicks close together, note the position of the dial at each click.

Record the positions of the dial each time you hear two clicks.

Graph these points.

Use the points you recorded and graph them on one of the line graphs.

Reset the lock and set it 3 numbers left of zero.

Reset the lock and set it three numbers left of zero.

Continue recording the location of the two clicks.

Repeat the process of recording the location of the two clicks until your line graphs are complete.

Keep testing until your line graphs are done.

Keep testing until the line graphs are complete and you have enough information to determine the safe's combination.

Look for points on your graphs where the two y-values converge.

Look for points on your graphs where the two y-values converge. This will indicate the possible combinations.

Write down the x-values at these locations.

Write down the x-values at the locations where the y-values converge.

Try every possible sequence of the numbers you located.

Use the x-values you recorded to try every possible sequence of the numbers you located until you find the correct combination.

Try combinations using adjacent numbers if the safe won't open.

If the safe won't open, try using combinations of adjacent numbers to see if that works.

Try again from the beginning.

If you can't get the safe open, start again from the beginning and repeat the process. With enough patience and persistence, you'll eventually be able to crack the safe and gain access to what's inside.

Drawing the Root Locus of a System

A root locus is a graphical representation of the roots of the characteristic equation, plotted as a function of a parameter, usually the gain. This is a useful tool in control system analysis and design. In this article, we will show you how to draw the root locus of a system.

Part 1: Basic Concepts

1. Know that the simplest system has an input and an output. The purpose of a control system is to manipulate the input to get a desired output.

2. Show a system by a box. A block diagram is a graphical representation of a system, where a block represents a mathematical operation or a physical component.

3. Remember that a system without feedback in engineering notation is like the one shown in the image. A block diagram without feedback is called an open-loop system.

4. Manipulate the last result to get (see the image above). This is the transfer function of the open-loop system.

5. Show, then, with the same formal notations onwards. The transfer function is a ratio of two polynomials in s, where s is the Laplace variable.

6. Manipulate the last result to get (see the image above). This is the transfer function of the closed-loop system with negative feedback.

7. Note that the ratio Y(s) / X(s), whatever it is, is called the transfer function. The transfer function describes the relationship between the input and the output of a system.

8. Keep in mind that you can have an equation, 1 + H(s)G(s) = 0. This is the characteristic equation of the feedback system, which determines the stability of the system.

9. Remember that a complex rational function is the ratio of two complex polynomials. The poles and zeros of the transfer function are the roots of the denominator and numerator polynomials, respectively.

10. Compare the ratio Y(s) / X(s) in two systems without feedback and with feedback to see what is the effect of the feedback in a system. The feedback reduces the error between the desired and the actual output and improves the performance and stability of the system.

Part 2: Drawing the Root Locus
1. Do a simple calculation to convince you that the feedback function can be gobbled into the input before the comparison point. This is the concept of forward path transfer function.

2. Observe the simple feedback. The feedback function is K / (s + 2).

3. Write equation 2, then as (see the image above). This is the characteristic equation of the closed-loop system.

4. Separate gain K. It is better to separate gain of the system as an independent block. The block diagram of the closed-loop system is shown in the image.

5. Write, then, equation 3 as (see the image above). This is the transfer function of the closed-loop system.

6. Note that the denominator determines stability of the system. A pole is a value of s that makes the denominator zero, which corresponds to an unstable system.

7. Calculate the magnitude (modulus) and angle (argument) of G(s). G(s) is a rational function; that is, equal to a polynomial divided by a polynomial both in the same variable s. Hence, |G(s)| is the distance from the origin to the point on the graph of G(s) in the complex plane, and arg(G(s)) is the angle between the positive real axis and the complex vector G(s).

8. Remember G(s) is a rational function; that is, equal to a polynomial divided by a polynomial both in the same variable s. Hence, the poles and zeros of G(s) are the roots of the denominator and numerator polynomials, respectively.

9. Observe that, generally, it is not easy to find roots of a polynomial of degree greater than three or four and write it out in its roots factors, as it is done in Equation 5.

10. Begin from the simplest system. For the example in this article, we will assume that the transfer function of the open-loop system is G(s) = 1 / (s + 1)(s + 3).

11. Remember. The root locus is the loci of the closed-loop poles as the gain K is varied from zero to infinity.

12. Solve a similar Root Locus for the control system depicted in the feedback loop here. 

13. Ask questions regarding K. What are the values of K for which the closed-loop system is stable or unstable? What are the poles and zeros of the closed-loop transfer function for various values of K?

14. Begin from K = 0. This is the starting point of the root locus. The poles of the open-loop system are s = -1 and s = -3.

15. Increase K. You have still two real roots, until K = 1 / 4, where two roots will be equal; that is s1 = s2 = – 1 / 2. At this gain, the closed-loop system exhibits a critical damping response.

16. Increase K > 1 / 4. The two poles of the closed-loop system will move towards each other and eventually meet at the origin of the complex plane, when K = infinity.

17. Know the meaning of things happening in complex plane. The root locus is a plot of the poles of the closed-loop system in the complex plane, as the gain K is varied. The real part of the poles corresponds to the damping of the system, while the imaginary part corresponds to the frequency of oscillation.

18. Note that the complex plane is not like the real line. The complex plane is a two-dimensional plane, where numbers are represented by complex numbers z = x + iy, where x and y are real numbers and i is the imaginary unit.

19. Evaluate arbitrary test point s1 with respect to the root of polynomial s + 2 = 0. This is the concept of ruling asymptotes, which are the straight lines that pass through the poles and the zeros of the open-loop transfer function.

20. Assume you have certain number of the real roots on the real line. The segments of the real axis that lie to the left of an odd number of real poles and zeros belong to the root locus.

21. Remember the characteristic function for the general feedback loop was 1 + G(s)H(s) = 0. The root locus of a system depends on the open-loop transfer function G(s) and the feedback function H(s).

22. Recognise a proper system. A proper system is one whose transfer function has no poles or zeros at the origin.

23. Know the meaning of branches. The root locus branches are the curves that connect the poles of the closed-loop transfer function, as the gain K is varied. The branches start at the poles of the open-loop transfer function and end at the roots of the characteristic equation.

Tennis is a fun and challenging sport to play, but getting better can be quite frustrating if you don't know where to start. Whether you're a beginner or an advanced player, this guide will provide you with some helpful tips on how to improve your tennis game. You will learn the right way to grip a tennis racket, choose a racket that is suitable for your age and strength, practice hitting and get to know other players on the court by introducing yourself, warm-up and play matches about twice a week, and try different plans of attack during a match.

Part 1: Equipment

The first step to becoming a better tennis player is choosing the right equipment. A suitable tennis racket is essential to play the game well. Weight, grip size, head size, and balance are all important factors that you should consider when selecting a racket. Make sure to choose a racket that is appropriate for your age, strength, and playing style. Additionally, it's crucial to grip your tennis racket in the right way. 

1. Learn the right way to grip a tennis racket

The most common grip is the Eastern forehand grip, which is a neutral grip that is suitable for beginners. Place your hand on the racket and align the base knuckle of your index finger with the third bevel of the racket handle. Next, wrap your fingers around the handle and place your thumb flat against the back of the handle. 

Part 2: Practice

Practice is critical if you want to become a better tennis player. Hitting with other players as well as practicing solo will bring you tremendous benefits. Here are some tips on how to practice effectively. 

1. Practice hitting and introducing yourself to other players

Go to a local tennis court or join a tennis club to practice hitting and meeting other players. Start by introducing yourself and arranging a match with someone of similar skill level. Practicing with others allows you to learn from their strengths and weaknesses and also helps identify your own. 

2. Warm-up and play matches about twice a week

Warming up before playing is crucial to avoid injuries. Try doing some light cardio exercises like jogging, jumping jacks, or skipping rope for 5-10 minutes. Afterward, stretch your muscles for another 5-10 minutes to increase blood flow and flexibility. Additionally, aim to play matches about twice a week to improve your consistency, stamina, and shot-making abilities. 

3. Try different plans of attack during a match

There are different plans of attack that you can try during a match. They are:

a) Serve & Volley - Serve hard and charge the net position. 

b) Chip & Charge - Hit a deep ball and charge. 

c) Inside-Out Forehand - Sidestep around a ball hit to your backhand side and hit it using a forehand stroke.

d) Junk Balling - Hit only slices with backspin.

e) Rally & Wait - Exchange groundstrokes and go for a hard winner. 

Part 3: Technique

Here's some expert advice on how to improve your technique and avoid common mistakes.

1. Always keep your eyes on the ball

It might seem obvious, but keeping your eyes on the ball is crucial. Doing so allows you to track the ball's movement, enabling you to hit it cleanly.

2. Plant your feet just before hitting

Many players make the mistake of hitting the ball while they're still moving. However, planting your feet right before the shot allows you to maximize your power and accuracy.

3. Be aware of your position on the court

It's essential to know where you are on the court and adjust accordingly. Try to stay in the center of the court to have maximum reach.

4. Determine your playing style

Polymer clay molds can add an interesting dimension to your art projects and crafts. Creating your own molds can be a fun and creative process. With a little bit of patience and practice, you can easily create your own polymer clay molds at home. In this article, we will guide you through the steps of making your own polymer clay molds.

Method 1: Regular Polymer Clay Molds

1. Condition any polymer clay until it's smooth and pliable. Work it in your hands until it becomes easy to manipulate.

2. Roll the clay into a smooth ball between palms after conditioning. This will help remove any air bubbles.

3. Put a release on the clay and/or the item to be molded if needed. A release can be anything from a thin layer of oil to cornstarch. This will allow easy removal of the item from the mold.

4. Push the item being used to create the mold into a ball or a slab of raw clay. Press it firmly but gently.

5. Gently remove the item from the clay. Be cautious to not damage the clay mold.

6. Place the raw clay mold on a metal baking tray or on another oven-safe carrier. Make sure it's stable.

7. Bake the clay in a preheated oven. Follow the manufacturer's instructions for baking temperature and time.

8. Set a timer for 20 to 45 minutes depending on the thickness of the mold and the brand/line of clay used. Check on the mold periodically.

9. Remove the hardened mold from the oven on its carrier and allow it to cool. Give it time to cool to room temperature.

10. Make as many molds as you want once you've gotten the hang of it. Practice makes perfect.

Method 2: Using Pre-Made Molds

1. Rigid or silicone molds can also be purchased already made. Look for these molds in craft stores or online.

2. If you want, make casts from your molds with scrap clay then number the matching molds ("innies") and casts ("outies") on their back sides to keep matching molds and casts straight. This is especially helpful if you create a lot of molds.

3. Roll the clay into a smooth ball as in method 1.

4. Remove the cast from the mold. Be cautious not to damage the mold.

5. If you want, highlight or antique the casts. This will give them a more interesting look.

6. Use the casts in many ways (including casts from texture molds). Be creative and explore the possibilities.

7. If desired, the clay cast can be cut into another shape before baking.

Method 3: Texture Molds

1. Follow the instructions for making regular molds as in method 1, but start with a flat sheet of clay for most texture molds.

2. It will be best to place a sheet of paper or deli wrap, etc, under the clay sheet before continuing so the clay won't stick to the work surface later.

3. Use a release, then press anything shallow but dimensional and at least somewhat firm into the clay sheet.

4. Carefully separate the clay and texture material. Be cautious so as not to damage the texture.

5. Use part or all of the raw textured sheet in some way for a final piece and bake later.

Method 4: Two-Part Molds

1. To create a reverse mold, first make and bake a mold or a texture sheet.

2. Press new raw clay into or onto that mold to create its opposite.

3. Separate the hardened clay from the raw clay, and bake the new clay.

4. Cut two thick slabs of clay. These will be the two halves of the mold.

5. Roll over one wide side of each slab with a roller or jar to make it very flat.

6. Dust the rolled-over side of one slab well with cornstarch or baby powder.

7. Press the item down into that side of the slab until it is about halfway into the clay.

8. Remove the item from the first slab, and bake it.

9. Heavily dust one side of the second slab (especially since polymer clay will bond to other polymer clay when heated if it's bare), then carefully press it down onto the first slab and snug all around the item as much as possible.

10. Cool, then separate the halves of the final mold and remove the item.

11. To use the two-part mold later, experimentation may be necessary to find the right amount of raw clay for the mold, i.e., just enough to fill, but not enough to overfill, and the best shape of clay to use.

12. Do everything as above but instead of using two slabs, wrap a wad of clay (flat or any shape that works) halfway around the item, leaving the upper edges of the wad uneven or adding registration marks.

13. Use a second wad of clay as above rather than a second slab.

In conclusion, making polymer clay molds can be a fun and rewarding experience. Use this guide to create your own molds and explore the wide range of options for creating unique and interesting art projects.

Maintaining the health and speed of your Windows 8.1 Pro hard drive can be accomplished through performing regular disk defragmentation. This process works by reorganizing fragmented data on the hard drive, making it easier and quicker for your computer to access and process information. In this article, we will guide you through the steps to defrag (disk defragment) a hard drive on Windows 8.1 Pro.

1. Navigate to your Desktop
Begin by navigating to your desktop. Once you have reached your desktop, right-click anywhere (not on an icon) and select "Personalize" from the drop-down menu.

2. Open Personalization Settings
After clicking "Personalize", a window called "Personalization" should appear. From there, click on the "Change desktop icons" option located on the left-hand side of the window.

3. Enable Computer Icon
Next, click on the checkbox next to the "Computer" or "This PC" option and click "Apply" and "OK" to save the changes. You should now see the Computer icon appear on your desktop.

4. Open Disk Properties
Double-click on the "Computer" or "This PC" icon to open the Hard Drive Properties. From there, select the Properties option from the context menu.

5. Run Disk Cleanup
In the Hard Drive Properties window, click on the "Disk Cleanup" button located at the bottom right-hand corner. Wait for the system to calculate the amount of data that can be deleted.

6. Access the "Optimize Drives" Option
After completing the disk cleanup, select the "Tools" tab from the Hard Drive Properties window. You will then see the "Optimize Drives" option. Click on it to open the defragmentation tool.

7. Optimize Hard Drives
Once the "Optimize Drives" window has opened, select the hard drive you want to defragment. If you have multiple drives, select the one you want to optimize by clicking on it such that it highlights in blue. Then click "Optimize" next to the "Analyze" button.

Conclusion
By following these simple steps, you can defragment your hard drive in Windows 8.1 Pro, ensuring optimal performance and speed for your computer.

How to Make a Carnation Corsage

If you're attending a wedding or prom, a beautiful carnation corsage can add a touch of elegance to your outfit. With a few materials and some basic floral arrangement skills, you can create your own stunning corsage in no time. In this article, we'll guide you through the steps for creating a carnation corsage that will make you the belle of the ball.

Materials:
- Carnations (spray or single, depending on preference)
- Filler flowers (ferns, leaves, or additional flowers)
- 22-gauge wire
- Florist's tape
- Wired silk ribbon
- Shears
- Wire cutter
- Pins
- Plastic container (for storage)

Instructions:

1. Snip each carnation head off with shears. Remove any leaves from the stem that will be below the corsage.

2. Snip some filler ferns, leaves, or flowers. Trim them to a length that complements the carnations.

3. Cut several 6 inch (15.2 cm) pieces of 22-gauge wire using a wire cutter.

4. Thread a piece of wire through the upper part of the stem, just below the base. Twist the wire tightly around the stem to secure it.

5. Cut a 6 inch (15.2 cm) piece of green florist's tape. Affix the top to the point just above where the wire is inserted into the stem.

6. Wrap the tape around the wire at a downward angle until you reach the ends. This will cover the wire and provide a polished look.

7. Arrange the stems of your filler flowers or leaves around your carnation. You should aim for a balanced look with equal proportions on both sides.

8. Cut another 6 inch (15.2 cm) piece of florist's tape and wrap the stems around the artificial stem. This will help hold everything in place.

9. Repeat this process for each of the spray or single carnations you are using.

10. Arrange each of the carnations in the order you would like them to appear. You can experiment with different arrangements until you find one that looks best to you.

11. Cut a long piece of florist's tape. Wrap the tape around the base of the corsage several times to create a sturdy stem.

12. Cut a very long piece of wired silk ribbon. Create a loop in the ribbon and place it between your thumb and forefinger. Continue looping and stacking the ribbon in 4 to 5 figure 8 loops.

13. Take a 6 inch (15.2 cm) piece of wire and thread it through the center of your loops. Twist the wire tightly to secure the loops together.

14. Align the ribbon with the base of the carnations. Wrap a long piece of florist's tape around the bow wire and the larger corsage stem to secure the ribbon in place.

15. Place a pencil or pen near the bottom of the corsage stem. This will give it an elegantly curved shape.

16. Place 2 pins in the top of the spiral, for pinning on a lapel or dress. Make sure the pins are securely in place.

17. Trim any spray that extends too far from the sides of the corsage. You want it to be compact and neat.

18. Keep the corsage in a plastic container in the refrigerator until it is ready to be given. This will help it stay fresh for longer.

With these steps, you'll have a stunning carnation corsage that will look beautiful and hold up for hours. Whether you're attending a wedding or prom, your corsage is sure to turn heads and make you feel confident and beautiful.

Babysitting can be a fun and rewarding job for teens and adults alike. Whether you're looking for a way to earn extra cash or just enjoy spending time with kids, there are several things you can do to ensure a successful babysitting experience. In this article, we'll walk you through the steps of how to babysit, from attending a childcare or babysitting class to knowing what to do at bedtime.

Part 1: Before You Start Babysitting

1. Attend a childcare or babysitting class.

Before you start babysitting, it's a good idea to attend a childcare or babysitting class. These courses cover topics like first aid, CPR, and child development, and can help you feel more confident and prepared when caring for children.

2. Be a mother's helper.

If you're new to babysitting, consider starting out as a mother's helper. This involves assisting a parent while they care for their child, rather than being solely responsible for the child's well-being. This can be a lower-pressure way to gain experience and build your skills.

3. Set up a schedule.

Before you agree to babysit, make sure you know when the parents need you and for how long. Set up a schedule in advance so that you know what to expect and can plan your own activities accordingly.

4. Decide upon a rate of pay.

Decide upon a rate of pay that feels fair to you and that the parents are willing to pay. Make sure to consider factors like your experience, the number of children you'll be caring for, and any additional duties (like light housekeeping) that you'll be taking on.

5. Create a list of health/safety information.

Create a list of important health and safety information, such as the child's allergies, emergency contact numbers, and any medical conditions or medications the child may have. Keep this information handy while you're babysitting.

6. Market yourself.

Spread the word that you're available for babysitting gigs. Let friends, family, and neighbors know that you're looking for work. You can also create a listing on a babysitting website or app, like Care.com or Sittercity, to reach a broader audience.

7. Know what to do when being interviewed.

When you go to meet the parents and their child, make sure to dress appropriately and be polite. Ask questions about the child's routine and needs, and let the parents know about your own experience and qualifications.

8. Know your comfort zone and its limits.

Be honest with yourself about your comfort level when it comes to caring for children. If you're not comfortable with certain tasks, like bathing or driving the child, make sure to let the parents know in advance.

9. Ask yourself these questions before you decide to take the leap.

Before you agree to babysitting, ask yourself whether you enjoy spending time with children, are responsible and reliable, and feel comfortable setting and enforcing boundaries.

Part 2: While You're Babysitting

1. Get the parents’ and child's information.

Make sure to get important information from the parents before they leave, like emergency contact numbers, the child's routine, and any household rules (like whether or not the child is allowed to use electronics).

2. Find out what activities are allowed.

Check with the parents to see what activities are allowed while you're babysitting. Some parents may not want their child to watch TV or play video games, for example.

3. Set up a menu for your time there.

If you'll be babysitting during meal times, make sure to set up a menu that's both kid-friendly and healthy. Ask the parents for any dietary restrictions or preferences.

4. Find out what appropriate punishments are used, when the child misbehaves.

Ask the parents what kind of disciplinary measures are appropriate if the child misbehaves. Make sure to follow their rules and guidelines.

5. Spend time getting to know the kids.

Take some time to get to know the children you're babysitting. Ask them about their interests, play games with them, and let them know that you're there to have fun.

6. Join in with their play time activities.

If the child wants you to join in with their play time activities, make sure to do so. This can help build a stronger bond between you and the child.

7. Tell stories.

Kids love to hear stories. Bring some books or make up your own story to share with the child.

8. Come up with fun projects.

If the kids get bored, come up with some fun projects to keep them entertained. Crafts, science experiments, or cooking activities are all great options.

9. Take them to a playground if the parents say it's OK.

If the parents are comfortable with it, take the children to a nearby playground or park for some outdoor fun.

10. Check in often.

Make sure to check in with the parents throughout the night to let them know how things are going, and to ask any questions or share any concerns.

11. Follow the schedule.

Stick to the schedule that you set up with the parents, including meal times, bedtime, and any other routine activities.

12. Watch a movie.

If the parents have given you permission, watching a movie can be a great way to wind down before bedtime.

13. Take the children out back.

If the home has a backyard, take the children outside to play. Just make sure to supervise them at all times.

14. Make up a handshake.

Kids love secret handshakes. Come up with a fun one to share with the child while you're babysitting.

15. Never leave the kid(s) alone.

Never leave the child alone, even for a moment. Always make sure to supervise them, especially if they're playing outside or in a different part of the house.

16. Don’t bring people over to the house.

Respect the parents' privacy and don't invite anyone over to the house while you're babysitting.

17. Don’t abuse electronics use.

Make sure to follow the parents' rules about electronics use. Don't let the child spend too much time watching TV or playing video games.

18. Don’t play movies/TV on repeat.

Avoid playing the same movie or TV show on repeat, as this can become frustrating for the child.

19. Never answer the door unless you are expecting someone and only when you make sure that it is that person.

Don't answer the door for anyone other than the parents, and only after making sure that it's actually them.

20. Clean up before the parents get home.

Make sure to tidy up the house before the parents arrive home. This will show them that you're responsible and respectful.

21. Don't let the kids "get away" with things.

Make sure to enforce the parents' rules and discipline the child if they misbehave. However, be careful not to overstep your bounds or use excessive force.

22. Always feel free to call the parents if you feel you need to.

If you have any questions or concerns while you're babysitting, don't hesitate to call the parents and ask for their guidance.

23. Make sure that you know procedures for emergencies; who to call, what to do, where to go, that sort of thing.

Be prepared for emergencies by knowing who to call and what to do in case of an accident or emergency.

24. Know how to change a diaper.

If you're caring for an infant or a young child who's not yet potty trained, make sure to know how to change a diaper.

25. Know how to feed children.

Make sure to know how to prepare and feed children of different ages, and to follow any dietary restrictions or preferences that the parents have mentioned.

26. Know what to do at bedtime.

Make sure to follow the parents' bedtime routine, including brushing teeth, reading stories, and tucking the child in. Make sure to supervise the child while they're sleeping, and to be prepared for any nighttime wake-ups or accidents.
