How to Find the Perfect Concealer or Foundation Shade

Choosing the right shade of concealer or foundation can be a challenge, but it’s not impossible. Whether you’re looking for a perfect match or trying to sculpt and highlight your features, there are a few key things you should do to achieve the perfect look.

Recognize the Difference Between Skin Undertone and Shade

Before you start looking for the right shade of concealer or foundation, it’s important to recognize the difference between skin undertone and shade. Skin undertone is the underlying color of your skin – it can be cool (pink, red or bluish), neutral (a mix of cool and warm) or warm (yellow, peach or golden). Skin shade, on the other hand, is the level of lightness or darkness of your skin.

Examine the Veins on the Underside of Your Wrist

One way to determine your skin undertone is to examine the veins on the underside of your wrist. Look closely at the veins – what color are they? If they appear greenish, you are probably warm-toned. If they look blue or purple, you are likely cool-toned. If they appear to be a mix of both, you are probably neutral-toned.

Reference Your Jewelry Collection

Another way to determine your skin undertone is to reference your jewelry collection. If you tend to wear silver jewelry, you are probably cool-toned. If you prefer gold jewelry, you are probably warm-toned. If you wear both, you are likely neutral-toned.

Wrap a White Towel Around Your Face to Examine Your Skin

To determine your skin shade, wrap a white towel around your face and examine your skin. This will help you determine whether your skin is fair, medium, or dark.

Exfoliate and Moisturize Your Skin

Before applying concealer or foundation, make sure your skin is prepped properly. Exfoliate and moisturize your skin to ensure a smooth base for your makeup.

Wear White and Test the Makeup in Good Lighting

When testing concealer or foundation, wear white and be sure to test the makeup in good lighting. This will help you see the true color of the product and ensure it matches your skin tone.

Match the Undertone of Your Skin First

When looking for a concealer or foundation, always match the undertone of your skin first. This will help ensure a natural-looking finish.

Match the Color of Your Face, Neck, and Décolletage

When applying concealer or foundation, match the color of your face, neck, and décolletage. The neck tends to be the lightest, and the face and décolletage are usually slightly darker because they are exposed to more sunlight and elements.

Try 3 Different Shades to Compare

To ensure you find the perfect shade, try 3 different shades to compare. Foundation shades usually fall somewhere on a loose spectrum of fair, moderately fair, medium, medium deep, deep and very deep.

Go 1-2 Shades Lighter Than Your Skin Tone to Neutralize Dark Areas

If you have dark areas on your skin you want to neutralize, go 1-2 shades lighter than your skin tone.

Match Your Foundation Exactly for Concealing Other Areas of the Face

For areas of redness and most other skin issues, it’s best to cover with a concealer that exactly matches your foundation/skin tone. If you have trouble matching them exactly, go for a neutral beige with faint yellow shades.

Adjust Your Chosen Shade to Match the Seasons

As your skin changes throughout the year, you may need to adjust your chosen shade to match the seasons.

Go 1-2 Shades Lighter Than Your Skin Tone for Highlighting

To highlight, apply a concealer 1-2 shades lighter than your skin tone to the areas of your face that naturally catch the light – the top of the cheekbones, directly beneath the arch of the brow, down the center of the nose, and the Cupid’s bow. Highlighting with concealer can help you sculpt your face and give it added dimension.

Go 1-2 Shades Darker Than Your Skin Tone for Contouring

To contour, apply a concealer 1-2 shades darker than your skin tone to the natural hollows of the face – right below the cheekbone, along the jawline, and at the temple near the hairline. Highlighting and contouring are currently enjoying a surge of popularity, so you'll probably see contouring kits and other special products made for this on the market. However, all you really need to get this look are the right concealer shades.

Address Specific Discolorations with Color Correcting Concealer

For specific discolorations, you may want to use a color correcting concealer. These concealers come in shades that are not flesh tones and can be used to neutralize redness or discoloration on the skin.

By following these tips, you can find the perfect concealer or foundation shade for your skin tone and achieve a flawless look for any occasion.

How to Create Jobs or Start a Business by Bids and Quotes

If you're looking to start a new business or create jobs, one strategy you can try is bidding on projects or jobs and quoting prices for your services. This can be a highly effective method for securing new business, but it requires careful planning and preparation. In this article, we'll outline 10 key steps you can take to effectively bid on jobs and projects, and start building your business through competitive pricing.

1. Prepare yourself for the new work: This may be the key if individuals or corporations expect success from the bid-tendering process.

Before you can start bidding on jobs, you need to make sure your business is set up and ready to handle the work. This means having the necessary equipment, tools, staff, and resources in place to deliver on the promises you make in your bids. It's also important to have a clear understanding of your strengths and weaknesses as a business, so you can target jobs that are a good fit for your skill set.

2. Get the job specifications: Learn all about the work, materials, products or project that you need to bid on.

Once you know what kind of work you're looking for, you'll need to start researching potential projects and jobs to bid on. This may involve reviewing online listings, reaching out to potential clients, or networking with colleagues in your industry. When you find a job that interests you, make sure to gather as much information as possible about the job requirements, timeline, and budget.

3. Be sure that you read the specs of your job or product and prepare your exact bid -- understanding all of the specifications and knowing the skill level and quality that you and your partners or employees must be able to do.

Before you submit your bid, take the time to carefully review the job specifications and make sure you understand what's required. This will help you avoid bidding too high or too low, and ensure that you're offering a competitive price for your services. It's also important to be realistic about your capabilities and skill level, and only bid on jobs that you're confident you can deliver on.

4. Write your job bid.

Once you have a clear understanding of the job requirements and your own capabilities, it's time to write your bid. Your bid should include a detailed breakdown of your services, timeline, and pricing. Make sure to highlight your strengths and expertise, and explain why you're the best choice for the job.

5. Ask the customer whether they will accept and seriously consider a bid using a different process or materials, done your way (for you and your team's know-how or a specialty).

If you have a unique approach or technique that you think would benefit the project, don't be afraid to pitch it to the customer. You may be able to differentiate yourself from other bidders by offering a fresh perspective on the job requirements.

6. Show a portfolio of similar work on your website (jobs you've completed): include your online gallery of photos, articles, documents (or PDFs) and references for customers to read.

Having a comprehensive portfolio of your work is a great way to demonstrate your skills and expertise to potential clients. Make sure to showcase your best work, and include testimonials from satisfied customers.

7. You, as the bidder, or a partner, or sales persons should follow-up: visit, call or email to thank the potential customer for the bid and ask for the business to check your bid status and ask whether there are any questions.

Following up with potential customers is a great way to show that you're serious about the job, and to keep your bid top of mind. Make sure to follow up in a timely manner, and be professional and courteous at all times.

8. Keep all commercial aspects of the quote in confidence, but it is important to get any details of the winning bid outcome and winning price if possible.

It's important to maintain confidentiality around your commercial negotiations, but it's also important to keep tabs on your competition. If you can learn more about the winning bid or the price that was offered, you may be able to adjust your pricing strategy for future bids.

9. Stick to your bid, proposal, estimated amount, time schedules and specs.

Once you've submitted your bid, it's important to stick to your commitments. Make sure to deliver your services on time, and to the quality level that you promised in your bid. This will help you build a reputation as a reliable and trustworthy business, which can lead to more work in the future.

10. Get paid, considering giving up an early pay discount: this requires knowing the terms and how long you expect to wait to be paid.

Finally, make sure to get paid for your work. Consider offering an early payment discount to encourage timely payments, and make sure to set clear payment terms upfront. With these strategies in place, you'll be well on your way to bidding on jobs and building your business through competitive pricing.

If you have ever had a stomach ache, then you know exactly how uncomfortable and painful it can be. The same goes for dogs. A stomach ache or upset stomach can leave your furry friend feeling lethargic, uncomfortable, and in pain. Thankfully, there are things that you can do to help ease your dog's discomfort and restore their health. In this article, we’ll show you how to cure a dog's stomach ache.

Withhold food

The first step in treating a dog's stomach ache is to withhold food. Dogs are known to eat just about anything they can get their paws on, so it's crucial to give their digestive system a break. You should withhold food from your dog for at least 12 hours. This will help the stomach to calm down and begin to heal.

Provide clean, fresh drinking water

Although you will be withholding food, you should provide your dog with clean, fresh drinking water. Dehydration can make a stomach ache worse, and access to clean water will help to prevent that.

Ease your dog back into a regular diet

After a few hours of withholding food and providing water, you can begin to ease your dog back into their regular diet. However, you should do this gradually. Start with small, easily digestible meals, such as plain boiled chicken and rice.

Feed him a small meal at first.

Be sure to feed your dog small, frequent meals rather than one large meal. This will prevent your dog from overeating, which can make their stomach ache worse.

Give him some TLC (tender loving care)

It's vital to give your dog lots of love and attention during this time. A calm and comfortable environment can help reduce stress and anxiety, which can improve your dog's overall health.

Provide a gentle heat source

Some dogs find comfort in a warm heat source, such as a heating pad or a warm water bottle wrapped in a towel. Place it on your dog's stomach for a short period, but be careful not to use too much heat, as it can cause burns.

Contact the vet when necessary

If your dog's stomach ache lasts more than a day, or if your pet is showing signs of severe pain or distress, you should contact your vet immediately.

Treat him with anti-nausea medication

Your vet may prescribe anti-nausea medication for your dog, which can be helpful in reducing nausea and vomiting.

Be alert to restlessness

Changes in behavior, such as restlessness and agitation, are signs that your dog may be in pain.

Note if he’s looking at his flanks

Dogs suffering from a stomach ache may frequently look at their flanks, trying to find a comfortable position.

Look for excessive licking

Dogs often try to lick their stomachs to soothe any pain or irritation. It may be an indication that your pet is suffering from a stomach ache.

Listen for stomach rumbling and flatulence

Stomach rumbling and flatulence are typical signs of a dog's stomach ache.

Notice if your dog assumes the 'praying position' 
A classic sign of stomach discomfort is when the dog adopts what's called the "praying position." This position involves stretching out their front legs and tucking their head down between them.

Look for vomiting and diarrhea 

Vomiting and diarrhea are common signs that your dog is suffering from a stomach ache.

Keep rotting food out of reach 

Pets can't always differentiate between fresh and rotting food. Make sure that you keep any rotting food out of reach from your furry friend.

Do not free-feed your pet

Some owners free-feed their dogs, meaning they put out large amounts of food and allow their pets to graze throughout the day. However, this can lead to overeating, which increases the risk of a stomach ache.

Buy a good quality dog food

Choosing a good quality dog food can help to reduce the risk of a stomach ache. Look for foods that contain high-quality proteins and are free from additives and preservatives.

Do not feed your dog from the table

Feeding your dog human food is not recommended, as it can lead to upset stomachs and other health problems.

Don't let him play with sick dogs

Sick dogs can transmit diseases that can cause stomach aches and other health issues in your furry friend. Avoid allowing your dog to play with sick dogs.

Take your dog’s underlying health issues into consideration

Preexisting health issues, such as diabetes, can make a dog more susceptible to stomach aches. Consult with your veterinarian if your dog has any underlying health issues.

In conclusion, a stomach ache can leave your dog feeling uncomfortable and in pain. By following these tips, you can help your furry friend feel better, fast. Remember to contact your vet if you have any concerns or if the symptoms persist.

How to Make Your Own Beauty Products: Understanding the Various Reasons to Use Homemade Beauty Products

There are many reasons to use homemade beauty products over commercial ones. First of all, homemade beauty products are usually cheaper than store-bought ones, which can be expensive due to their branding and advertising costs. Additionally, homemade beauty products are typically made with natural ingredients that are free from harmful chemicals often found in commercial products.

If you are interested in creating your own beauty products, begin by experimenting with facial and skin-care options. Start by allowing all facials and moisturizers to sit on your skin for 10-15 minutes before rinsing off with warm water. Also, it's essential to test any product you create at home on a small area of skin first to ascertain the possibility of any adverse reactions.

One simple facial scrub you can make is with oatmeal and water. This scrub will help to clear and cleanse your skin. You can also mix 2 tablespoons of sugar with 1 teaspoon of milk to create a face scrub that uses milk to cleanse and exfoliate.

Plain, whole-milk yogurt is another excellent option for a face mask to calm redness from sun, wind or harsh products. Sugar and olive oil can also be used as an exfoliant. Mix 1 tablespoon of sugar with a few drops of olive oil for a sweet facial exfoliant.

You can also make a mild astringent face mask from apples and pears or a facial scrub from grapes. Additionally, you can use papaya to relax and cleanse your face. Wet green tea leaves can create softer, silkier skin.

Try using baking soda to loosen blackheads and honey to make a moisturizing face mask. Take care when using eye creams and lotions. Cut 10 rounds of cucumber and use them to refresh tired eyes.

To make a skin softening bath, add a cup of milk and 2-3 tablespoons of honey to your bathwater. If you have oily skin, use aloe vera gel as an astringent. For hair care, revive tired locks with cucumber and carrots; peel and grate half a cucumber and squeeze out the juice through muslin cloth.

For really dirty hair, add a teaspoon of baking soda to your shampoo, and to extend your shampoo, mix honey in your shampoo. Eggs are an excellent option for strong, shiny hair. Mix two eggs with 1/4 cup olive oil and coat your hair with the mixture. For a hair rinse, mix honey and water in equal parts.

Lastly, vinegar can be used on your hair to balance pH and create shine. If you have dull hair, mix equal parts of honey and olive oil and apply to your hair. Using an Array Class in JavaScript is a great way to store and manipulate sets of data in your program. With Arrays, you can store multiple values in a single variable, access those values using an index, and easily manipulate the data. In this article, we’ll show you how to create an Array object in JavaScript and how to use it effectively.

Part 1: Creating an Array Object
The first step in using an Array class is to create an Array object. You can do this using one of two methods.

Method 1: Empty Array Object
To create an empty array object, you can use the following code:

var aValues = new Array();

This creates an empty array with no values. You can then populate the array with values as needed.

Method 2: Pre-populated Array Object
If you know ahead of time how many items your array will contain, you can pass the array size as a parameter. For example, if you know you need an array with 20 items, you can create it like this:

var aValues = new Array(20);

This creates an array with 20 items, all initialized to the default value of null.

Part 2: Populating Array
Once you have created your Array object, you can populate it with values using bracket notation. This is similar to how it is done in Java. Here is an example:

var aColors = new Array();
aColors[0] = “red”;
aColors[1] = “green”;
aColors[2] = “blue”;

This creates an array called aColors with three values:

aColors[0] = “red”
aColors[1] = “green”
aColors[2] = “blue”

If you want to specify all the values at once, you can do so as follows:

var aColors = new Array(“red”, “green”, “blue”);

This creates the same array as above.

Part 3: Manipulating Array
Arrays in JavaScript dynamically grow in size with each additional item. You can add items to an array using the next open position, and the array will grow and shrink automatically. Here is an example:

var aColors = new Array(“red”, “green”, “blue”);
alert(aColors.length); //outputs “3”
aColors[3] = “purple”;
alert(aColors.length); //outputs “4”

In this code, the next open position is 3, so the value “purple” is assigned to that position. The length property is then updated to 4.

If you want to place a value in a position beyond the current length of the array, you can do so and ECMAScript will fill in the missing positions with null. For example:

var aColors = new Array(“red”, “green”, “blue”);
alert(aColors.length); //outputs “3”
aColors[25] = “purple”;
alert(aColors.length); //outputs “26”

In this code, the value “purple” is placed in position 25. Since the array only has 3 values, positions 3 through 24 are filled with null.

Part 4: Using Array Literals
Finally, you can also define an Array object by using the literal representation, which is indicated by using square brackets [] and separating the values with commas. For example:

var aColors = [“red”, “green”, “blue”];

This creates an array called aColors with the same values as in the previous examples.

In conclusion, the Array class in JavaScript is a powerful tool for storing and manipulating sets of data in your programs. By creating an Array object, populating it with values, and dynamically manipulating the array size, you can write code that is flexible and easy to work with.

Kitchen hygiene is important in preventing the spread of germs and contamination of food. If you handle raw poultry, meat or fish in the kitchen, it's essential to take steps to reduce the risk of foodborne illness. Here are some tips for reducing kitchen germs and keeping your food safe.

1. Wash your hands, utensils, containers and cooking vessels every time you handle raw poultry, meat or fish.

Raw meat, poultry and fish carry harmful bacteria such as E. coli, Salmonella and Listeria. Therefore, it is necessary to sanitize your hands, utensils, containers and cooking vessels thoroughly after handling these types of meats. Use soap, hot water and a scrub brush to wash your hands and utensils. Sanitize your containers and cooking vessels by washing them in a dishwasher or boiling them in water for at least five minutes.

2. Refrigerate or freeze perishable foods until you are ready to cook the foods.

Perishable foods like meats, eggs, dairy, fruits and vegetables need to be stored in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent bacteria growth and spoilage. Keep the temperature of your fridge below 40 degrees Fahrenheit (4.4 Celsius) to ensure safety.

3. Dispose of foods that don't smell or look fresh.

Fresh food should not have a bad odor or appearance. If it does, dispose of it immediately to avoid the risk of foodborne illness.

4. Scrub and wash utensils, cooking vessels, cutlery and cutting boards thoroughly with soap and water every time you use them.

Wash all of your utensils, cookware and implements every time they come into contact with raw meat or other potentially harmful foods. Use hot soapy water and a scrub brush to ensure that all surfaces are completely clean.

5. Disinfect countertops, cutting boards and the sink regularly with a bleach solution.

To ensure that surfaces are sanitized properly, mix a solution of one tablespoon of bleach in one gallon of water and spray it onto countertops, cutting boards and sink. Allow the solution to sit for ten minutes before rinsing with warm water and drying.

6. Boil marinade after marinating meat if you plan to use the marinade for basting or as a dip.

Marinades can contain harmful bacteria from raw meat. To make it safe to use marinade without cooking bacteria that may be present, boil it in a pot to kill any bacteria before using it.

7. Refrigerate raw fish, poultry and meat in a meat drawer to avoid contaminating foods with blood.

Raw meat requires special handling and storage to minimize the risk of contamination. A meat drawer in the fridge can help keep raw meat separate from other foods to prevent cross-contamination.

8. Seal refrigerated food in plastic containers or plastic wrap to keep out germs, blood and odors.

Plastic wrap or containers can protect refrigerated food and beverages from bacteria growth, while also preventing blood and odors from meat from spreading to other food items.

9. Cook all seafood, including fish, clams, oysters and mussels.

It's important to cook seafood thoroughly to kill any bacteria that might be present. Cook seafood until the internal temperature reaches 145 degrees Fahrenheit (63 Celsius).

10. Boil or cook eggs until the whites are firm and the yellow yolk begins to harden.

Undercooked eggs can contain harmful bacteria like Salmonella. Use a food thermometer to ensure cooked eggs reach a temperature of 160 degrees Fahrenheit (71 Celsius).

11. Keep food at its proper temperatures--either hot or cold--until just prior to serving.

When serving food to others, keep cold dishes cold and hot dishes hot to prevent bacterial growth and spoilage.

12. Avoid using sponges, which collect food particles and harbor germs.

While sponges are a cleaning staple, they are not ideal for sanitation. Stick with paper towels or washable dishcloths to wipe countertops and wash dishes.

13. Reduce kitchen germs by using clean towels and dishcloths.

Regularly launder towels and dishcloths or use disposable paper towels to minimize bacterial growth.

14. Empty the garbage daily to prevent disease-carrying insects or vermin.

Germs can thrive in items like garbage, so avoid necessary exposure by emptying waste containers as needed.

15. Clean spills in the refrigerator immediately.

Any liquid spills in the fridge can harbor bacteria and yeast, which can quickly spread to other foods.

16. Store dry foods like sugar, flour, cereal, crackers and cookies in plastic containers to discourage pests that may carry germs and parasites.

Prolong the shelf life of your pantry items by keeping things in sealed containers. This discourages mice, roaches and other insects from making a home in your food.

17. Check under the sink and other places for leaking water that may harbor germs.

Water can attract bacteria like mold, which can grow and spread quickly in dark, damp spaces. Ensure these areas are dry by cleaning up spills and leaks as soon as they occur.

18. Wait until the end of your shopping trip to buy food that requires refrigeration, including meat.

Shopping for perishable items is best left for the end of the trip. This allows you time to transport food immediately home to your refrigerator or freezer, reducing the risk of spoilage and contamination. 

When you follow these tips to reduce kitchen germs, you'll be well on your way to a safe and healthy kitchen.

If you're a fan of Tim Burton's portrayal of the Cheshire Cat from "Alice in Wonderland," you might be interested in making a Cheshire Cat costume of your own. With a bit of crafting and some basic sewing skills, it's possible to create a full body suit that captures the whimsical nature of this iconic feline. Follow these steps to make a Cheshire Cat costume body that looks like it's straight out of the world of Tim Burton.

Part 1 of 3: Gather Your Supplies for the Suit

Before you dive into making your Cheshire Cat costume body, you'll need to gather up the necessary supplies. Here's what you'll need:

- furry fabric in shades of purple and pink
- cheap fabric to use as a template
- sewing machine
- zipper
- scissors
- newspaper
- duct tape
- shoes you don't mind covering up
- black fabric paint
- toy stuffing
- black gloves
- black fur
- hot glue gun

Part 2 of 3: Prepare the Legs

One of the key features of a Cheshire Cat costume is the legs. You can opt for digitigrade legs, which require a bit more work but look more convincing, or non-digitigrade legs.

- Decide what you want your legs to look like. Digitigrade legs will require more work and involve creating a separate set of "shoes" to put over your feet.
- Cut around the outline you've made, leaving about a centimeter of extra fabric. If you're doing digitigrade legs, stop outlining at the top of your thighs.
- Sew along this line with your sewing machine.
- Turn the costume inside out and try it on to see how it fits.

Part 3 of 3: Add the Finishing Touches

With the legs taken care of, it's time to finish off your Cheshire Cat costume body. Here's what you need to do next:

- Cut out and sew the tail. Decide where you want your tail on your costume, and cut a slit as wide as your tail is seam side down. When you turn the suit inside out, you'll also turn the tail inside out. Sew the tail in place.
- Make claws for your gloves. Place your hand on your fur and outline it. Put the outlines on another piece of fabric, fur side in, and cut around your outline. Sew along the outline you made except for the wrist, where you'll put your hand in. Add claws if desired by sewing or gluing them along the edge of the gloves.
- Build your feet with newspaper. Cover your paw shape in duct tape. Rip out the newspaper from the duct tape. Cut the duct tape paw-shape into sections that are flat.
- Sew the claws onto the gloves like you did with the gloves.
- Turn the slipper fur-side out and if you wish, put your shoes inside the slipper. Stuff the slipper with toy stuffing to give it more shape. Cut out a piece of black fur or fabric to look like the bottom of the paw, and glue it onto the bottom of the slipper. Paint the bottom of the slipper with black fabric paint to mimic paw pads.

With these steps complete, you'll have a Cheshire Cat costume body that's sure to turn heads. Wear it to a costume party or Halloween celebration, and you're bound to get plenty of compliments on your handiwork!

How to Reduce the Stigma of Older Children, Teenagers, and Adults Wearing Diapers for Bedwetting'

Bedwetting is a common problem that affects many individuals, particularly children. However, when the problem persists into the teenage years or adulthood, it can become a source of embarrassment and shame. Wearing diapers to manage bedwetting can compound these negative feelings, leading to social isolation and stigma. Fortunately, there are steps you can take to reduce the stigma associated with wearing diapers for bedwetting.

Step 1: Change the definition of diaper

One of the first steps to reducing the stigma of wearing diapers for bedwetting is to change the language we use to describe them. Instead of referring to them as "diapers," consider using more neutral or positive terms, such as "protective underwear" or "incontinence products." These terms can help to normalize the use of these products and reduce the negative stigma associated with them.

Step 2: Have talk show hosts discuss bedwetting

Talk shows and other media outlets can play an important role in reducing the stigma of bedwetting and the use of protective underwear. By featuring guests who openly discuss their experiences with bedwetting and the use of protective products, these shows can help to break down barriers and encourage more open conversations about this issue.

Step 3: Ask celebrities to talk about their experiences with bedwetting

Celebrities can also play an important role in reducing the stigma of bedwetting. By sharing their own experiences with bedwetting and the use of protective products, they can help to break down social barriers and promote greater acceptance of those who need to use these products.

Step 4: Ask physicians to counsel patients about the different types of protective underwear available

Healthcare professionals such as urologists and other specialists can also play a critical role in reducing the stigma of wearing protective underwear for bedwetting. By counseling patients about the different products available and their benefits, healthcare providers can help to educate the public and promote greater acceptance of these products.

Step 5: Encourage authors of parenting books to have a positive view of protective underwear

The authors of parenting books can also have a significant impact on reducing the stigma of bedwetting and protective underwear. By adopting a positive and supportive view of protective products, these authors can help to reduce the negative associations that often accompany their use.

Step 6: Normalize the use of protective underwear for bedwetting

Finally, manufacturers of adult diapers and other protective products can help to reduce the stigma of bedwetting by advertising their products and increasing awareness of their availability. By increasing the visibility of these products, they can help to normalize their use and encourage greater acceptance among the general public. Additionally, parents can encourage stores to carry these products, ensuring their availability to those who need them most.

In conclusion, reducing the stigma of wearing diapers for bedwetting requires a concerted effort from multiple stakeholders, including healthcare providers, media outlets, celebrities, authors, and product manufacturers. By working together, we can help to create a more accepting and supportive environment for those who need to use these products to manage their bedwetting.

Have you ever wanted to give your furniture a glamorous update without spending a fortune? Silver leafing may be just what you need! With some patience and a few supplies, you can transform ordinary furniture into a stunning statement piece. Here are the steps you need to follow to silver leaf furniture.

1. Go to an online craft store or brick and mortar store to find all the supplies you will need for your refinishing. You will need silver leaf, gilding size, soft-bristled paintbrushes, clear coat sealer, and a primer or paint color.

2. Purchase a book of silver leaf. Make sure you buy enough to cover the entire surface of your furniture.

3. Opt to purchase aluminum leaf instead of silver leaf if you want to save money. Aluminum leaf can produce a similar effect at a lower cost.

4. Decide whether you want to silver leaf the entire piece of furniture or whether you want to paint some of the surfaces with silver spray paint. This will depend on your personal preference and the style of your furniture.

5. Buy 3-hour quick set gilding size. This type of size dries quickly, which makes it easier to handle.

6. Purchase a primer or a paint color. The primer will help the silver leaf adhere better to the surface of the furniture.

7. Buy soft bristled paintbrushes in large sizes in order to burnish the gold leaf. Burnishing is the process of smoothing out the silver leaf to create a shiny finish.

8. Get some clear coat sealer to protect the silver leaf from damage.

9. Strip the existing paint off of the piece of furniture if it is chipping away. You can use sandpaper or a chemical stripper.

10. Sand the surface of the furniture to create a smooth base for the primer.

11. Brush off the surface with a broom to ensure that it is free of dust.

12. Paint the surface with a grey primer. This will provide a good base for the silver leaf and help it to adhere properly.

13. Let the paint cure completely for a day or more before you start leafing. This is important to ensure that the surface is dry and ready for the silver leaf.

14. Paint the top surface of the furniture with three-hour quick set gilding size. Use a large brush to ensure an even coating.

15. Return when the allotted time is up. The size should be tacky to the touch, but not completely dry.

16. Hold the book of silver leaf with the spine near your palm. Position your hand at one corner of the surface you just set with gilding size.

17. Pick your hand up and turn to the next sheet of silver leaf. Carefully lay the silver leaf over the gilding size.

18. Repeat, tiling silver leaf all over the surface of the piece of furniture within three hours of painting on the size. It's important to work quickly to avoid the size drying out.

19. Take your very soft bristled painters brush and brush lightly along the surface. This will help to smooth out any bumps and create a shiny finish.

20. Gather some excess pieces of silver leaf and brush them into places where there are holes in the silver leaf. This will help to fill in any areas that are not completely covered.

21. Repeat on the other sides of the furniture until the entire piece is covered in silver leaf.

22. Choose a spray paint sealer for the easiest application. Spray the sealer according to package directions, but using a very gentle stroke. You don't want to dislodge any of the silver leaf.

23. Wait for the surface to cure completely before using the furniture. This may take a few days, but it's important to ensure that the sealer is fully dry.

With these simple steps, you can transform any piece of furniture into a stunning work of art. Just remember to be patient and work carefully to ensure the best results.

Replacing a window can seem like a daunting task, but if done carefully and with the right tools, it can be accomplished easily. Before beginning, make sure you have the correct measurements for your current window. Here's how to replace a window:

1. Measure the height of the existing window.
Measure from the bottom of the window frame to the top of the window frame. Write down this measurement.

2. Measure the width of the existing window.
Measure from one side of the window frame to the other. Write down this measurement.

3. Finally, check the squareness by measuring diagonally across the window at both sides.
Make sure the measurements across the window are the same. If they are not, you may need to make additional adjustments when installing the new window.

4. Know that if you buy a window that fits the existing window frame, you won't have to buy a whole new window frame.
This can save you both time and money. Make sure to measure your existing window carefully before purchasing a new one.

5. Remove the inside stop pieces from the right and left sides of the window.
These are the thin strips of wood that keep the window in place. Carefully remove them with a pry bar or hammer.

6. Take out the inside sash from the window frame.
Gently remove the inside sash from the window frame.

7. Slide the outside sash down to the bottom portion of the frame.
Slide the outside sash down until it's at the bottom of the frame.

8. Clean up the remaining window frame.
Remove any debris or old caulking from the window frame.

9. Double-check for rotting wood in the window frame.
If you notice serious rot or water damage, consider calling a professional for a quote on replacing the window frame and any surrounding structure.

10. Run a bead of caulk along the inner part of the outside stops on the jambs.
This will create a watertight seal for the new window.

11. Center both the inside and the outside sash vertically inside the window frame.
Adjust the sashes until they are centered vertically inside the window frame.

12. Place an expander on top of the window, caulking it (optional).
An expander is a piece of vinyl or aluminum that seals the gap between the top of the window and the frame.

13. Place the window in the frame, shimming as necessary.
Shims ensure that the window is level and plumb. Insert shims between the frame and the window as necessary.

14. Put in the mounting screws in each jamb.
Screw in the mounting screws through the sides of the window jamb and into the frame.

15. Expand the header so that it creates a seal between the top of the window and the old frame.
The header is a metal strip that fits over the top of the window and creates a seal.

16. Check to see that the windows work properly and don't contain any gaps.
Test the windows by opening and closing them. Make sure there are no gaps between the window and the frame.

17. Caulk the inside of the window and reattach the inside stops.
Apply a bead of caulk along the inside window jamb. Reattach the inside stop pieces with a hammer or pry bar.

Replacing a window can seem like a daunting task, but if you follow these steps carefully and patiently, you'll have a new window in no time.

Being your own Certificate Authority (CA) can be a useful skill for those interested in digital security. CAs are responsible for verifying the identity of websites and individuals, and issuing digital certificates to ensure secure communication and data transfer. By becoming your own CA, you can secure your own communication channels, as well as those of your organization. Here's how you can do it.

1. Generate your CA's private key

The first step in creating your own CA is to generate a private key. To do this, open a terminal window and issue the following command:

openssl genrsa -des3 -out server.CA.key 2048

The options explained:
- openssl: the name of the software
- genrsa: creates a new private key
- des3: encrypt the key using the DES cipher
- out server.CA.key: the name of your new key
- 2048: the length, in bits, of the private key

Store this certificate and the password in a safe place.

2. Create a certificate signing request (CSR)

The next step is to create a CSR for your CA. A CSR is a request for a digital certificate that includes information about your identity. To create a CSR, issue the following command:

openssl req -verbose -new -key server.CA.key -out server.CA.csr - sha256

The options explained:
- req: creates a signing request
- verbose: shows you details about the request as it is being created (optional)
- new: creates a new request
- key server.CA.key: the private key you just created

Fill out the information as much as possible, including your country name, state or province name, locality name, and organization name.

3. Self-sign your certificate

The next step is to self-sign your certificate using the private key you created in step 1. To do this, issue the following command:

openssl ca -extensions v3_ca -out server.CA-signed.crt -keyfile server.CA.key -verbose -selfsign -md sha256 -enddate 330630235959Z -infiles server.CA.csr

The options explained:
- ca: loads the Certificate Authority module
- extension v3_ca: loads the v3_ca extension, a must-have for use on modern browsers
- out server.CA-signed.crt: the name of your new signed key
- keyfile server.CA.key: the private key you created in step 1
- verbose: shows you details about the request as it is being created (optional)
- selfsign: tells openssl that you are using the same key to sign the request
- md sha256: the encryption algorithm to use for the message

4. Inspect your CA certificate

Once you have self-signed your certificate, you should inspect it to ensure it contains the correct information. To do this, issue the following command:

openssl x509 -noout -text -in server.CA.crt

5. Create a private key for an Apache Server

If you have an Apache server, the next step is to create a private key for it. To do this, issue the following command:

openssl genrsa -des3 -out server.apache.key 2048

The options explained:
- openssl: the name of the software
- genrsa: creates a new private key
- des3: encrypt the key using the DES cipher
- out server.apache.key: the name of your new key
- 2048: the length, in bits, of the private key

Store this certificate and the password in a safe place.

6. Create a CSR for the Apache Server

Once you have created a private key for your Apache server, the next step is to create a CSR. Issue the following command to create a CSR:

openssl req -verbose -new -key server.apache.key -out server.apache.csr - sha256

The options explained:
- req: creates a signing request
- verbose: shows you details about the request as it is being created (optional)
- new: creates a new request
- key server.apache.key: the private key you just created

Fill out the information as much as possible, including your country name, state or province name, locality name, and organization name.

7. Use your CA certificate to sign the new key

To use your CA certificate to sign the new key, issue the following command:

openssl ca -out server.apache.pem -keyfile server.CA.key -infiles server.apache.csr

The options explained:
- ca: loads the Certificate Authority module
- out server.apache.pem: the file name the signed certificate
- keyfile server.CA.key: the file name of the CA certificate that will be signing the request
- infiles server.apache.csr: the file name of the CSR

Fill out the information as much as possible, including your country name, state or province name, locality name, and organization name.

8. Save a copy of your private key in another location

As always, you should keep a copy of your private key in a safe and secure location.

9. Configure your Apache2.conf file

Finally, you can use the resulting server.apache.pem file along with the private key you generated in step 1 to configure your apache2.conf file. Follow all the steps in Creating SSL Certificates for Apache.

10. Convert your signed certificate to a PKCS12

You may also want to convert your signed certificate to a PKCS12 file format for distribution or use in other software. To do this, issue the following command:

openssl pkcs12 -export -in user_cert.pem -inkey user_private_key.pem -out user_cert.p12

11. Create a private key for email

If you want to secure your email communication, the next step is to create a private key for it. To do this, issue the following command:

openssl genrsa -des3 -out private_email.key 2048

12. Create a CSR for email

Once you have created a private key for your email, the next step is to create a CSR. Issue the following command to create a CSR:

openssl req -new -key private_email.key -out private_email.csr

Fill out the information as much as possible, including your country name, state or province name, locality name, and organization name.

13. Use your CA certificate to sign the new email key

To use your CA certificate to sign the new email key, issue the following command:

openssl ca -out private_email.pem -keyfile server.CA.key -infiles private_email.csr

Fill out the information as much as possible, including your country name, state or province name, locality name, and organization name.

14. Convert the certificate to PKCS12

You may also want to convert your email certificate to a PKCS12 file format for distribution or use in other software. To do this, issue the following command:

openssl pkcs12 -export -in private_email.crt -inkey private_email.key -out private_email.p12

15. Create a Public Key certificate for distribution

Finally, you may want to create a public key certificate for distribution. To do this, issue the following command:

openssl pkcs12 -export -out public_cert.p12 -in private_email.pem -clcerts -nokeys -name "WikiHow's Public Key"

By following these steps, you can become your own CA and ensure secure communication and data transfer for yourself and your organization.

Riding the subway in New York City can be an overwhelming experience, especially for first-time visitors. The subway system is vast, complex, and often crowded. However, with a little bit of preparation and guidance, you can navigate the subway like a pro. In this article, we will take you through the steps to ride the New York City subway like a local.

1. Get or use a computer and log on to the MTA website, look at the map, and find your departure and arrival stations.

Before you even leave your home or hotel, it is essential to plan your subway journey. You can use the MTA website or app to find your departure and arrival stations on the subway map. It's best to know which subway line(s) you need to use and any transfers you may need to make.

2. Make sure you have the appropriate fare on your MetroCard.

The most convenient way to pay for your subway fare is by using a MetroCard. You can buy a MetroCard from either the station agent, the MetroCard Vending Machines, or at various merchants scattered throughout the five boroughs. Ensure you have the right amount of money on your card to avoid any delays in getting to your destination.

3. Estimate the time it will take to arrive at your destination - by looking at the subway map or using the TripPlanner+.

The MTA's TripPlanner+ tool can be invaluable in helping you estimate how long your journey will take. You can input your start and end points, and the app will suggest the best routes, as well as provide an estimate of how long it should take.

4. Know what a station entrance looks like.

Each subway station has its unique entrance, and it can be helpful to know what it looks like before arriving. Most entrances are well marked, with the subway's iconic green and white signage and canopies.

5. At your departure station, ask a station agent, if one is available, for a map so that you have a portable guide.

Not all stations have a station agent, but if you happen to be at one that does, you can ask them for a map. These portable guides can be helpful in navigating your journey while on the subway.

6. Getting on the right train is hard for a tourist.

One of the most common mistakes tourists make is getting on an express train when they should have taken the local train. Be sure to double-check the train's destination before boarding.

7. Before boarding your train, wait for the disembarking passengers to fully egress before you enter the subway car.

Common courtesy dictates that you should wait for other passengers to exit the subway car before entering. This practice can help prevent any congestion and make everyone's travels more comfortable.

8. If you are wearing a bag or pack, remove it from your back or shoulder and carry it in your hands in front of you.

It's essential to be mindful of the space you're taking up on the subway. If you're carrying a backpack or a large bag, it's courteous to remove it from your back or shoulder and carry it in front of you to reduce your footprint.

9. If you want to sit, take the first available seat.

It's not uncommon to see subway passengers standing throughout their entire journey, but if you're in need of a seat, take the first available one. Just make sure to offer your seat to someone in need if they board the subway.

10. Avoid looking other passengers directly in the eye for more than an instant.

New Yorkers value their privacy, and staring at someone on the subway can make them uncomfortable. Be sure to avoid extended eye contact with other passengers.

11. Although asking for directions or help is perfectly fine, it's best not to talk to people you don't know.

While it's okay to ask someone for directions, be cautious of starting up a conversation with strangers in enclosed subway cars. You never know who may be having a bad day.

12. If you are accidentally short on change, step aside from the MetroCard machines and keep looking for change.

If you find that you're short on change while trying to buy a MetroCard, step aside from the machine and keep looking for change. Don't hold up other commuters or the line behind you.

13. If your MetroCard won't read for some reason, try the other turnstiles after several failed attempts on the first.

Sometimes MetroCards can become damaged or unreadable. If you're having trouble getting your MetroCard to work, try moving to another turnstile. If it still doesn't work, seek the help of a station agent.

14. If you are a tourist, get a city map.

Having a city map can be incredibly helpful when navigating the streets of New York City. Many maps show subway lines and can be used to help orient yourself.

15. Obtain a refillable MetroCard through a station MetroCard Vending Machine.

If you're planning on staying in New York for a while, consider obtaining a refillable MetroCard. These cards can be refilled with money and used indefinitely, making buying a new card unnecessary every time you use the subway.

16. Ask the station agent for a free subway map.

If you're at a station that has a station agent, you can ask for a free subway map. These maps can be very useful when navigating the subway system, and they're free!

17. Follow overhead signs for directions to the line you want.

Subway stations can be incredibly busy and confusing, but the overhead signs designate which lines are on a particular platform. Be sure to follow these signs to ensure you arrive at the right platform. 

Riding the New York City subway can be a daunting task, but by following these simple steps, you can navigate the system like a pro. Whether you're on vacation or commuting to work, the subway is an essential mode of transportation in New York City, and it's always worth taking the time to learn how to use it.

Have you ever considered becoming a podiatrist? Podiatrists are doctors who specialize in the diagnosis and treatment of conditions related to the foot and ankle. They help to keep people walking, exercising, and living a healthy, active life. If you want to become a podiatrist, there are several steps you need to follow. In this article, we'll guide you through each step of the process.

1. Take advanced placement classes before college.

To become a podiatrist, you'll need to first attend college. To prepare for this, it's a good idea to take advanced placement (AP) classes in high school. These classes will help you to earn college credits and get a head start on your college education. Some recommended AP classes include biology, chemistry, physics, and anatomy.

2. Complete a bachelor's degree in premed.

After high school, you'll need to complete a bachelor's degree in premed. This will prepare you for the rigorous curriculum that awaits you in podiatric medical school. You'll need to take classes in biology, chemistry, physics, and math.

3. Pass the Medical College Admission Test, also known as the MCAT.

Before you can apply to podiatric medical school, you'll need to pass the Medical College Admission Test (MCAT). This standardized test is used to assess your knowledge of the sciences and your ability to apply that knowledge to the field of medicine. A good score on the MCAT is essential for gaining admittance to podiatric medical school.

4. Find a college of podiatric medicine.

There are 9 accredited colleges of podiatric medicine in the US. These colleges have all been accredited by the Council on Podiatric Medical Education. While you may have to move to go to podiatric college, because of their limited number, these schools will give you the specialized education and experience that you will need to become a successful podiatrist.

5. Apply to podiatric college.

Once you've found a college of podiatric medicine, it's time to apply. You'll need to submit your transcripts, MCAT scores, and letters of recommendation. The admissions committee will review your application and make a decision.

6. Complete the requirements for your Doctor of Podiatric Medicine (DPM) degree.

The DPM degree is a four-year program that covers all aspects of podiatric medicine. You'll take classes in anatomy, physiology, pharmacology, and podiatric techniques. You'll also complete clinical rotations in hospitals and clinics.

7. Pass the first two parts of the National Board exams.

They are taken in two parts while in podiatric medical school. The first part, covering basic science, is usually taken at the end of the second year of podiatry school. This exam is designed to test your knowledge of the sciences and your ability to apply that knowledge to the field of podiatric medicine.

8. Complete a residency in podiatry.

After completing your DPM degree, you'll need to complete a residency in podiatry. This is a post-graduate program that provides you with hands-on training in a clinical setting. During your residency, you'll work with experienced podiatrists and other medical professionals.

9. Consider specialized training.

If you want to specialize in a particular area of podiatric medicine, such as sports medicine or orthopedics, you may need to complete additional training. This may involve completing a fellowship or additional coursework.

10. Pass the final part of the American Podiatric Medical Licensing Exam after completing your residency.

Once you've completed your residency, you'll need to pass the final part of the American Podiatric Medical Licensing Exam. This exam is designed to test your knowledge of podiatric medicine and your ability to apply that knowledge in a clinical setting. Once you've passed this exam, you'll be licensed to practice podiatric medicine.

Becoming a podiatrist requires dedication and hard work, but it can be a rewarding and fulfilling career. By following these steps, you'll be on your way to helping people maintain healthy feet and ankles for a lifetime.

Adding Glossy Condition to Any Type of Hair is something that can make any hair type look and feel amazing. Many people struggle with maintaining a healthy and smooth-looking head of hair, but with the right tips and tricks, anyone can achieve shiny, silky hair. Whether you have fine, thin hair, or thick, curly hair, the following steps can help you add a glossy condition to any type of hair.

1. Prepare Yourself

The first step in adding glossy condition to any type of hair is to prepare yourself. One great way to do this is to form a routine of showering in the afternoon or the morning if you have a lot of time, and allowing your hair to dry naturally. It's important to always start with clean and fresh hair for best results.

2. Comb Hair Before Washing

Before washing your hair, it's important to comb it to avoid nasty tangles and breakages. Use a wide-toothed comb or paddle brush to gently detangle your hair.

3. Start with Hot Water

Start the process with hot water - not scalding, however - and allow it to simply drench your hair and scalp. This helps to open up the hair cuticles and activate the shampoo and conditioner.

4. Shampoo Thoroughly

Shampoo hair thoroughly with a sulfate and sodium free shampoo. Massage the scalp and gently pull wefts of hair taut with shampoo on your fingers to achieve deep-down cleansing. This will help to remove any buildup and make your hair look and feel healthier.

5. Wash with Warm Water

After shampooing, wash your hair with warm water until the water runs clear. This will help to remove any residue and ensure that your hair is clean.

6. Condition with Care

Apply a little less conditioner than shampoo - Organix is a good brand - just to the tips (if your hair is oily), or to the mid-lengths downwards (if you have normal/dry hair). Remember, use a sulfate and sodium free conditioner. This will help to nourish and hydrate your hair without weighing it down.

7. Rinse with Cold Water

Rinse your hair with cold water. This helps to close the hair cuticles and lock in moisture, making your hair look shinier and smoother.

8. Pat Hair Dry

Pat your hair dry with a warm towel. Don't rub your hair vigorously with the towel as this can cause breakage and damage.

9. Apply Anti-Frizz Serum

Apply anti-frizz serum to your hair to keep it from becoming frizzy, even on the most humid of days. This will help to smooth your hair and give it a glossy finish.

10. Allow Your Hair to Dry Naturally

Allow your hair to dry naturally, or use a room fan to dry it. Face the fan so it is approximately 6 inches (15.2 cm) away from your face. Once your hair is dry, use a wide-toothed comb or paddle brush to brush it out.

11. Brush Before Sleeping

Brush your hair before sleeping to avoid tangles, but don't pull. It's also recommended to brush your hair again in the morning to smooth any kinks or waves that may have formed during the night.

12. Additional Tips

Stay away from chlorine pools, harmful UV/UVB rays, and chemical styling (perms and relaxers) if you can. Many people wash their hair every single day, but if you can, try washing every other day or every 3 days. Finally, get your hair trimmed regularly to avoid split ends and maintain the health of your hair.

In conclusion, adding a glossy condition to any type of hair is achievable with the right tips and tricks. By following these steps, you can have a head of shiny, smooth, and healthy-looking hair.

How to Sue for Defamation: A Step-by-Step Guide

If someone has made a false statement about you that has caused harm to your reputation, you may have grounds to sue for defamation. Defamation refers to a false statement that causes damage to a person's reputation. If you decide to pursue a defamation lawsuit, there are several steps you need to take to make your case. Here's how to sue for defamation:

1. Analyze the statement

Carefully scrutinize the statement to ensure that it was, in fact, false. You cannot sue someone for defamation if the statement was true.

2. Prove that the statement was published

You need to show that the statement was communicated to someone other than you. This could be through spoken or written words, such as email or website posts.

3. Prove the statement was false

Evidence must be presented that proves the statement is false beyond a reasonable doubt. Without this proof, your case cannot succeed.

4. Prove that the statement caused injury

If the statement is in itself untrue, it needs to be proven that it caused harm to your reputation and caused you to suffer some form of injury.

5. Prove “special damages”

For slander cases specifically, “special damages” must be proven. These refer to damages that can be quantified, such as lost earnings or lost future earnings.

6. Determine if the statement is protected by “absolute privilege”

In some legal situations, people are granted immunity from defamation lawsuits. A successful defense of absolute privilege can make or break a defamation case.

7. Determine if the statement is protected by “qualified privilege.”

Similarly, people are granted a right to make particular statements under certain circumstances. A statement protected by qualified privilege can serve as a defense against a defamation claim.

8. Inform the publisher and request a retraction

It may be possible to resolve the matter without going to court by requesting the party that made the false statement to retract it.

9. Meet with an attorney to discuss your case

An experienced attorney can help you understand the strengths and weaknesses of your case and can guide you through the legal process.

10. Consider Alternative Dispute Resolution

Alternative dispute resolution (ADR) can provide a way to resolve the matter without going to court. This could include methods like mediation or arbitration.

11. Consider Arbitration

In some cases, arbitration may be mandatory. It can be beneficial to hire an attorney to help you navigate the process.

12. Fill out a defamation complaint and file your lawsuit

If all other options fail, you can file a complaint to begin the legal process of a defamation lawsuit.

13. Have the defendant served with a copy of the complaint

After filing your defamation complaint, you will need to have the defendant served with a copy of the complaint to begin the legal process.

14. Negotiate a settlement, if possible

The parties may be able to come to an agreement regarding a settlement amount that will allow both parties to move forward without proceeding to court.

15. Go to court if necessary

If a settlement cannot be reached, you may need to go to court to have a judge or jury determine whether the defendant is guilty of defamation and the amount of damages you are entitled to.

By following these steps, you can assert your legal right to sue for defamation and protect your reputation.

Making moist and delicious banana bread is easier than you think, especially with these easy-to-follow steps. From preparing the ingredients to baking the finished loaf, this guide will show you how to make the perfect, moist banana bread every time.

Part 1: Gather Ingredients

Before you start making banana bread, make sure you have all of the necessary ingredients. Here's what you'll need:

- 3 ripe bananas, mashed
- 1/3 cup melted butter
- 1 tsp baking soda
- Pinch of salt
- 3/4 cup sugar
- 1 large egg, beaten
- 1 tsp vanilla extract
- 1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour

Part 2: Preheat and Grease

Preheat your oven to 350°F and grease a 9-inch loaf pan with a tablespoon of butter.

Part 3: Combine Wet Ingredients

In a medium sized mixing bowl, mix the mashed bananas and melted butter together. Add in the baking soda and salt and mix well. Then, stir in the sugar, beaten egg, and vanilla extract until well combined.

Part 4: Mix Dry Ingredients

In a separate medium sized mixing bowl, mix flour, salt, cinnamon and baking powder together.

Part 5: Combine Mixtures

Add in the dry ingredients to the wet mixture slowly, making sure to mix it well between each addition. Stir until the mixture is well combined and there are no lumps.

Part 6: Bake the Banana Bread

Pour the mixture into the greased 9-inch loaf pan. Put the pan into the oven and bake for about 45 to 60 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean. Remove the pan from the oven and let it cool for 10 minutes. Once it’s cooled, slice and serve.

Part 7: Alternative Recipes

If you want to try something different with your banana bread, try one of these alternative recipes:

- Almond Marzipan Banana Bread: Prepare the marzipan and then add it to the flour mixture. Mix the butter/sugar mixture with the flour mixture and stir it up until well combined. Put the pan into the oven and bake for about 45 to 60 minutes. Cool the banana bread by taking out the pan and sitting it on the stove or cooling rack for 10 minutes. Once it’s cooled, slice and serve.
- Gluten-Free Banana Bread: Add baking powder, almond meal, cinnamon, salt and brown rice flour to the banana mixture, then stir together to combine. Pour the mixture into the 9-inch loaf pan and bake for 45 to 50 minutes. Allow the bread to cool for 15 minutes before serving, then remove it from the pan.
- Vegan Banana Bread: While preheating the oven to 350°F, cover the bottom of a 9-inch loaf pan with coconut oil. Mix flax meal and water together in a medium sized bowl, then let the mixture sit for five minutes until it thickens. In a large bowl, whisk the flour, salt and baking soda together. Add the oil flax/water combination to the mixture in the medium bowl. Pour the batter into the oiled 9-inch pan and bake for 20-25 minutes. Once the banana bread is finished baking, leave it on the rack to cool for 5-10 minutes.

With these easy-to-follow steps and alternative recipes, you can make delicious and moist banana bread in no time. Enjoy it on its own or with your favorite topping. Happy baking!

How to Complete a High School Logical Proof

Completing a logical proof can be daunting, especially in a high school classroom setting where the pressure to do well is high. But don't worry! With some basic knowledge and practice, you can become a logical proof pro. Here's how:

1. Learn your logical connectives (including the negation statement).
Logical connectives are the building blocks of logical proofs. They include "and," "or," "if-then," and "not." Understanding the meanings of these connectives is crucial to creating a valid argument.

2. Learn how to interpret the signs used in what can later be called a logical proof.
Most logical proofs are presented in a two column format with statements on one side and reasons on the other, connected by various logical connectives. Understanding how to read and interpret these columns is key to being able to complete a proof successfully.

3. Define for yourself the definition of a tautology.
A tautology is a statement that is always true, no matter the values of the variables involved. Knowing the definition of a tautology is helpful because any logical statement that can be reduced to a tautology is automatically considered true.

4. Realize that all statements made in a logical proof will end up becoming a logically-equivalent statement (or a statement that is always assumed to be true no matter what condition it ends up being at the end).
This means that every statement you make in your logical proof must be carefully considered for accuracy and logical consistency.

5. Realize that at least two given premises make up a good logical argument that can lead to one and only one conclusion.
In other words, a valid logical proof requires at least two given statements, known as premises, that lead to a single, valid conclusion.

6. Learn the many laws that can be used to prove the answer to a given proof.
There are many laws, rules, and formulas that can be used within logical proofs, such as the distributive law, modus ponens, and modus tollens. Familiarize yourself with them through studying and practice.

7. Produce a two-column format.
Set up your proof by creating a standard two-column format, with the statements on the left and the reasons on the right.

8. Look at your proof-premises you must prove.
Read carefully the given premises you are required to prove in your proof.

9. Write down each of the two given statements.
List out the two premises you are given to work with on the left-hand column of your two-column format.

10. Write down for these given reasons (in the Reasons column), the reason for writing down these items.
In the right-hand column, write down your reasons for including each statement. For example, if the first premise is "All cats are mammals," your reason would be "Given: All cats are mammals."

11. Use each law as you read about earlier, to try to deduce a new fact that can lead you to a final answer.
Take a look at the premises you've been given and use the logical laws and rules you've learned to come up with new statements that can help lead you to the conclusion.

12. Write down the law you used to deduce the fact as the Reason given in the Reasons column.
As you introduce new statements, add them to the left-hand column and provide the reason you were able to deduce the statement in the right-hand column, citing the law or rule you used.

13. Understand the definition of what a valid conclusion is.
A conclusion is only considered valid if it is a logical consequence of the premises given. In other words, it must follow logically from the statements you have already made.

14. Make sure that you arrive at the same answer the question-proof asked you to arrive at.
Before submitting your proof, double-check that your final conclusion makes logical sense and fits the criteria of the question prompt.

By following these steps and practicing regularly, you'll soon become a master at completing high school logical proofs.

Have you ever needed to manually build GNU Compiler Collection (GCC) from scratch on a Linux Mint Static Edition? If so, this guide is for you! This process will allow you to have a portable version of GCC for use on other machines or for sharing with others. In order to complete the build, you'll need to download and install several libraries and packages. Here's how to get started:

1. Put the downloads in a temp directory (you can use whatever directory you want) for example, /home/”your_username”/gcc_archive.

2. Build the infrastructure in a temp directory that is different than the downloads directory or its sub directories: /tmp/gcc.

3. Configure the infrastructure using static libraries like this: ./configure --disable-shared --enable-static --prefix=/tmp/gcc. The --disable-shared flag may be worth a closer look depending on your needs.

4. Open up a terminal and enter the following command: mkdir gcc_archive. Download and place all GMP, MPFR, MPC, ELF, and GCC packages in this directory.

5. Install the necessary packages to set up a proper build environment by typing/copying/pasting: sudo apt-get install binutils build-essential m4 autogen bison flex.

6. Install GMP (GNU Multiple Precision Arithmetic Library) by typing/copying/pasting the following commands into your terminal:
- cd gcc_archive
- wget -c ftp://ftp.gnu.org/gnu/gmp/gmp-5.1.3.tar.bz2
- chmod a+x gmp-5.1.3.tar.bz2
- tar jxvf gmp-5.1.3.tar.bz2
- cd gmp-5.1.1
- ./configure --disable-shared --enable-static --prefix=/tmp/gcc
- make && make check && make install
- cd ..

7. Install MPFR (GNU Multiple-precision floating-point rounding library), MPC (GNU Multiple-precision C library), ELF (stands for Executable and Linkable Format), and GCC (GNU Compiler Collection). To install these, type/copy/paste the following commands into your terminal:
- wget -c http://ftp.gnu.org/gnu/gcc/gcc-4.8.1/gcc-4.8.1.tar.bz2
- chmod a+x gcc-4.8.1.tar.gz
- tar zxvf gcc-4.8.1.tar.gz

8. Note: build gcc in a scratch directory on the same mount point. Once everything is complete, the new portable GNU GCC will be located in /tmp/gcc. Just change into your /tmp directory and move your new portable GNU GCC to /home/"your_username"/ directory.

Congratulations! You've successfully built GNU Compiler Collection from scratch on Linux Mint Static Edition. This will allow you to have a portable version of GCC for use on other machines or for sharing with others.

UGG boots are a popular winter accessory that can keep you cozy and stylish. However, they can also be a nightmare to clean. Here's a guide on how to clean Ugg boots, step-by-step.

Part One: Brushing the Boots
1. Use a suede brush to comb the outside of the boots. Start by brushing the boots gently in one direction, then switch to a back-and-forth motion to remove any dirt or debris.
2. Brush the boots as described in the previous part. Be sure to brush the entire boot, including the sole and the wooly part.

Part Two: Cleaning and Drying the Boots
1. Wet the outside surface of the boots. Use a damp cloth to wet the entire boot, being careful not to soak it.
2. Squeeze a small amount of cleaning product onto a damp sponge. Use a cleaner specifically designed for Ugg boots.
3. Use the sponge to work the cleaning product into the surface of the boots. Be sure to cover every part of the boot, paying special attention to any stains or discoloration.
4. Rinse the boots off. Use a damp cloth to remove all of the cleaner from the boots.
5. Stuff the boots with newspaper or paper towel. This will help the boots maintain their shape as they dry.
6. Wait 24 to 48 hours for the Uggs to dry. Do not use direct heat to dry the boots.
7. Add the finishing touches. Brush the boots into top shape again, and add protectant if desired.

Part Three: Alternate Cleaning Methods
1. Realize that this method is not recommended by the manufacturers, as there is a potential for damaging the boots. Only use this method as a last resort.
2. Place the Ugg boots into a pillowcase. Tie the pillowcase closed.
3. Put the washing machine onto the wool cycle. Use a minimal amount of detergent.
4. Remove from the washing machine. Roll the boots gently in a towel to remove excess water. Do not twist or wring the boots.
5. Brush into top shape again. Be sure to brush in one direction.
6. Be very careful with other types of Ugg boot. Not all Ugg boots are made of the same materials, and some may require different cleaning methods.
7. Clean such Uggs by simply wiping them gently, in one direction.
8. Use chalk to remove oil and grease stains. Simply rub the chalk onto the stain, let it sit for several minutes, and then wipe away with a clean cloth.
9. Use an eraser to remove dirt and salt stains. Gently rub the eraser over the stain to remove it.
10. Remove water spots. Dampen the entire boot with a cloth, then use a suede brush to fluff up the wet area.
11. Comb the wooly part to remove debris. Use a fine-toothed comb to gently remove debris from the wooly part of the boot.
12. Remove odors with baking soda. Sprinkle baking soda inside the boots, then let them sit for several hours before shaking out the excess powder.
13. Limit your Ugg use. The less you wear your Ugg boots, the less you'll have to clean them.
14. Clean the boots by hand. Using a damp cloth and gentle cleaner, clean the boots by hand, following the same steps as above.
15. Invest in a care kit. Ugg makes a care kit specifically designed to clean and protect their boots.
16. Test for color fastness. Before cleaning your Ugg boots, test a small, inconspicuous area to make sure the cleaner won't damage the color of the boots.
17. Never dry using direct heat. This can cause the boots to shrink, warp, or become discolored.

Backpacks are a great way to carry your belongings while on-the-go. Why not make your own that is both stylish and durable? This article will guide you through the steps of creating your very own backpack with the following instructions.

Part 1: Cutting Out The Pieces

4.	Turn the flap right-side-out and press it flat with an iron, then topstitch the edges of the flap for a clean finish.
