Starting up a drum circle can be a fun and energizing way to build community while making music. Here's how to get it going!

1. Get some drums and other percussion instruments.
To start a drum circle, you'll need instruments! Gather some hand drums like djembes, congas, or bongos, as well as shakers, rattles, and other percussion toys. You can purchase or rent instruments, or even make your own!

2. Steer away from electronics.
While electronic drums and instruments can be cool, keep the focus on acoustic instruments for this kind of community gathering.

3. Get enough instruments for one to five people, or more.
Start with enough instruments for a small group, but as interest grows, make sure you have extras, so everyone can join in. 

4. Don't forget the obvious: a "drum circle" is a circle!
Find a space where everyone can sit in a circle, facing each other. This sets the tone for community collaboration from the start.

5. Create circles within circles once the circle is bigger than 20 participants.
As your group grows, create smaller circles within the main circle. This helps everyone feel included and connected.

6. Find a nice outdoor location for your drum circle, like a big backyard, or a nearby park so people from the public can join in.
Drum circles are often outdoor events, so find a location with plenty of space to accommodate your group, as well as anyone who wants to stop by and join in.

7. Always welcome those who walk in and want to join the fun.
Drum circles are all about inclusion, so greet newcomers with open arms and show them how to join in.

8. Go indoors if it is going to be chilly, or wet, or dark.
If the weather turns bad, move your drum circle indoors. Find a space with good acoustics, like a yoga studio or community center.

9. Have at least one person who has a little experience, so he/she can start the beats and/or maintain a steady motion.
Designate one person to lead the group -- someone with some drumming experience who can keep the rhythm going.

10. Understand that rhythms are spontaneous, one person starts a beat or a rhythm then someone else adds on to it, so on and so forth.
Drum circles are all about collaboration and improvisation. Start with a basic rhythm and let everyone build on it organically.

11. Start off with slow beats and vibes, eventually the drum circle will rise with adrenaline but you have to let it happen, don't force it.
As the group gets warmed up, the rhythm will build and evolve naturally. Don't rush things, and let the energy flow.

12. Don't be shy or timid, drum circles are supposed to be fun.
Relax and have fun! There's no right or wrong way to drum.

13. Be friendly and admire each other's attempts at making music.
Drum circles are all about positivity and encouragement. Support each other and lift each other up.

14. Play friendly and supportive, don't get involved in competitive or aggressive playing.
There's no room for ego in a drum circle. Play from the heart and support the collective sound.

15. Remember that we all share the space with our neighbors!
Be mindful of the people and spaces around you. Keep the volume and energy level appropriate for your surroundings. 

With these tips, you're well on your way to starting your own drum circle!

Fostering a child can be a rewarding experience, but it also requires a lot of patience, empathy and respect. As a foster parent, it's essential to treat your foster child with dignity, kindness and compassion, while also making sure that they feel equally valued and included in your family.

In this article, we will discuss some practical tips that can help you foster parent with respect, and provide a safe and nurturing environment for the child in your care.

1. Let Friends and Family Know
Before welcoming a new child into your family, it's important to inform your friends and family members in advance. Let them know that you are fostering a child and that you expect them to treat the child equally. Encourage them to get involved in welcoming the child and making them feel included.

2. Treat Them Equally
Make sure that you provide the same opportunities, incentives, and privileges to your foster child that you would provide to your biological child. This includes things like birthday celebrations, holiday gifts, family outings, and other special events.

3. Let Them Know Their Parents Loved Them
It's important to reassure your foster child that their birth parents loved them to the best of their ability, and that it's not their fault that they are in foster care. Encourage them to talk about their feelings, and provide a safe space for them to express their emotions and concerns.

4. Act as If You Made a Choice to Support Them
Don't treat your foster child as if you are doing them a favor by providing them with food, shelter, and love. Instead, act as if you made a conscious choice to support them, and that they are a valued member of your family. This will help them feel more secure and less like a burden.

5. Let Them Know They Are Normal
Make sure that your foster child knows that they are normal, and that you have normal expectations and consequences for them. Avoid labeling them as "foster kids" or making them feel like they are different from your biological children.

6. Teach Them Life Skills
Teach your foster child important life skills, such as cooking, cleaning, budgeting, and self-care. This will help them feel more independent and capable, and prepare them for life outside of foster care.

7. Don't Exclude Them from Family Pictures
Make sure that your foster child is included in family pictures and other important family events. This will help them feel like they belong and are valued.

8. Don't Give Insulting Gifts
Avoid giving your foster child generic or insulting gifts for birthdays or holidays, while spoiling your biological children with expensive gifts. This will make your foster child feel excluded and undervalued.

9. Foster for the Right Reasons
Become a foster parent because you realize that a foster child is in desperate need of food, clothing, shelter, as well as love, consistency, expectations, and to be treated fairly. Don't become a foster parent simply because you want to fulfill a personal desire or because you feel pressured to do so.

10. Give Them Time to Transition and Trust
Remember that your foster child has likely been through trauma and may need time to transition, bond, and trust. Don't take their pain, tragedy, and mistrust personally, and give them the space and support they need to heal.

11. Don't Expect Perfection
As a foster parent, don't expect perfection from yourself, your foster child, or the foster care system. Understand that there will be challenges and setbacks along the way, and focus on providing a safe and loving home for your foster child.

12. Respect Their Intelligence and Emotions
Finally, don't underestimate the intelligence and raw emotion hiding in your foster child. Treat them with respect, kindness, and empathy, and provide them with the support and love they need to thrive.

Aquaponics is a combination of aquaculture and hydroponics that allows you to grow plants and raise fish at the same time. Not only is it great for the environment, but it also produces fresh and healthy food for your home. Here's how you can make your own indoor aquaponics system using items from IKEA.

Materials:

- Frame (IKEA RÅSKOG or similar)
- Wire basket (IKEA KNAPPER or similar)
- 25 liter (6.6 US gal) plastic container
- Small 600 lph electric submersible pump
- Male and female threaded adapters
- 25mm-13mm reducer
- 60mm bell siphon
- 100mm media guard
- Ball-valve by-pass
- Growing media (clay pebbles, gravel, or similar)
- Fish (goldfish, tilapia, or similar)
- Plants (lettuce, herbs, or similar)

Instructions:

1. Visit IKEA to purchase the frame. Look for a sturdy and durable frame that can hold the weight of the growing media and water.
2. Use the wire basket as support for the 25 liter plastic container that will house the growbed. The container should fit snugly inside the wire basket and be able to hold the growing media.
3. If you want to personalize the system to fit in with your home décor, now is a good time to do it. Paint or decorate the frame and container to match your style.
4. Use a small 600 lph electric submersible pump in one corner of the fish tank which takes the water up to the growbed. The pump should be placed lower than the growbed to allow the water to flow back down.
5. Obtain male and female threaded adapters. Attach the female adapter to the pump and the male adapter to the top of the growbed.
6. Place the male adapter through the top of the growbed. Make sure it is centered and secure.
7. Observe the 25mm-13mm reducer on the far left of the photo shown below. Attach the 25mm side to the male adapter and the 13mm side to the 60mm bell siphon.
8. Place the 60mm bell siphon in the middle. The bell siphon should be placed higher than the growbed and the 25mm-13mm reducer.
9. Finally, the 100mm media guard, shown on the far right, is simply to keep the growbed media out of the bell siphon. Attach it to the top of the bell siphon.
10. Bell siphons can be tricky to get working. Check online resources or consult an expert for troubleshooting tips if it's not working.
11. Add the ball-valve by-pass. This can help control the flow of water in case the bell siphon fails.
12. Once you have all the framework, the containers, and the plumbing set up, add water into the fish tank and start the pump up. The water will flow through the system, providing nutrients to the plants and oxygenating the water for the fish.
13. Fill the top container (the growbed) with some sort of growing media. You can use clay pebbles, gravel, or another growing medium that is suitable for aquaponics.
14. Once this has been done, you are ready to add the fish and to start putting plants into your system. Follow the guidelines provided for the specific fish and plants you choose.
15. Read up on aquaponics for more details. Do some research to learn more about this sustainable system and how to take care of it properly.

With some creativity and the right materials, you can make a simple and effective indoor aquaponics system from IKEA products. Not only will you have fresh produce at your fingertips, but you'll also be doing your part for the planet. Give it a try and see how it works for you!

Renovating a bathroom can be a daunting task, but with proper planning and preparation, it can be an exciting DIY project. Whether you're looking to give your bathroom a complete facelift or a simple upgrade, there are a few key things to keep in mind. Follow these steps to renovate your bathroom like a pro.

Part 1 of 3: Planning

1. Decide how you want the bathroom to look like.
Before you begin any renovation work, decide on the overall look and style that you want to achieve. Browse magazines, catalogs, and online resources for inspiration and ideas. Create a vision board or a Pinterest board to help you visualize your ideal bathroom.

2. Plan a budget.
Renovating a bathroom can be expensive, so it's important to plan a budget before you start any work. Consider the cost of materials, labor, permits, and any unexpected expenses that may arise. Be realistic about what you can afford and adjust your plans accordingly.

3. Think about how much work needs to be done, and what sort of work.
Assess the condition of your bathroom and determine what needs to be updated or replaced. Do you need new fixtures, new flooring, or a complete renovation? Make a list of everything that needs to be done, and prioritize your tasks based on the most urgent needs.

4. Decide how much time and effort your want to spend on your bathroom.
Be realistic about the amount of time and effort you want to put into your bathroom renovation. If you're short on time or don't have the skills to tackle certain tasks, consider hiring a professional. On the other hand, if you're a DIY enthusiast, you may want to take on more of the work yourself.

5. Consider asking a professional designer for help.
A professional designer can help you create a cohesive look for your bathroom and make sure that your renovation meets all building codes and safety standards. They can also help you choose the right materials, colors, and fixtures to achieve your desired look.

6. Know when you need to hire a contractor or trained professionals.
Some aspects of bathroom renovation may require the help of a contractor or trained professionals, such as plumbing or electrical work. Make sure to hire reputable and licensed professionals to ensure that your renovation is safe and up to code.

Part 2 of 3: Shopping and Preparing

7. Make sure that your new bathroom meets building codes while still being comfortable.
Before you start purchasing materials for your bathroom renovation, make sure that your plans meet all local building codes and safety regulations. You don't want to invest time and money into a renovation only to have to redo it because of code violations.

8. Take advantage of the space in a master bathroom.
If you have a larger bathroom, consider using the extra space to add features like double vanities, a soaking tub, or a separate shower and bathtub. Make sure to plan your layout carefully and consider all the features you want to add.

9. Have a backup bathroom.
If you only have one bathroom, consider setting up a temporary bathroom to use while you renovate. This can be as simple as setting up a portable toilet and a shower in another room or outside.

10. Take measurements of everything before you go shopping.
You will need to know the exact side of your bathroom, including the width, length, and height. This will help you decide what fixtures and materials will fit in your space and prevent you from making costly mistakes.

11. Choose slip-free, non-absorbent flooring.
Choose a flooring material that is slip-free and non-absorbent, such as porcelain tile or vinyl plank. These materials are easy to clean and maintain and are less likely to be damaged by moisture or humidity.

12. Choose moisture and mildew-resistant paint.
In a high-moisture environment like a bathroom, it's important to choose a paint that is specifically designed to resist mildew and moisture. These paints are formulated to prevent mold and mildew growth and help keep your bathroom looking fresh and clean.

13. Decide what sort of material you want for your counter.
There are a variety of materials to choose from for your bathroom counter, including natural stone, quartz, and laminate. Consider your budget, aesthetic preferences, and maintenance requirements when choosing your countertop material.

14. Choose your bathtub, sinks, showers, and other fixtures.
Choose fixtures that fit your style and meet your needs. For example, if you have young children or older adults in your home, consider a walk-in bathtub or grab bars for added safety.

15. Choose storage that is both efficient and stylish.
In a small bathroom, storage is essential. Look for shelving, cabinets, and organizers that maximize your space and help you keep your bathroom clutter-free. Don't forget to consider the style and color of your storage solutions to ensure that they fit in with your overall design.

16. Make sure you have adequate lighting in your bathroom.
A well-lit bathroom is essential for both safety and aesthetic reasons. Consider adding task lighting around your vanity, and install overhead lighting that is both functional and stylish.

17. Make sure that you have adequate ventilation.
Proper ventilation is important in a bathroom to prevent mold and mildew growth and to keep your bathroom smelling fresh. Consider installing an exhaust fan or opening a window to increase airflow.

18. Pick out some new accessories to match your new bathroom.
Once your renovation is complete, don't forget to add the finishing touches with stylish and functional bathroom accessories. Look for items like bath mats, shower curtains, and soap dispensers that complement your new bathroom design.

Part 3 of 3: Renovation

19. Switch off all water valves if you are going to do anything to the sink, bathtub, shower, or toilet.
Before you start any plumbing work, make sure to turn off the water supply to your bathroom to prevent any accidents or water damage.

20. Cover anything that isn't getting renovated with plastic or paper to protect it.
Cover your floors, furniture, and other items with plastic or paper to protect them from dust, debris, and paint.

21. Get rid of anything that you will be replacing.
Remove any old fixtures, cabinets, or flooring that you will be replacing to make room for your new items.

22. Start by painting your bathroom.
Painting is a simple and relatively inexpensive way to update your bathroom. Start by painting the walls and ceiling, choosing a color that complements your fixtures and design scheme.

23. Add tile or new flooring once the paint has dried.
After your paint has dried, add new tile or other flooring materials to your bathroom. This will help add texture and depth to your design and make your bathroom feel like a brand new space.

24. Install any toilets, sinks, tubs, and showers.
Install your new fixtures, starting with the larger items like toilets, sinks, tubs, and showers. Make sure to follow all instructions carefully and pay attention to any safety precautions.

25. Install any new cabinets, shelves, cabinets, and towel rods.
After your fixtures are installed, add new storage solutions like cabinets and shelves. These will help keep your bathroom organized and clutter-free.

26. Install new lights and faucets.
Once all your larger items are installed, add new lights and faucets to complete your bathroom renovation.

27. Clean any dust, paint, or debris.
After your renovation is complete, clean your bathroom thoroughly to remove any dust, paint, or debris. This will help ensure that your new bathroom is sparkling clean and ready to use.

Making your own kitten food can be a great way to ensure that your furry friend is getting the best possible nutrition. While it may seem daunting at first, by following a few simple steps, you can create a delicious and nutritious meal that your kitten will love.

Part 1: Preparing the Protein

1. Purchase the main protein product. The main protein source for your kitten food will be a combination of rabbit and poultry meat. You will need to purchase 3 pounds of raw muscle meat, 14 ounces of raw heart, and 7 ounces of raw liver.

2. Remove half of the skin from the meat. You can leave some skin on for added flavor, but too much can be harmful to your kitten's health.

3. Cut the raw muscle meat into chunks. Ensure that they are small enough for your kitten to eat comfortably.

4. Grind the liver, non-chunked meat, and heart. You can use a meat grinder or a food processor to do this.

5. Thaw the rabbit meat and mix in the ground and chunked poultry meat. Ensure that everything is well mixed.

6. Bake the poultry. Bake the poultry until cooked through.

7. Cut the poultry and liver into chunks about the size of a die (half-inch cubes or larger). Ensure that everything is cut into bite-sized pieces.

Part 2: Adding Supplements

1. Purchase supplements. You will need to buy 5,000 - 10,000 mg fish oil, vitamin additives, some simple table salt, a source of fiber.

2. Prepare 16 ounces (2 cups) of water and 3.08 tablespoons (9.25 teaspoons) of bone meal. Add the supplemental ingredients to the water.

3. Mix up the supplemental ingredients including vitamins into the water. Ensure that everything is well mixed.

4. Use the refrigerator for defrosting. Defrost the supplements in the refrigerator.

5. Ready 2 tablespoons of unflavored gelatin and 4 raw egg yolks. Beat the egg yolks and gelatin together until well mixed.

6. Prepare a supplement solution. Combine the supplement water and the egg yolk mixture and stir.

7. Add a portion of chicken liver. Ensure that the liver is cut into small pieces.

8. Add a source of fiber. You can use a supplement at this point or use vegetables such as sweet potatoes.

Part 3: Mixing the Batches

1. Mix all three batches. Combine the protein batch, supplement solution, and fiber batch together. Ensure that everything is well mixed.

2. Set up your freezer containers correctly. Divide the mixture into small containers that can be easily frozen.

3. Freeze the kitten food. Keep the kitten food in the freezer until you are ready to use it.

By following these simple steps, you can create your own delicious and nutritious kitten food that your furry friend will love. Ensure that you feed your kitten the correct portion sizes to prevent overfeeding. Enjoy!

Are you ready to step into a world of Victorian elegance, science fiction, and punk aesthetic? Dressing up in steampunk fashion is not just for cosplayers or costume parties, it's a fun and unique way to express your creativity and personality. With a little bit of planning and some inspiration, you can create a steampunk outfit that will turn heads and make you feel like a character from your favorite science fiction novel. 

1. Imagine a character you want to be 

The first step in planning out a successful steampunk character is to think up a vibrant, interesting character you want to dress as. Are you a daring inventor, a steampunk warrior, or a Victorian adventurer? Once you have an idea of your character, it will be easier to plan out your outfit and add accessories to make it more unique. 

2. Begin with a Victorian outfit and add from there 

Steampunk fashion is essentially a science fiction take on old Victorian elegance. Start with a Victorian outfit, such as a high-neck blouse, long skirt, or tailored suit, and add steampunk elements like gears, cogs, and brass accents. You can also incorporate fabrics like leather, lace, or burlap to give your outfit a rough, industrial feel. 

3. Include some punk aesthetic in your costume 

Steampunk is not just about Victorian elegance, it's also about rebellion and punk aesthetic. Add some punk attitude to your costume with accessories like spiked jewelry, combat boots, or a leather jacket. Don't be afraid to mix and match different styles to create a unique and eclectic steampunk outfit. 

4. Mix steampunk with ideas from other fandoms 

If you're keen on cosplaying in general, chances are you have items from previous costumes laying around. Mix and match your old costumes with steampunk elements to create a new and unique character. You can add a touch of Star Wars, Harry Potter, or anime to your steampunk outfit and create a cosplay mashup that will blow everyone's mind. 

5. Be yourself 

Above all, the point of steampunk is ultimately to have fun and express yourself. Don't feel like you have to conform to a particular steampunk style or trend. Be true to yourself and your own unique style, and your steampunk outfit will reflect your personality and creativity. 

6. Look up costume ideas for inspiration 

Need some inspiration for your steampunk outfit? Look up other steampunk cosplayers or designers for ideas. Pinterest, Etsy, and Instagram are great places to find steampunk fashion inspiration. Save photos of outfits or accessories that you like and use them as a reference when planning your own costume. 

7. Raid a thrift store for your costume 

You don't have to spend a lot of money to create a steampunk outfit. Raid your local thrift store for Victorian-style clothing, hats, and accessories. Look for items like lace gloves, petticoats, top hats, and corsets that can be steampunked up with some DIY additions. 

8. Augment your costume with colorful fabrics 

Steampunk fashion doesn't have to be all black and brown. Incorporate some colorful fabrics like velvet, satin, or silk to make your outfit more vibrant and eye-catching. You can also add some colorful ribbons or embroidery to give your costume a personal touch. 

9. Incorporate a vest or a corset into your outfit 

For men, a vest under an old-fashioned overcoat is a great place to start for a costume. For women, a corset can be used to create an hourglass figure and add Victorian elegance to your outfit. Look for corsets with brass buckles or gears to add steampunk elements to your costume. 

10. Sew gadgets onto your costume 

Steampunk is all about gadgets and gizmos. Sew gears, cogs, or watch parts onto your outfit to create a functional and unique costume. You can also add pockets to your jacket or skirt to store your phone or other essentials. 

11. Style your hair accordingly 

Hair is an important part of any costume, especially if your character is supposedly of upper stock and class. Look up Victorian hairstyles and add steampunk elements like metal hairpins or gears. You can also add some hair extensions or dye your hair to match your outfit. 

12. Make your own steampack 

A steampack is a backpack that incorporates steampunk elements, like gears, cogs, and brass accents. You can make your own steampack using old leather bags or backpacks and adding steampunk elements like chains, buckles, or leather straps. 

13. Make a steampunk-themed gun 

Every steampunk character needs a signature weapon. Make a steampunk-themed gun using toy guns and adding steampunk elements like gears, cogs, and brass accents. You can also add some glow-in-the-dark paint or LED lights to make your gun more futuristic. 

14. Create steampunk goggles 

Goggles are arguably the most recognizable trope in steampunk fashion. You can make your own steampunk goggles using old welding goggles or swimming goggles and adding steampunk elements like gears, cogs, or leather straps. You can also add some colored lenses or LED lights for an extra futuristic touch. 

15. Walk with a cane or parasol 

When you're walking around in dress, you can be made to appear more interesting if you have something to hold and carry around. A cane or parasol can add Victorian elegance to your outfit and give you something to lean on or protect yourself from the sun. Look for canes or parasols with steampunk elements like brass handles or gears. 

In conclusion, dressing steampunk is all about creativity, personality, and fun. Mix and match different styles, raid thrift stores, and add your own personal touch to create a unique and memorable steampunk outfit. Whether you're cosplaying at a convention, attending a steampunk-themed party, or just having fun with friends, dressing steampunk is a sure way to stand out and have a blast.

Are you considering getting a pet for your child, but not sure where to start? It's important to take your time and carefully evaluate your options before making a decision. In this article, we'll outline some helpful tips on how to decide on a first pet for your child.

1. Wait until your child expresses an interest in getting a pet.

It's important not to force a pet on your child. Wait until they express an interest in getting a pet before moving forward. This will ensure that your child is excited and committed to the pet, which will make the experience more enjoyable for everyone involved.

2. Discuss the animal in question with your child.

Once your child has expressed interest in a specific animal, have a conversation with them about why they want that particular pet. Discuss the responsibilities that come with owning a pet, and make sure your child understands the level of care that will be required.

3. Research the different possibilities together with your child.

Do some research together on the different types of pets available, and what care each one requires. Consider factors such as size, lifespan, and the level of attention each pet requires. This will help you make an informed decision about which pet will be the best fit for your family.

4. Read up on whichever pet you both decide on, before you buy it.

Before buying any pet, do some reading on how to care for that particular species. Learn about their nutritional needs, exercise requirements, and any special habits or behaviors they may have.

5. Set limits and rules regarding the care of the pet ahead of time.

Before bringing a pet home, be sure to set clear rules and expectations with your child regarding the care of the pet. Discuss who will be responsible for feeding, exercising, and cleaning up after the pet, and make sure everyone is on the same page.

6. Discuss your budget before you walk into the shop.

It's easy to get carried away with all the fun accessories and toys that are available for pets. Before walking into the store, set a budget with your child and agree on what you will and will not purchase.

7. Examine the animals' condition in the store.

When you arrive at the pet store, take a good look at the animals that are available for sale. Make sure they look healthy and well-cared-for. If you notice any signs of illness or poor care, consider leaving the store and finding a different retailer.

8. Better yet, do not go to a traditional pet store at all.

Consider adopting a pet from a local animal shelter or rescue organization. This will not only help a homeless animal find a loving home, but it will also be a more affordable option than purchasing a pet from a store.

9. Let your child choose the appropriate accessories and the actual animal him/herself.

How to Identify Negative Self Talk

Negative self talk is a common mental habit that many people engage in without even realizing it. This type of internal dialogue can be harmful, leading to feelings of insecurity, anxiety, and low self-esteem. Fortunately, it is possible to learn how to identify negative self talk and replace it with more positive and empowering thoughts. In this article, we'll go over some tips on how to recognize negative self talk and work on changing it.

Identify the running commentary in your head.

The first step in identifying negative self talk is to become aware of the thoughts that are running through your mind. Pay attention to your inner voice and the things that it tells you about yourself. Are you often critical of your appearance, abilities, or personality? Do you find yourself thinking negatively about the future or dwelling on past mistakes?

Accept that your inner voice is often wrong.

It is important to recognize that the voice in your head is not always a reliable source of information. Negative self talk often arises from distorted thinking patterns, such as black-and-white thinking or jumping to conclusions. By accepting that your inner voice may be wrong, you can begin to challenge and change its messages.

Use your feelings as a cue to examine your thoughts.

Negative self talk can often be linked to negative emotions such as anxiety, sadness, or frustration. When you experience these feelings, take a moment to examine the thoughts that preceded them. Are any of your thoughts irrational or unhelpful? If so, try to identify and challenge them.

Figure out if you are "filtering."

Although negative self talk can take any variety of types and topics, it usually derives from a common set of general forms. One such form is "filtering," where you focus on the negative aspects of a situation and ignore the positive. Examples might be thinking that your presentation was terrible because one person yawned, or assuming your date didn't like you because they looked away for a moment.

Perceive if you are "personalizing."

Have you ever blamed yourself for the weather ("It only stormed because I wanted to go to the beach.") or your favorite sports team's performance ("They always lose when I watch.")? This type of negative self talk is called "personalizing" and can lead to feelings of guilt, shame, and hopelessness.

Catch yourself "catastrophizing."

Do you assume that it will rain on your wedding day or that failing a test will ruin your entire future? This type of negative self talk is called "catastrophizing" and can make small problems seem much bigger than they really are.

Pick up on your habit of "polarizing."

Some people perceive themselves and the world in a strictly binary fashion - black or white, good or bad, yes or no, positive or negative, and so on. This type of negative self talk is called "polarizing" and can lead to overly simplistic thinking and rigid attitudes.

See if you are "self-limiting."

If you make up your mind beforehand that you can't accomplish something, you create a self-fulfilling prophecy that sabotages your chances of success. This type of negative self-talk is called "self-limiting" and can hold you back from achieving your full potential.

Judge whether you are "jumping to conclusions."

This form of negative self talk is very similar to the other forms that draw from assuming the worst in a situation. Do you assume that someone is thinking badly of you without any evidence? This is called "jumping to conclusions," and can cause unnecessary stress and anxiety.

Home in on your "habits of speech."

Do you, without thinking, call yourself "stupid" under your breath when you make a mistake, or say to yourself "Good idea, fatso" when you succumb to a tempting dessert? These types of negative self-talk occur so frequently and unconsciously that they are often referred to as "habits of speech."

Observe how you make others' thoughts your own.

Sometimes negative self talk arises from assuming that other people are thinking negatively of you. For example, you may assume your boss is angry with you because they seem distant in a meeting. In reality, their demeanor may have nothing to do with you.

Challenge your inner voice.

Once you have identified your negative self talk, it's time to start challenging it. Ask yourself if your thoughts are based on evidence or if they are just assumptions and exaggerations. Look for alternative interpretations and try to reframe your thoughts in a more positive light.

Practice positive self talk.

Replace your negative self talk with more positive and empowering statements. For example, instead of telling yourself "I'm never going to get this done," try saying "I can do this if I stay focused." Over time, this will become a habit and you will find it easier to be kinder to yourself.

Create a healthier environment.

Surround yourself with positive influences, such as supportive friends, inspirational books, and uplifting music. Take care of your physical health with regular exercise, healthy eating, and adequate rest. Remember, the more you care for yourself, the easier it will be to stay positive and confident.

In conclusion, negative self talk can be a destructive force in your life, but it's not something you have to live with forever. By identifying and challenging your negative thoughts, you can replace them with more positive and empowering ones, creating a healthier and happier mental environment for yourself. Good luck!

How to Understand Depression

Depression is a common mental disorder that causes people to feel sad, hopeless, and unmotivated. Understanding depression can help you or a loved one cope with its effects. This article will cover everything you need to know about understanding depression, including the daily cycle of depression, the emotional and physical pain it can cause, and how it affects your perspective. We'll also talk about the signs and symptoms of depression, including changes in job performance, weight changes, and sexual habits. Finally, we'll discuss the different ways depression affects men and women, including how hormone cycles and seasonal changes play a role.

Part 1: Understanding the Daily Cycle of Depression
Depression can cause a cycle of depression that can be difficult to break. The daily cycle of depression usually starts with feelings of sadness, emptiness, and hopelessness in the morning. As the day goes on, these feelings can become more intense, leading to drastic changes in mood and behavior. By evening, depression can bring feelings of extreme tiredness and lack of energy. Understanding this cycle can help you identify triggers and take steps to manage your symptoms.

Part 2: Emotions and Physical Pain
One of the most challenging aspects of depression is the emotional and physical pain it can cause. Depression can cause physical pain, including headaches, stomachaches, and muscle aches. You may also experience emotional pain, such as feelings of guilt, shame, and worthlessness. Understanding these symptoms and talking to a medical professional can help you develop a treatment plan that works for you.

Part 3: Changes in Perspective
Depression can change your perspective and make everything more difficult. You may find yourself unable to enjoy the things you once loved or struggling to see the good in anything. This can lead to feelings of isolation and withdrawal from others. Understanding how depression affects your perspective can help you identify when you need help and seek treatment.

Part 4: Signs and Symptoms
Depression can cause a wide range of symptoms, including changes in job performance, weight changes, and sexual habits. You may also notice changes in your sleep patterns, appetite, and energy levels. Recognizing these symptoms and talking to a medical professional can help you take the first step towards recovery.

Part 5: Men and Depression
Men are more likely to hide their feelings, which can make it difficult to recognize the signs of depression. Men with depression may avoid social connections, withdraw from friends and family, and take up bad habits like drug or alcohol abuse. Understanding how depression affects men is essential to support others and receive help when needed.

Part 6: Women and Depression
Depression is more prevalent in women than in men, and hormone cycles can play a significant role. Women may experience symptoms of depression during times of hormonal changes, such as during menstruation or menopause. Women are also under considerable pressure to balance multiple responsibilities, which can lead to feelings of overwhelm and depression.

Part 7: Seasonal Changes
Seasonal changes can also affect depression, especially in women. The winter months, in particular, can trigger feelings of sadness or depression, known as seasonal affective disorder (SAD). Understanding how seasonal changes affect you can help you develop coping strategies to manage your symptoms.

In conclusion, understanding depression is essential in coping with its effects. Whether you or someone you know is experiencing depression, knowing the signs and symptoms and seeking professional help can make a significant difference. Remember, you are not alone, and with the right care, treatment, and support, depression can be manageable.

Princess seams are a popular sewing technique that can be used to take in and tailor the fit of your clothing. Whether you are looking to modify a blouse, dress, or jacket, princess seams are a great way to achieve a custom fit without costly alterations. In this article, we will guide you through the steps of using princess seams to take in your clothing.

Part 1: Prepare your garment to mark it

Before you begin marking your garment, you will need to have a clear idea of which areas you want to adjust. Take some time to try on the garment and assess the fit. Look for areas where the fabric is loose or baggy, and make note of these areas so that you can target them with the princess seams.

Once you have identified the areas you want to modify, it’s time to prepare your garment for marking. Here’s how:

1. Lay your garment flat on a table or other surface.

2. Mark the measurement for Top of the Shoulder to Apex on the garment using white chalk. Be sure to use white chalk as coloured chalk may stain your clothing.

3. Divide the Apex to Apex measurement in half.

4. Measuring in from the center of your garment, mark half of the Apex to Apex measurement along the same axis as your previous mark.

5. From your Apex, draw a line down towards the hem and parallel to the center front, through your Ribcage, Waist, Upper Hip, and Mid Hip. If you would like to adjust your garment through the widest part of your rear end, you can also draw the line through the Lower Hip.

6. Go over this line with more chalk, making sure the line has quite a bit of chalk on it.

7. Unfold your garment.

Part 2: Mark the other side of the garment

To ensure that your princess seams are symmetrical, you will need to mark the other side of the garment. Here’s how:

1. Transfer the chalk line from one side of the front to the other by folding your garment in half along the same center front line, this time folding the other way.

2. Lay the garment flat on a table and gently hit the chalk line. This will help to make the line more visible so that you can see it when you unfold the garment.

3. Unfold the garment again.

Part 3: Pin and sew the princess seams

With your garment marked and prepped, it’s time to start pinning and sewing the princess seams. Here’s how:

1. Put the garment on, inside out.

2. Pin the garments so that you are dividing the extra fabric evenly between the two princess seams.

3. Take the garment off and double-check to make sure the seams look even.

4. Sew along the lines you just pinned. Be sure to use a stitch that is appropriate for the fabric you are working with.

5. Try your garment on again, this time right side out.

With these simple steps, you can use princess seams to take in your clothing and achieve a custom fit. Whether you are new to sewing or an experienced seamstress, this technique is a versatile and effective way to modify your wardrobe.

Have you ever wanted to make a cozy and cute hooded towel for yourself or a loved one? Look no further! With just a few simple steps and materials, you can create a personalized hooded towel that is both practical and fun.

Materials:
- Large bath towel and a hand towel in coordinating colors
- Sewing machine or needle and thread
- Pins
- Scissors

Steps:
1. Purchase a large bath towel and a hand towel in coordinating colors. This will ensure that your hooded towel looks cohesive and put together.
2. Cut a hand towel in half horizontally so that you end up with two squares. These will be used to make the ears for your hooded towel.
3. Fold one of the hand towel squares in half, and sew along the cut edge using a ½-inch (1.27 centimeters) seam allowance. This will form the basic shape of your ear. Repeat with the other hand towel square.
4. Turn the hood inside out. This will allow you to attach the ears to the inside of the hood later on.
5. Add a border to the hood, if desired. This can be as simple as sewing a strip of ribbon or lace around the edge of the hood for an extra decorative touch.
6. Consider adding some animal ears to the hood. To do this, cut four large triangles or half circles out of the extra hand towel half.
7. Sew along the angled/curved edges of each ear using a ½-inch (1.27 centimeters) seam allowance. Then, turn each ear inside out.
8. Cut two slits on the top of the hood where you want to place the ears. Slide the ears by ½ inch (1.27 centimeters) into each slit and pin them in place.
9. Sew the ears down from the inside of the hood using a ½-inch (1.27 centimeters) seam allowance. This will firmly attach the ears to the hood.
10. Spread the bath towel out horizontally, find the midpoint along the top edge, and mark it with a pin. This is where the hood will be attached to the towel.
11. Position the hood above the bath towel, and overlap the two edges by ½ inch (1.27 centimeters). Pin the hood in place on the towel.
12. Sew the towels together using a straight stitch. Make sure to remove the pins when you are done, and trim off any loose threads.
13. Finally, add any final, decorative touches to the hooded towel, if desired. This could include embroidering a name or design onto the towel, or adding additional decorative elements like pom-poms or buttons.

And there you have it! A cozy and personalized hooded towel that is perfect for snuggling up after a bath or a day at the beach. Enjoy!

As the internet continues to grow and evolve, the threat of hacking attacks becomes more prevalent. Website owners must take proactive measures to protect their websites from malicious attacks. SQL database-driven websites are at particular risk. Any web page that passes parameters to a database can be vulnerable to attacks. In this article, we will provide practical tips on how to protect your website from hacking attacks.

1. Get a basic overview of hacking
It is essential to understand what hacking is and how it is done to take preventative measures. Hacking involves using technical skills to gain unauthorized access to a computer system or network. It can cause significant financial, reputational, and legal damage to your website and business.

2. Understand how hackers do it
Hackers use various techniques, including phishing, trojan horses, and injection attacks to gain access to a system. Injection attacks focus on the use of malicious code to exploit vulnerabilities in a web application's code. This makes SQL database-driven websites particularly susceptible to hacking.

3. Understand how to hack your own website
One of the most effective ways to prevent hacking is to understand how to hack your own website. You can do this by entering code into your website's URL, such as:
http://www.mywebsite.com/bookreports.asp?reportID=21'
This will generate an error that can give hackers access to your database's names and column names.

4. Hide website errors
To protect against this type of vulnerability, you should set up custom error pages for your website. This can prevent private database details from being visible to hackers.

5. Manipulate the URL query string
Besides fishing for errors, hackers can use the URL query string to enter even more dangerous code. For instance:
http://www.mywebsite.com/bookreports.asp?reportID=21'; drop table myTablename--
This can permanently delete your table.

6. Manipulate the form input
The form input is another point of entry for hackers. They can enter malicious code such as:
Fred'; drop table myTablename--
This can cause permanent damage to your table.

7. Block input containing malicious code
Input validation is a crucial tool for website security. It involves checking if the input received through the URL query string or textbox is safe. You can use input validation rules, filter characters, and sanitize input by escaping.

8. The wash and rinse cycle
Input validation should be a two-part process, like a wash and rinse cycle. The first step is to filter out anything malicious to block potential threats. The second step, where necessary, is to sanitize the input by replacing or escaping it.

10. Use advanced security techniques
If you want to pursue more advanced security techniques, you can research and explore them on your own. There are several resources available for those who want to take their website's security to the next level.

In conclusion, protecting your website from hacking attacks is critical. SQL database-driven websites are particularly vulnerable to attacks. Diarrhea is a common symptom of opiate withdrawal. Over-the-counter medications like Imodium or Pepto-Bismol can help.

8. Think about using some lower-level controlled substances if they're legal in your country or state

14. Try community detox

16. Check yourself into a rehabilitation facility

17. Give yourself a lot of positive reinforcement

Overcoming addiction is challenging, so make sure to give yourself a lot of positive reinforcement and acknowledge your progress.

18. Remember to eat food and drink water

Exercise can help relieve stress and alleviate some withdrawal symptoms.

You're capable of overcoming addiction, so believe in yourself and your ability to overcome this challenge.

21. Quit for yourself and no one else

How to Quit Drinking Alcohol

Alcoholism is a widespread problem that can cause significant harm to a person's health, relationships, and career. Quitting alcohol can be one of the most challenging things to do, but it can also be one of the most rewarding. If you are ready to take control of your life and quit drinking, then this guide can help you achieve your goal.

1. Talk to your doctor.

Before you decide to quit drinking, it is recommended to talk to your doctor. They can help you understand the potential side effects of quitting and recommend resources to help you through the process.

2. Change your attitude about quitting.

Quitting alcohol is a huge accomplishment, and it is important to approach it with a positive attitude. Focus on the benefits of quitting instead of what you might be losing.

3. Try to pick some significant date to quit.

Having a specific date to quit drinking can give you something to aim for and help you prepare mentally and physically for the journey ahead.

4. Get rid of all bottles, cans, etc.

Remove all alcohol from your home and workplace. This will help you avoid temptation and make it easier to resist the urge to drink.

5. Feel your feelings.

Quitting alcohol can be an emotional roller coaster. Allow yourself to feel your emotions and work through them instead of suppressing them with alcohol.

6. Don't put yourself with people or in situations where you're likely to drink.

Avoid situations that might trigger the urge to drink or put you in the company of people who encourage drinking.

7. In the initial stage, reduce the quantity of alcohol intake.

Reducing your alcohol intake gradually can minimize physical withdrawal symptoms and make quitting easier.

8. Have food before you drink.

Having food in your stomach before drinking can help slow down the absorption of alcohol and reduce the impact of its effects.

9. Drink a lot of water.

Drinking plenty of water can help you stay hydrated and reduce the urge to drink alcohol.

10. Revise recipes that call for alcohol.

Explore non-alcoholic alternatives to your favorite recipes or substitute alcohol with other ingredients.

11. Don't try to explain quitting to people.

You don't owe anyone an explanation for your decision to quit drinking, and you don't have to defend it to others.

12. If you are a scheduled drinker, change your routine.

Changing your routine can help prevent the urge to drink and make quitting easier.

13. Don’t give up on yourself.

Quitting alcohol can be a challenging process, but don't give up on yourself. Believe in yourself and be patient with the process.

14. Don’t let guilt consume you.

Feelings of guilt are natural during the quitting process, but don't let them consume you. Focus on the positive changes you are making in your life.

15. Buy a "sober wallet".

Purchase a new wallet to commemorate your sobriety and remind you of your goal.

16. Buy a small piece of inexpensive jewelry as a reminder of your sobriety.

A piece of jewelry can be a powerful reminder of your commitment to sobriety.

17. Take a B vitamin supplement daily for your first week off alcohol.

Alcohol can deplete your body of essential B vitamins, so taking supplements can help ease withdrawal symptoms.

18. Make lists.

Making lists can help you stay organized and motivated during the quitting process.

19. If you are tempted, try to visualize what you might look like totally out of control.

Visualizing the consequences of drinking can help you resist the urge to drink.

20. Embrace the psychological benefits of sobriety.

Quitting alcohol can have a positive impact on your mental health, self-esteem, and relationships.

21. Remember the reasons why you quit in the first place.

Revisit your reasons for quitting alcohol regularly to stay motivated and focused on your goal.

22. Do not avoid all situations where you would normally drink.

Instead of avoiding situations where you might be tempted to drink, find healthy alternatives to enjoy yourself.

23. Memorize inspirational thoughts.

Having inspiring quotes or thoughts memorized can help you stay motivated and focused.

24. Give yourself a prize for every day or every hour that you haven't had a drink.

Reward yourself for each day or hour that you stay sober to celebrate your progress.

25. Learn meditation.

Meditation can help you stay present and focused during the quitting process, reducing stress and anxiety.

26. Ask for support.

Don't be afraid to reach out to friends, family, and professionals for support during the quitting process.

27. Consider joining a support group like Alcoholics Anonymous or SMART Recovery.

Support groups can provide a community of people who understand what you are going through and offer guidance and support.

28. Watch as sobriety changes your life in front of your own eyes.

Quitting alcohol can have many positive effects on your life, including better health, stronger relationships, and greater self-confidence.

29. Don't be afraid to talk about your experiences.

Sharing your experience with others can help you stay accountable and inspire others who are going through the same thing.

30. Admit to yourself, and remember it, that there is absolutely nothing in your life more important than this one thing.

Quitting alcohol is one of the most important things you can do for your health and well-being. Make it a priority and don't let anything or anyone distract you from your goal.

Peg solitaire is a classic board game that can be quite challenging to win, but with the right strategy, you can improve your chances of success. The English board version of the game has the form of a plus sign +, with pegs in each of the holes. The goal is to jump a peg over another peg onto a hole, removing the pegs from the board move by move. It's important to note that the field has four side areas, each with a size of 3x2, and one center area with a size of 3x3.

Start by clearing one side of its pegs, then move on to the next side until you've cleared them all. The trick to making this easier is to memorize the steps for clearing one side, then repeating them for each of the four sides.

To start, make your first move going from right to left into the middle hole. Next, clear a side area by moving from the corner towards the middle, and then from the bottom right corner to the upper right corner. Once you've done that, rescue the lonely peg in the corner and move it back towards the center. Repeat these steps for each of the four side areas, making sure to use the same pattern each time.

After you've cleared all four sides, you'll come to the famous arrow pointing left. To move past this point, take the peg behind the arrow's head one circle around the arrow, going up, right, down twice, left, and up again. This will get you to the final lying T-figure.

To win the game, take the center peg up, the left peg to the center, then move the bottom two pegs up and the two remaining pegs down. This will leave you with one peg in the center and the game successfully solved!

In conclusion, while winning the peg solitaire game on the English board can seem like a daunting task, following these simple steps can increase your chances of successfully completing the game. Remember to clear each side area using the same pattern, move past the arrow to the lying T-figure, and then use the final pattern to win the game. Good luck!

How to Multiply Using the Russian Peasant Method

This method, also known as the Ancient Egyptian method, involves halving and doubling numbers until you end up with the product of the original numbers. Follow the steps below to learn how to multiply using the Russian peasant method.

Steps:

1. Think of the numbers you want to multiply. For example, let's use 27 and 14.

 27 | 14

11. Understand why the method works. The Russian peasant method works because it converts the problem into binary (base 2) multiplication, rather than base 10 (which standard multiplication uses). This makes it easier to perform calculations using only two digits (0 and 1) and simpler arithmetic.

Installing IBM Java on Ubuntu Linux

This document assumes that you might have another vendor version of Java installed on your Ubuntu Linux system, such as OpenJDK or Oracle Java which is common when you use Ubuntu Linux. In order to ensure that there is no system conflict with multiple versions of Java, we will remove and disable other vendor versions of Java. Then, we will proceed to download and install IBM Java on Ubuntu Linux. 

Part 1: Removing and Disabling Other Vendor Versions of Java 

1. Open the terminal on your Ubuntu Linux system. 

2. To remove OpenJDK from your system, issue the following command: 

sudo apt-get purge openjdk-\* 

This command will completely remove OpenJDK/JRE from your system. 

3. If Oracle Java is installed on your system, you will need to comment out the references to Oracle Java in the /etc/profile, .profile or .bashrc file. For example, as root, use a text editor such as nano or gedit to edit your /etc/profile. You may have a file that looks like this:

JAVA_HOME=/usr/local/java/jdk1.7.0
PATH=$PATH:$HOME/bin:$JAVA_HOME/bin
JRE_HOME=/usr/local/java/jre1.7.0
PATH=$PATH:$HOME/bin:$JRE_HOME/bin
export JAVA_HOME
export JRE_HOME
export PATH

You want to make sure you comment out the references to Oracle Java, using the ## symbol in your /etc/profile, .profile and .bashrc file so change the file to look like this:

##JAVA_HOME=/usr/local/java/jdk1.7.0
##PATH=$PATH:$HOME/bin:$JAVA_HOME/bin
##JRE_HOME=/usr/local/java/jre1.7.0
##PATH=$PATH:$HOME/bin:$JRE_HOME/bin
##export JAVA_HOME
##export JRE_HOME
##export PATH

Save the /etc/profile file and exit. 

Part 2: Downloading and Installing IBM Java on Ubuntu Linux 

1. Register as a user on the IBM website in order to download IBM SDK/JRE. 

2. Download the version of IBM Java SDK and JRE for your system architecture. For example, we will download the IBM Java SDK/JRE for 64 bit Ubuntu Linux, which is:

ibm-java-sdk-7.0-0.0-linux-x86_64.tgz 
ibm-java-jre-7.0-0.0-linux-x86_64.tgz 

3. Create a directory to hold the IBM Java SDK and JRE using the following command:

sudo -s mkdir -p /opt/ibm/java 

This makes the directory available to all users on the system. 

4. Change into the download directory and copy the IBM Java SDK and JRE to /opt/ibm/java/ directory: 

cd /home/"your_user_name"/Downloads 
sudo -s cp -r ibm-java-sdk-7.0-0.0-linux-x86_64.tgz /opt/ibm/java 
sudo -s cp -r ibm-java-jre-7.0-0.0-linux-x86_64.tgz /opt/ibm/java 

5. Next, change into your IBM Java directory: 

cd /opt/ibm/java 

6. Make the compressed IBM Java binaries executable for all users on the system by running the following commands: 

sudo -s chmod a+x ibm-java-sdk-7.0-0.0-linux-x86_64.tgz 
sudo -s chmod a+x ibm-java-jre-7.0-0.0-linux-x86_64.tgz 

7. Unpack the IBM Java SDK by issuing the following commands: 

sudo -s tar xvzf ibm-java-sdk-7.0-0.0-linux-x86_64.tgz 
sudo -s tar xvzf ibm-java-jre-7.0-0.0-linux-x86_64.tgz 

The IBM SDK and the JRE will unpack into a single directory called /opt/ibm/java/ibm-java-x86_64-70. 

8. Edit the system wide PATH /etc/profile in order to create a system wide PATH for the IBM Java SDK/JRE on Ubuntu Linux. Enter the following information: 

export PATH=${PATH}:/opt/ibm/java/ibm-java-x86_64-70/bin:/opt/ibm/java/ibm-java-x86_64-70/jre/bin:$PATH 

Save the file and exit. 

9. Inform the system that IBM Java SDK JRE is available: 

sudo update-alternatives --install "/usr/bin/java" "java" "/opt/ibm/java/ibm-java-x86_64-70/jre/bin/java" 1 
sudo update-alternatives --install "/usr/bin/java" "javaws" "/opt/ibm/java/ibm-java-x86_64-70/jre/bin/javaws" 1 
sudo update-alternatives --install "/usr/bin/javac" "javac" "/opt/ibm/java/ibm-java-x86_64-70/bin/javac" 1 

10. Inform your Ubuntu Linux system that IBM Java SDK/JRE must be the default Java. 

11. Reload your system wide PATH /etc/profile by typing the following command: 

. 

12. Test to see if IBM Java installed correctly by using the command: 

java -version 

You should receive a message that displays:

java version "1.7.0-ea" 
Java(TM) SE Runtime Environment (build pxa6470-20100531_04)IBM J9 VM(build2.6, JRE 1.7.0 IBM J9 2.6 Linux amd64-64 jvmxa6470-20100522_58582 (JIT enabled, AOT enabled) 
J9VM - R26_head_20100521_1457_B58494 JIT dev_20100507_15747 
GC - R26_head_20100521_1652_B58499 
J9CL - 20100522_58582) 
JCL - 20100514_02 based on Sun 7b76 

13. Test that your IBM Java compiler works by using the command: 

javac -version 

You should receive a message that displays: 

javac 1.7.0-internal 

14. You can also switch between different installed vendors of Java, such as OpenJDK, Oracle and IBM, by using the command: 

sudo update-alternatives --config java 

Make sure you select the Java directory which references IBM Java and press enter.

Using a Hoyer Lift: Step by Step Guide

A Hoyer lift is a piece of medical equipment designed to assist in transferring patients from one location to another, such as a bed to a wheelchair or vice versa. In this article, we'll take a detailed look at how to use a Hoyer lift to transfer a patient safely and effectively.

Step 1: Prepare the Bed
If you're using a hospital bed, make sure the guard rails are up and locked whenever they don't interfere with your access. It's also a good idea to raise the bed to its maximum flat height if possible, as this will make it easier to maneuver the lift.

Step 2: Position the Patient
Have the patient lie on their back near the side where you'll be placing the lift. Remove any excess blankets or sheets from the top of the patient, and have them raise the leg nearest you. Then, roll the patient onto the side opposite you. This will create room for you to position the lift and sling.

Step 3: Place the Sling
Fold the sling in half lengthwise and place it next to the patient. Then, roll the patient onto their back and then onto their other side. Tug gently at the top layer of the folded sling to unfold it and position it under the patient. Finally, roll the patient back onto their back over the sling.

Step 4: Position the Lift
Lock the Hoyer lift into position under the patient's bed. Make sure the legs of the lift are spread wide enough to fit around the bed or wheelchair. Lower the boom until the sling bar is over the patient.

Step 5: Attach the Sling
Hook the loops on the sides of the u-sling to the cradle. Make sure the sling is properly attached and secure before proceeding.

Step 6: Lift the Patient
Raise the boom slowly, lifting the patient off the bed. Make sure the patient is comfortable and secure in the sling before proceeding.

Step 7: Transfer the Patient
Roll the lift with the sling and patient in place slowly to the new destination. Make sure the wheels are locked in place before transferring the patient. Lower the boom until the patient is positioned comfortably.

Step 8: Remove the Sling
Unhook the sling loops and remove the sling from the patient. Make sure the patient is comfortable and supported before leaving them in their new location.

By following these steps carefully, you can use a Hoyer lift to transfer patients safely and effectively. Always double-check your equipment, and never attempt to lift a patient if you are unsure or inexperienced. With proper training and preparation, a Hoyer lift can make patient transfers much easier and more comfortable for both the patient and the caregiver.

Bedtime can be a challenging time for parents, but there's no need to fear. With a little bit of patience, perseverance, and Supernanny inspiration, you can harness the power of routine to get your child to sleep soundly in no time. Follow these steps to handle the bedtime routine like Supernanny:

1. Block out outside noises from the room. This will help your child stay calm and fall asleep faster. Consider using a white noise machine or playing soft music to create a soothing environment.

2. Get the child into their pajamas. This signals to your child that it's time for bed and can help them transition into a sleepy state.

3. Get the sleeping area ready. Make sure the room is at a comfortable temperature, the sheets are clean and cozy, and any toys or distractions are put away.

4. Help your child unwind in their room. Spend some time reading stories, talking, or doing a quiet activity together to help your child relax and feel comfortable.

5. Figure out which of Supernanny's two techniques might be best for your child. Depending on your child's age and personality, you can choose between the "Stay in the Bedroom" and "The Three Trips" techniques.

6. Keep calm and stay in the bedroom. This is the first step in implementing the "Stay in the Bedroom" technique. Sit quietly and calmly next to your child's crib or bed, and let them know that it's time to sleep.

7. Place the child into their crib. This is where they'll stay for the night.

8. Turn out the lights in nearby rooms (such as hallways leading to the child's room). This will help your child feel secure and minimize distractions.

9. Sit down next to the crib, but keep within your child's eyesight. This will provide a comforting presence for your child and help them feel safe.

10. Resist the urge to get up and handle your child, unless they actually get out of their crib. This will help your child learn to self-soothe and fall asleep without needing your help.

11. Return the child back to their crib, if the child tries to escape. Be firm and consistent in enforcing the bedtime routine.

12. Return yourself to the same spot on the floor. This will help your child feel secure and minimize any disruptions.

13. Let the child cry until they tire themselves out and cry themselves off to sleep. This can be difficult, but it's an important part of the routine.

14. Get up and walk out of the room once you can be assured that they have actively fallen asleep. This signals to your child that it's safe to fall asleep on their own.

15. Handle subsequent nights. If your child continues to struggle with sleeping, consider implementing the "Three Trips" technique.

16. Bring the child into their bed, like you always would have done, then exit the room. This is the first step in the "Three Trips" technique.

17. Leave the room. If your child gets out of bed, calmly and quietly return them to their room without engaging in conversation or providing attention.

18. Give them a hug and a cuddle as you pick them up and transport them back into their room the first time. This will help provide a sense of comfort and security.

19. Leave the room, much like you did before. Repeat this process up to three times, and be consistent in your approach.

20. Stay consistent in the route and technique in subsequent nights that the child gets out of bed. This will help your child learn the routine and fall asleep more easily in the future.

With these steps, you'll be able to handle the bedtime routine like Supernanny and enjoy a peaceful night's sleep for you and your child.

Learning welding as a hobby can be an enjoyable and useful skill to have. Whether it is creating metal sculptures, fixing household appliances, or even building a small home business, welding skills can come in handy. If you're interested in learning welding as a hobby, here's how:

4. Learn on your own.

You can also learn welding on your own with the following steps:

5. Buy, borrow or rent a welder.

Welders can be expensive to buy, but you can find affordable ones to rent or borrow.

6. Obtain your welding rods (electrodes).

Different types of welding rods (electrodes) are used for different welding applications. Obtain the right welder for your welding project.

7. Find some mild steel to practice with.

8. Set your piece of steel on a clean, dry, level surface which is heat resistant and nonflammable.

Your working space should be steady, level, dry, and nonflammable. This helps to prevent accidents.

9. Attach your ground clamp.

10. Put on your welding gloves.

Welding gloves protect your hands from the heat of the welder.

11. Insert the "clean end" (the end without the powder flux coating) of your electrode into the electrode holder.

This will hold the electrode in place while you weld.

12. Practice "striking" the electrode against the welding stock (the sample metal you will be welding on).

This helps to start the welding process.

13. Set the temperature range (or amperage) of your welder to about 80A (amps).

This helps to keep the welding process consistent.

14. Put on your safety glasses and welding hood (or helmet, as it is sometimes called), with the dark lens flipped up to allow you to see.

This protects your eyes from the brightness of the electric arc.

15. Turn the welder on.

This starts the flow of electricity to the welding electrode.

16. Flip the dark lens or full face helmet down before you strike the electrode against the practice metal.

This protects your eyes while welding.

17. Move the electrode along the surface of the metal slowly, watching the pool of molten metal beneath the arc flame.

This helps to achieve a consistent weld.

18. Run your bead an inch or so along the metal, then pull the electrode back to break the arc.

This stops the flow of electricity.

19. When you raise your shield, to look at your weld and evaluate it, you must have your safety glasses on.

This ensures your eyes are protected when evaluating your weld.

20. Use a chipping hammer (or other tool) to knock the slag (oxidized metal and melted flux) off the bead to see the new metal you have deposited from the welding rod.

This helps to gauge the quality of your weld.

21. Continue practicing on pieces of scrap metal, using the same rods and amperage setting, until you get a good, consistent bead.

Practicing will help you improve your welding skills.

22. Try joining two pieces of metal by welding.

23. Experiment with other rods (electrodes) and amperage to see the different effects you get.

This helps to gain more experience and a better understanding of welding.

24. Look into other welding processes, such as MIG (metal, inert gas) with solid and flux-core wire, or TIG (tungsten, inert gas), and oxyacetylene.

Hernias are a common medical condition that affect millions of people every year. They can occur in different parts of the body, such as the abdomen, groin, or upper thigh, and can cause discomfort, pain, and other symptoms. Knowing if you have a hernia can be difficult, but there are several risk factors and signs to watch out for. In this article, we will guide you through the steps to assess your risk factors, recognize the symptoms, and understand the potential outcomes of this condition.

Part 1: Assess your risk factors

1. Take note of any bulges: One of the most common signs of a hernia is a bulging or swelling in the affected area. This can occur when an organ protrudes through a weak or torn muscle wall. You may notice a lump or mass that grows larger when you cough, sneeze, or strain.

2. Pay attention to vomiting: If you experience persistent vomiting, this may be a sign of a more serious type of hernia, such as a paraesophageal hernia. This can occur when the stomach pushes through the diaphragm and causes severe symptoms, such as chest pain and difficulty breathing.

3. Watch for constipation: Chronic constipation can put a strain on your abdominal muscles and increase your risk of hernias. It can also cause pain and discomfort in the lower abdomen, which may lead to a hernia.

4. Don't ignore abnormal feelings of fullness: If you feel bloated or full after eating, this may be a sign of a hernia. You may also experience indigestion, heartburn, or regurgitation.

5. Keep track of your pain levels: Hernias can cause different types of pain, such as a dull ache, sharp stabbing pain, or a burning sensation. Pay attention to the location of the pain and how it changes over time.

6. Know when to see a doctor: If you suspect you have a hernia, it's important to see a doctor for proper diagnosis and treatment. Some hernias can lead to serious complications if left untreated, such as bowel obstruction or strangulation.

7. Take your gender into consideration: Men are more likely to develop hernias than women, especially older men over the age of 50. This is due to the natural weakening of the abdominal muscles over time, as well as lifestyle factors such as smoking and obesity.

8. Know your family's history: If you have a family member with a history of having hernias, you are at a greater risk yourself. This may be due to genetic factors that make you more susceptible to developing weak abdominal muscles.

9. Take your lung condition into account: Chronic coughing or bronchitis can put a strain on your abdominal muscles and increase your risk of hernias. If you have a chronic lung condition, it's important to manage it properly to prevent further complications.

10. Pay attention to chronic constipation: If you suffer from chronic constipation, you may be more likely to develop a hernia due to the prolonged straining.

11. Know that you're at risk if you're pregnant: Women who are pregnant may experience hernias due to the increased pressure on their abdominal muscles. This is especially common during the third trimester when the baby is growing rapidly.

12. Try to keep your weight at a healthy level: Obesity can put a strain on your abdominal muscles and increase your risk of hernias. Maintaining a healthy weight through diet and exercise can help reduce your risk.

13. Consider whether your job could be the culprit: Certain occupations that require heavy lifting or prolonged standing can increase your risk of hernias. If you work in a job that puts strain on your abdominal muscles, be sure to take proper precautions and avoid lifting heavy objects if possible.

Part 2: Recognize the symptoms

1. Understand how doctors diagnose hernias: Your doctor will perform a physical examination to check for signs of a hernia, such as a bulge or lump in the affected area. They may also use imaging tests such as ultrasound or MRI to get a better picture of the hernia.

2. Recognize an inguinal hernia: This is the most common type of hernia, and happens when the intestines or bladder push the lower abdominal wall into the groin and inguinal canal. Symptoms may include a visible bulge in the groin area, pain or discomfort in the affected area, and a heavy or dragging sensation.

3. Suspect a hiatal hernia in people over 50: This type of hernia occurs when the stomach pushes up through the diaphragm and into the chest cavity. Symptoms may include heartburn, chest pain, difficulty swallowing, and regurgitation of food or liquids.

4. Look for umbilical hernias in babies: This type of hernia occurs in infants when the abdominal muscles don't fully close around the belly button. Symptoms may include a visible bulge around the navel, which may become more noticeable when the baby cries or strains.

5. Be careful of incisional hernia after surgery: This type of hernia can occur after a surgical incision has weakened the abdominal muscles. Symptoms may include a visible bulge around the incision site, pain or discomfort in the affected area, and difficulty moving or bending.

6. Recognize a femoral hernia in women: This type of hernia occurs when the intestines push through the femoral canal, which is located just below the groin crease. Symptoms may include a visible bulge in the upper thigh, pain or discomfort in the affected area, and a heavy or dragging sensation.

7. Report acute pain immediately: If the hernia's symptoms come on suddenly, the first thing the doctor will do is try to manage your pain. Acute pain may be a sign of a more serious complication, such as bowel obstruction or strangulation.

Part 3: Understand the potential outcomes

1. Consider getting elective surgery: If your hernia is causing significant pain or discomfort, your doctor may recommend surgery to repair the weakened muscle wall. This can help prevent further complications and improve your quality of life.

Geta, also known as Japanese wooden sandals, are a traditional type of footwear worn in Japan for centuries. They are made of two parts- the "ha" or sole, and the "thongs" which hold the foot in place. If you're interested in making your own pair of geta, you've come to the right place! 

Here's how to make a pair of geta using a saw and a drill: 

Materials: 
- Wood 
- Something for the thongs 
- Hand saw with a fairly fine cross-cut blade 
- Soles and ha: The soles for the typical adult geta are about 4 or 5 inches (10.2 or 12.7 cm) wide, 9 to 11 inches (22.9 to 27.9 cm) long, and 1/2 to 3/4 inch (1.3 to 1.9 cm) thick. 
- Most lumber yards (and Lowes) only sell "full" boards, usually 8 feet (2.4 m) long. 
- Thongs: I tried using nylon rope from the hardware store for the thongs, but it's not very comfortable. 
- The next layer which brings the total diameter to nearly 1/2 inch (1.3 cm) is some sort of fuzzy stuff that's like the gray padding you see in some shipping envelopes -- it looks like lint. Get about 1 1/2 yards (1.4 m) for each pair. 
- Miscellaneous: 1/8 inch (0.3 cm) nylon cord or rope for the small loop that holds the main thong between the toes. 
- Carpenter's glue. 

Step 1: Cut out the sole and ha pieces 
Using your hand saw, cut your wood to the size necessary for the soles and ha. The soles for the typical adult geta are about 4 or 5 inches (10.2 or 12.7 cm) wide, 9 to 11 inches (22.9 to 27.9 cm) long, and 1/2 to 3/4 inch (1.3 to 1.9 cm) thick. The ha should be slightly smaller than the sole, and about 2 to 3 inches (5.1 to 7.6 cm) wide. 

Step 2: Create the thong holes 
Using your drill, create two holes in each of the ha pieces and one hole in each of the sole pieces. Make sure that the holes are evenly spaced and centered. 

Step 3: Apply glue and clamp 
Using carpenter's glue, apply a small amount to the bottom of the ha. Place the ha piece on top of the sole piece, lining up the holes. Start thinking about ways to clamp the pieces in position while the glue dries. This could be done using large rubber bands, tightly wrapped masking tape, or by piling books or bricks on the joint. Repeat this process for the second pair of ha and sole pieces. 

Step 4: Add the thongs 
Thread the thongs through the holes in the ha pieces and then through the hole in the sole piece, tying a knot at the bottom of the sole piece to secure the thongs in place. Make sure that the thongs are twisted to create a comfortable fit. 

Step 5: Add the finishing touches 
To protect your wood from water/sweat damage, use polyurethane or another kind of wood finish to protect the wood. 

If you prefer a more authentic look, try making a single-piece geta. This will take considerably more effort, but the result is a more authentic (and more durable) alternative to the fake geta. 

Now that you know how to make your own pair of geta, you can enjoy this traditional footwear and show off your craftsmanship to others!
